title: Iran’s foreign minister describes moment of attack that killed Khamenei
summary:
Abbas Araghchi says he has kept on the move since being pulled from rubble after strike on first day of war

Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has described how he was pulled from the rubble of a leadership compound after the US-Israeli airstrike that killed the country’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, on the first day of the war, and has survived since by constantly moving around the capital, Tehran, by car.

In an interview with the Iranian journalist Javad Mogouyi, Araghchi confirmed Israel and the US had accurate intelligence on the location of Khamenei and other officials, enabling them to target Iran’s senior leadership.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has described how he was pulled from the rubble of a leadership compound after the US-Israeli airstrike that killed the country’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, on the first day of the war, and has survived since by constantly moving around the capital, Tehran, by car.
In an interview with the Iranian journalist Javad Mogouyi, Araghchi confirmed Israel and the US had accurate intelligence on the location of Khamenei and other officials, enabling them to target Iran’s senior leadership.
He said he had yet to meet the country’s new leader, Khamenei’s son Mojtaba, but said his appointment sent “a very important message to the world that there would be no change in the regime’s policies and ideals”.
Speaking to Mogouyi before the resumption of all-out hostilities 10 days ago, Araghchi said he had always doubted that negotiations with the US earlier this year would work, but said they had been necessary, even if there was only a 10% chance of success – not least to ensure there was no room for doubt that Iran had pursued diplomacy. “No one would be able to tell us that it was our fault,” he said.
In the interview published online on Sunday, Araghchi confirmed that Iran had offered the US a deal on its nuclear programme in the final round of talks in Geneva, but said Oman’s foreign minister, Badr Albusaidi, told him the following day that the mood in Washington had suddenly become more bellicose.
The joint US-Israeli strikes began shortly after 9am the next day, when senior officials had gathered for meetings at the ministry of intelligence, the strategic council on foreign policy, and the defence council.
“What matters, in my view, is the fact that Israel had intelligence about these meetings,” Araghchi said, adding: “This may point to a security gap that probably still exists. This needs to be fixed.”
Araghchi was reporting back to Khamenei’s deputy chief of staff, Ali Asghar Hijazi, when the building was shaken by three blasts within seconds – each closer than the last, he said. “The third explosion was almost next to our building. The section where Mr Hijazi’s office was located was directly hit, and the left side of the building was completely destroyed.”
Hijazi’s secretary was killed instantly, but Araghchi and Hijazi escaped the full force of the detonation.
“We were on the other side of the building, and after the explosion, the ceiling, walls, and everything collapsed on us. I grabbed Mr Hijazi’s hand, and we made our way through the beams and boards and pieces of wood, hearing the cries for help. Water was pouring from the ceiling. Everything was wrecked. We eventually got out, and I saw that various parts of the compound had been targeted.”
Araghchi was rushed to the foreign ministry by a passerby since his official car had been hit.
“For three days we were cut off from everything trying to find out who was alive and who had been martyred,” he said. “The enemy thought they could paralyse us by targeting leadership, but they failed.”
Araghchi said Iran had been prepared for such an attack, and had already drawn up plans to close the strategic strait of Hormuz if the supreme leader was targeted. The codename for such a scenario was “Code 110”, a reference to the clause of Iran’s constitution that lays out the supreme leader’s powers.
Araghchi said the US had decided to attack because it believed Iran’s government had been weakened abroad by blows to its proxies in Syria and Lebanon, and at home by economic protests – the speed and scale of which he admitted had surprised him.
Araghchi said regional governments had counselled Donald Trump against war, saying that attacking Iran would not be as easy as the US raid on Venezuela to abduct the then president, Nicolás Maduro. “Iran is different. Its support is a several-thousand-year civilisation, combined with Shia thought and beliefs about martyrdom. When these combine, they create something that cannot be easily defeated,” he said.
He told Mogouyi that Iran had warned neighbouring governments that any attack would be met with retaliation against targets in the region. “If Israel hits our nuclear facilities, we will hit theirs. Our missiles do not reach America, so we will hit their bases, which are unfortunately in your countries. If they hit our oil facilities, we will ensure that nobody in the region can sell oil,” he said.
He also said warnings to the Turkish government had prompted Ankara to shut down Trump’s plan to encourage a Kurdish revolt from Iraq into Iran. Turkey’s foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, “talked to the Americans and adopted a very firm position in this regard. A series of efforts foiled this plot,” Araghchi said.
He added that Iran was working to exacerbate divisions between the US and Israel. “There are sometimes conflicts of objectives and positions which can be played with,” he said, without giving details.
Araghchi said that after Israel’s 12-day bombing campaign against his country in 2025, Iran had improved its missile capabilities, reducing the time needed to reactivate a base after an attack from 10–15 hours to 35–40 minutes.
Discussing the choice of diplomacy or war, Araghchi said: “We do not fight unless the cost of not fighting is higher than the cost of fighting.”

title: Balance stablecoin collapses 99% after $1 million exploit drains its bitcoin vaults
full_text:
Balance stablecoin collapses 99% after $1 million exploit drains its bitcoin vaults
An attacker fed the lending system a fake, abnormally low bitcoin price, liquidated vaults that should have been safe, and pocketed the difference in a single transaction.
- Balance Coin, an algorithmic stablecoin designed to hold a $1 peg, crashed more than 99% to about $0.0014 after an attacker exploited a pricing flaw in its protocol.
- The attacker manipulated Balance Protocol’s bitcoin price oracle, triggering improper liquidations of collateralized vaults and netting about $912,000, largely at the expense of governance entity 42DAO.
- The exploit comes amid heightened concern over DeFi security as increasingly capable AI systems raise new risks, including a recent controlled test in which OpenAI models compromised Hugging Face servers.
Balance Coin, a low-circulation algorithmic stablecoin meant to hold a dollar peg, crashed more than 99% on Wednesday after an attacker exploited a pricing flaw in the protocol behind it, blockchain data shows.
The token, which traded near its $1 peg a day earlier, fell to about $0.0014, erasing nearly all of its roughly $3.5 million in nominal value.
The attacker's actual profit was smaller, around $912,000, drained from 42DAO, the governance entity behind Balance Protocol. The project runs a system where users lock bitcoin-backed collateral to mint the stablecoin, and vaults are liquidated if the collateral's value drops too far.
Security firm SlowMist said the attacker manipulated the protocol's oracle - the external price feed it relies on - to write an abnormally low bitcoin price into the system.
The lending contract then accepted that price without checking it against an accurate range and without any liquidation delay, letting the attacker instantly liquidate multiple vaults that should never have been eligible, then swap the seized collateral for profit.
The exploit lands amid growing scrutiny of DeFi security as AI systems grow more capable, including an instance from late Tuesday in which OpenAI models broke out of their own testing environment and compromised the servers of AI firm Hugging Face during a controlled evaluation.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin under $66,000 as traders await Alphabet earnings to gauge AI trade
full_text:
Bitcoin holds below $66,000 as the market waits on Alphabet to judge the AI trade
Bitcoin traded near $65,900 on Wednesday, holding just below the two-week high it touched earlier, up 1.5% on the week, per CoinDesk data.
The pause matches the broader market, where a two-day rebound in chip stocks stalled as traders waited on Alphabet's results after the U.S. close.
Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.8% and South Korea's Kospi trimmed strong early gains, with tech lagging in Europe too.
The trigger is Alphabet, which said last quarter it would more than double capital spending to as much as $190 billion this year. Investors want evidence that spending is generating returns, and the report lands just as chipmakers have been whipsawed by fears the pace of AI investment cannot hold.
Bitcoin has moved with the AI trade all month, up when the chip complex is strong and down when it wobbles, because the same risk appetite drives both and because bitcoin miners have rebuilt into AI data-center operators.
The majors were quiet otherwise. Ether held near $1,917, up 2% on the week, while Hyperliquid lagged at down 2% over seven days. The Fed meets July 28 and 29, six days after Alphabet gives the market its first hard look at whether the AI build-out is still worth paying for.

title: Bitcoin ETFs extend inflow streak to 6 days with $203M added
summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their inflow streak to six sessions, bringing in about $930 million while remaining down $4.84 billion on a net basis year to date.
full_text:
Bitcoin ETFs extend inflow streak to 6 days with $203M added
US spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their inflow streak to six sessions, bringing in about $930 million while remaining down $4.84 billion on a net basis year to date.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded their sixth consecutive day of net inflows on Tuesday, adding $203.1 million.
The Bitcoin ETFs attracted about $930 million over the six-session streak, their longest run of consecutive inflows since April, according to SoSoValue data.
The inflows came as Bitcoin traded above $65,000 and briefly climbed to $66,700 on Tuesday. At publication, Bitcoin traded at $65,802, up about 2% over the previous 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.
Broader crypto market sentiment also improved on Wednesday, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index rising to “fear” from “extreme fear.”
The recovery comes as analysts said Bitcoin needs to break above and hold the $65,000 to $65,500 range to strengthen the case for a sustained uptrend.
The funds have accumulated $51.8 billion in cumulative net inflows since launch, while total net assets reached $80.9 billion. US spot Bitcoin ETFs remain about $4.84 billion in net outflows year-to-date.

title: BIS warns USD stablecoins can evade capital controls, challenging traditional market regulations
summary: BIS says that FX restrictions and capital controls are less effective against stablecoins than against foreign currency bank deposits.
full_text:
BIS warns USD stablecoins can evade capital controls, challenging traditional market regulations
Quick Take
- The Bank for International Settlements said that dollar-backed stablecoins are “largely unaffected” by capital controls.
- BIS researchers suggested that foreign exchange restrictions and capital controls are less effective against stablecoins than against foreign currency bank deposits.
We'd love your feedback.
The Bank for International Settlements said that dollar-backed stablecoins could bypass capital controls, raising concerns regarding foreign exchange restrictions in emerging markets.
In a study published Tuesday, the BIS analyzed stablecoin flows across more than 130 economies and found that stablecoins appear "largely unaffected by either broad or specific capital flow restrictions," as they partly circulate outside the regulatory perimeter.
Notably, the researchers suggested that foreign exchange restrictions and capital controls — traditional tools governments use to limit money flowing in or out of their countries — are "less effective" against stablecoins than against conventional foreign currency bank deposits.
According to the report, the growing adoption of stablecoins has created a new channel for accessing U.S. dollar liquidity, particularly in emerging markets and developing economies. The BIS warned that policymakers in emerging markets may need to rethink their strategies as "dollarization is hard to reverse once established."
Still skeptical
The latest findings build on the global institution's broader skepticism toward stablecoins. In June 2026, the BIS reiterated in its annual report that stablecoins still fall short of money in singleness, elasticity, interoperability, and integrity, which it says are the foundational properties that any monetary system must keep.
Meanwhile, stablecoins are finding growing usage in both emerging and established economies, as regulators in the U.S., EU, Japan, and other regions are establishing dedicated frameworks to bring stablecoins into the regulated financial system. The total USD stablecoin supply reached $292.6 billion as of Tuesday, up from $253 billion a year ago, according to The Block's data dashboard.

title: US seeks forfeiture of $25 million in crypto tied to global fraud investigations
summary: US prosecutors seek forfeiture of $25 million in crypto recovered from five investigations into international fraud and laundering networks.
full_text:
US seeks forfeiture of $25 million in crypto tied to global fraud investigations
Quick Take
- The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia filed five civil forfeiture complaints seeking over $25 million in cryptocurrency recovered from international fraud schemes targeting U.S. and Canadian residents.
- Prosecutors said the funds are the latest in the more than $800 million recovered as part of the Scam Center Strike Force.
We'd love your feedback.
The U.S. Department of Justice has moved to forfeit more than $25 million in cryptocurrency recovered through five separate investigations into international fraud networks that allegedly targeted residents in the U.S. and Canada.
The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia said in a statement on Tuesday that Secret Service Washington Field Office agents, working through the Cyber Fraud Task Force, identified multiple laundering networks and thousands of victims worldwide who were misled into believing they were making legitimate crypto investments.
According to the statement, the first investigation, flagged by Canadian authorities in late 2024, traced more than 270 suspected victim transactions and seeks roughly $10.4 million. The second, involving online romance schemes with more than 200 victims, seeks approximately $12.1 million.
The third and fourth investigations — reported in May 2026 and March 2026 respectively by victims in the National Capital Region — seek about $1.2 million and $2.4 million. The fifth investigation, involving a fee-based recovery fraud, seeks approximately $285,000.
In each of the five cases, launderers were predominantly located in Southeast Asia, with IP addresses in China, Malaysia, and Cambodia, per the statement.
Prosecutors said the funds are the latest in the more than $800 million recovered as part of the Scam Center Strike Force, an initiative launched in November 2025 by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.
"This $25 million seizure is a direct result of the Scam Center Strike Force I launched in November 2025, and it demonstrates the power of aggressively targeting these international fraud networks," Pirro said. "Our investigators cut through complex laundering schemes, protected victims, and shut down criminal pipelines."

title: Synthesia’s AI training platform is moving beyond videos into live coaching
summary: Synthesia launched AI Roleplay Sessions, an interactive enterprise training platform where employees practice workplace conversations with AI avatars that provide feedback, scoring, and analytics to help companies measure training effectiveness.
full_text:
For years, Synthesia’s pitch was to use AI to help enterprises create interactive training videos, in minutes, for a fraction of the cost normally associated with developing corporate educational materials. The startup’s newest product is making a different bet — that the real moat in enterprise AI isn’t just generating content, but in proving that it worked.
On Wednesday, the British startup launched Roleplay Sessions, an interactive training product where employees can practice high-stakes conversations like sales pitches, performance reviews, and customer complaints with an AI avatar that talks back, pushes back, and then scores them against a rubric.
Roleplay is the first release under a broader “Sessions” platform Synthesia plans to expand into other formats, including job interviews and candidate screening, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.
The launch comes as enterprises take a harder look at whether their AI spend is paying off. Citing a meta-analysis of learning research, Synthesia argues that most corporate training — including, implicitly, its own core video product — stops short of actually changing behavior. The trainings tend to inform and demonstrate, but what really pushes someone into actually learning something is doing that thing, along with feedback.
“Video performs way better than text or sending out a document,” Synthesia CEO and co-founder Victor Riparbelli told TechCrunch. “But for most things, we learn the best by actually practicing something rather than just reading it.”
Roleplay also moves Synthesia into a more defensible position. The company’s avatar and voice technology are proprietary, but the underlying reasoning intelligence is OpenAI’s. By tacking on a layer that includes rubrics, performance data, and analytics, Synthesia is positioning itself less as an AI avatar company and more as a performance-management platform with a video front end.
“From a managerial executive layer, we’re seeing huge interest in mapping out the talent in their company in a way that’s been really difficult to do before,” Riparbelli said. “If you have your entire sales team practice with an AI role player, you can get very granular data on how your sales force is doing overall.”
Synthesia already has a few early Roleplay customers with scaled commercial rollouts, including “one of the top three companies by market cap in Europe, one of the top five Fortune 100, and one of the biggest recruitment companies in the world,” per a company spokesperson.
The two most popular use cases involve training sales teams and leadership — programs like practicing how to sell a product or have a difficult conversation. Much of it is soft skills training, Riparbelli said.
As with Synthesia’s main product, customers can either create their own training programs on the platform or enlist the help of Synthesia’s consultants to build a bespoke solution that relies in part on whatever training documents and context the company already has.
Roleplay is an enterprise offering for now, but the goal is to offer it more widely to small businesses, prosumers, and potentially educational institutions in the next few months as inference costs continue to fall. Riparbelli believes products like Roleplay represent the next phase of enterprise AI adoption, where companies care less about whether AI looks good in a social media demo and more about proving it generates measurable business outcomes.

title: 英國的教訓》將 AI 列為國家核心發展項目，同時砍掉科技部
summary:
英國新首相 Andy Burnham 上任隔天，就裁掉了前首相 Rishi Sunak 才成立兩年五個月的「科 […]

〈英國的教訓》將 AI 列為國家核心發展項目，同時砍掉科技部〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
英國新首相 Andy Burnham 上任隔天，就裁掉了前首相 Rishi Sunak 才成立兩年五個月的「科學、創新暨技術部」（DSIT），同一週卻任命 36 歲的 Kanishka Narayan 出任史上第一位列席內閣的 AI 部長。也在同一週，國家審計署發布報告，直指政府掛在嘴上的「數位轉型與 AI 每年可省 450 億英鎊」缺乏一致的估算方法。
（前情提要：英國 FCA 警告金融 AI「軍備競賽」：催監管 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini等大模型）
（背景補充：臺灣政府正積極布局「主權AI」，國科會主委吳誠文：籌組國家人工智慧戰略特別委員會）
英國 1980 年代的 BBC 政治諷刺劇《Yes, Prime Minister》裡，常務次長 Humphrey Appleby 有一套被引用了四十年的「政治家三段論」。第一步，我們必須做點什麼。第二步，這就是一件什麼。第三步，所以我們必須做它。這句臺詞之所以到今天還在流通，不是因為它好笑，是因為它太少出錯。
2026 年 7 月 20 日到 21 日，英國政府用不到 48 小時，把這個三段論完整地演了一遍。
7 月 20 日，Andy Burnham 在白金漢宮見完 King Charles III，回到唐寧街 10 號門口宣誓要結束政治動盪。他是英國第 59 任首相，也是 2016 年脫歐公投以來十年內的第七位。隔天，他解散了英國唯一一個以科技為名的中央部會。也在隔天，他讓 AI 第一次坐上了內閣會議桌。
這兩件事被大部分媒體分開報導，一方面是官僚重組，一件是人事任命。
英國那個禮拜
這邊要先把英國政治情況解釋一下，因為台灣讀者通常對英國這一輪換任的來龍去脈不熟。
Keir Starmer 在 2024 年 7 月帶工黨拿下壓倒性勝利，但兩年下來個人聲望崩盤，民調顯示選民認為他沒有帶來任何看得見的改變。2026 年 6 月 22 日，Starmer 在黨內議員普遍失去信心的情況下宣布辭去黨魁與首相。
麻煩在於，工黨黨章規定只有國會議員才能參選黨魁，而當時呼聲最高的 Andy Burnham 是大曼徹斯特市長，不是議員。解法是一場補選。Makerfield 選區的議員辭職讓位，Burnham 在 6 月 18 日補選當選，接著在 7 月 17 日以 379 位議員提名（超過工黨全體議員的九成四）在無競爭對手的情況下被推舉為黨魁，7 月 20 日正式接任首相。
上任第二天，他動了 Whitehall 的組織圖。
被關掉的是「科學、創新暨技術部」，2023 年 2 月 7 日由當時的首相 Rishi Sunak 在一次改組中成立，做法是把商業、能源暨產業戰略部拆成三塊，再從數位、文化、媒體暨體育部手上抽走數位政策，拼成一個新部。首任大臣是 Michelle Donelan，這個部活了兩年五個月。
它的職能被拆成三個部分，科技與科學政策併進新成立的「商業、創新、科學暨貿易部」（DBIST），由 Jonathan Reynolds 掌管。AI 政策與公部門的 AI 匯入移進內閣辦公室。數位政府職能，連同政府數位服務（GDS）與中央數位暨資料辦公室（CDDO），回到改名後的數位、文化、媒體暨體育部。原科學大臣 Liz Kendall 去職，科技大臣這個職位就此從英國內閣消失。
同一天，Kanishka Narayan 被任命為 AI 部長，橫跨內閣辦公室與 DBIST，並列席內閣。這是 AI 第一次在英國政府裡拿到內閣層級的席位。
Narayan 的履歷本身就是一個故事，他 1989 年 11 月生於印度比哈爾邦的穆札法普，12 歲隨家人移居威爾斯的卡地夫，一家人住在一房公寓，他走路去上公立中學。後來他念了伊頓公學、牛津大學 Balliol 學院的政治哲學經濟學系，再拿了史丹佛的 MBA。進國會前，他在 David Cameron 任內的內閣辦公室與 Liz Truss 任內的環境部當過公務員。2024 年 7 月，他當選 Vale of Glamorgan 選區議員，成為威爾斯史上第一位少數族裔背景的國會議員。2025 年 9 月接下 AI 與線上安全政務次長，不到一年就升到內閣。
他上任時說，AI 大概是人類史上最重要的技術，而它能帶來的是一個再工業化的英國、更強的國安、被真正改善的公共服務。他也承認有風險，也承認民眾對就業與速度的焦慮。這段話沒有什麼可挑剔的地方，甚至很誠懇的。問題不在他說了什麼，在於這句話是在科技部被解散的第二天說出來的。
英國內閣的特殊羅奇
一個政府對某件事的真實態度，看它開了什麼機關，不如看關掉什麼機關。
設一個部會是一種政治聲明，你需要一次改組、一份公告、幾張新的組織圖。關一個部會是組織定價。你必須在既有的預算、既有的人事、既有的法定職位上動刀，而且要願意承擔重來的成本。
前者告訴你這個政府想被看成什麼樣子，後者告訴你這個內閣願意為這件事付多少錢。
英國科技業對此的反應相當一致。techUK 與 Startup Coalition 聯名寫信給 Burnham，把這個計畫形容為「錯的時間做錯的改變」。他們的理由不是留戀機關，而是拆解本身有成本。他們在信裡點名，把 AI 安全研究院、主權 AI 基金、GDS 與英國研究創新署（UKRI）這些工作打散，會在最需要速度的時候讓一切慢下來。
Startup Coalition 的 Dom Hallas 說得更白。把科技塞進超大型的商業部，等於讓英國的科技公司跟鋼鐵這類產業去搶同一位大臣的注意力。曾任 Keir Starmer AI 機會顧問的 Matt Clifford 把這件事稱為「一個大錯」。創投機構 Plural 合夥人、同時擔任英國 AI 安全研究院主席的 Ian Hogarth 的說法最不帶感情，也最刺人。他說，這種規模的重組基本上會讓相關部會分心一年。
Burnham 政府的說法是，把商業、科學與貿易放在一起，才做得出協調一致的產業戰略。這個理由不算牽強。DSIT 本來就是從商業部拆出來的，拆完之後科技政策與產業政策確實各走各的。
但兩邊講的有點錯亂，政府講的是政策協調，產業講的是注意力分配。協調可以靠流程解決，注意力不行。一個部長一天只有那麼多小時，而在把鋼鐵、貿易談判、產業補貼與 AI 放在同個屋簷下的部會裡，AI 從被服務的領域，變成需要排隊的議題。
Narayan 那張新的內閣椅子，正是為了補上這個缺口而設的。他人在內閣裡，理論上可以跨部會拉動資源。這是升級。只是升級的是一個人，降級的是一整套編制。人會換，編制才會累積。
沒有分母
真正讓這一週值得被寫下來的，不是機關圖，是同一週出現的兩個數字。
第一個數字是 18 億英鎊。這是英國預算責任辦公室（OBR）在 2025 年 11 月，替那張叫「Brit Card」的全國數位身分證估的三年成本，涵蓋 2026-27 到 2028-29 年度。這張卡原本要載明姓名、國籍、出生日期、居留身分與照片，用途是查驗工作權，藉此打擊非法就業。它在 2025 年 9 月被宣布，隨即引爆英國國會請願史上第二大的連署，將近 300 萬人簽名反對。2025 年 10 月，政府被迫拿掉強制條款，改成自願，讓護照等既有證件也能用。整個 2025 年，Keir Starmer 都在為它辯護，還開過閉門會議討論怎麼落地。2026 年 7 月，Burnham 上任後直接把它廢了。
省下來的錢去哪了？值得說清楚，因為外界一度以為會轉進 AI。實際上，Burnham 政府說這筆資源要拿去補家庭電費，作為生活成本紓困的一部分。這是一個政治判斷，不是科技判斷。
第二個數字是 450 億英鎊。這是英國政府拿來描述「數位轉型與 AI 每年可以省下多少錢」的招牌數字，出自 DSIT 在 2025 年 1 月發布的《State of digital government review》。那份報告說，公部門若全面數位化，每年有超過 450 億英鎊「尚未實現的節省與生產力效益」，相當於公部門支出的 4% 到 7%。這個數字後來被首相與部長們反覆引用，成為財政論述的地基之一。
它是怎麼算出來的？DSIT 的假設是，100% 的例行任務與 10% 的非例行任務可以被自動化。
「這是一個合理的猜測，但它當然是一個猜測。它非常難衡量。」前 i.AI（政府 AI 孵化器）主任 Laura Gilbert 在國會作證時，這樣描述 450 億英鎊。
Gilbert 不是這個數字的敵人。她在唐寧街待了四年多，是政府資料科學團隊 10DS 與 i.AI 的創辦主任，是英國政府裡最懂這件事的人之一。她說得很誠實，而誠實在這裡反而更讓人不安。
英國智庫 Institute for Government 的 Nick Davies 講得更直接。他說，除非你有認真的計畫做出相當程度的人力縮減或減少資本支出，否則要達到那 450 億會非常困難。他還補了一句，什麼叫「例行任務」到現在都沒有定義清楚，他甚至懷疑政府自己知不知道。
下議院的科學、創新暨技術委員會在《Rewiring the state》報告裡，把這個數字直接點名為「令人擔憂的樂觀」，並且列為部長帶頭「炒作」的範例，認為這種炒作不是在推動數位轉型，是在拖累它。
然後是國家審計署。7 月 15 日，NAO 發布《政府人力規劃：經驗教訓》，用審計的語言把同一件事再說一次。報告指出，英國公部門僱用 620 萬人，人事成本 2600 億英鎊，76% 的公務員預期 AI 會在五年內改變自己的工作方式。但各部會公布的效率計畫「沒有提供部會如何推匯出預期人力效率的細節」，跨政府之間也沒有一致的方法論。內閣秘書長 Antonia Romeo 自己說過，公務體系的人力計畫「沒有充分反映 AI 與科技將如何改變公務體系的樣貌」。NAO 還補了一刀，公部門本身就缺乏達成這些效率所需要的技術與數位人才。
把這兩個數字並排放，這一週的形狀就出來了。
18 億英鎊是支出。它有明確的年度區間，有一個獨立機構背書，會進預算書，會被審計，也因此可以被砍掉。450 億英鎊是節省。它沒有一致的方法論，沒有可查核的分母，來自一個關於「例行任務」的假設，而它至今沒有被砍掉，因為沒有人被要求把它算給誰看。
政府砍掉了那個可以被驗算的數字，留下了那個不能被驗算的數字。
這就是我覺得這一週真正值得記下來的地方。在會計上，支出與節省是對稱的，一邊減一邊加。在政治上，兩者完全不對稱。支出必須被辯護，節省只需要被相信。當財政缺口壓在頭上，一個沒有分母的節省數字，就是最好用的填補劑。它不用招標，不用進度報告，不用扛延宕，也不用面對將近 300 萬人的連署。
而 AI 現在是這種數字最方便的載體。它夠新，新到沒有歷史基準可以打臉；它夠廣，廣到任何一項效率都可以掛在它名下；它又夠專業，專業到質疑它的人會被說成不懂技術。
DSIT 活了兩年五個月。Brit Card 從宣布到作廢，走了十個月。工黨從壓倒性勝選到換首相，用了兩年。英國從脫歐公投到現在，換了七位首相。
台灣呢
台灣的數位發展部在 2022 年 8 月掛牌，到今天快滿四年，關於它的爭論從來沒停過。專責部會還是分散職能，資源該集中在同個部會，還是嵌進各部會，這些問題跟英國吵的完全是同樣的議題。
英國提供了現成的案例，而且是負面方向的案例。它證明為了「表達重視」而成立的部會，在下一位首相（總統）眼中可能只是能被合併的拼圖。它同時也證明把科技併進大部會，產業界首先擔心的不是政策方向，是自己還排不排得到部長的行事曆。
我不覺得台灣應該從中得出「所以要保住數位發展部」或者「所以應該廢掉」的結論。這兩個結論都太廉價了。真正該問的是，成立到現在，這個部累積出什麼是別人拿不走的？如果答案是一批真的留得住的技術人才、一套跨部會通用的資料與身分基礎建設、幾件做完並且被驗證有效的專案，那它就是拆不動的。
如果答案主要是一套新的組織圖與好幾份年度施政計畫，那它跟英國面臨的治理問題沒有差別。
對政治人物來說，「有爭議」意思是這會掉票，「有勇氣」意思是這會讓你輸掉選舉。

title: 為什麼華語用戶需要自己的預測市場？yoyo market 做到了 Polymarket、Kalshi 做不到的事
summary:
華語用戶缺乏專屬的預測市場平台，歐美主導的Polymarket與Kalshi聚焦美國議題且門檻高。yoyo m […]

〈為什麼華語用戶需要自己的預測市場？yoyo market 做到了 Polymarket、Kalshi 做不到的事〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
華語用戶缺乏專屬的預測市場平台，歐美主導的Polymarket與Kalshi聚焦美國議題且門檻高。yoyo market專為亞太用戶設計，提供在地化事件（如棒球、K-pop、天氣），簡化操作介面，並通過合規策略避開敏感政治題材，填補亞洲40億人口的市場空白，打造真正的群眾智慧感測器。
（前情提要：亞洲終於有了自己的預測市場 — 由亞太團隊打造 yoyo market 全新版本上線）
（背景補充：Kalshi 世界盃吃下 543 億鎂交易量，是 Polymarket 的 2.6 倍）
二〇二四年美國大選夜，全世界盯著的不是 CNN 的計票板，而是一個叫 Polymarket 的網站——川普的勝選機率怎麼一路爬到 60%，最後與結果幾乎吻合。那一夜，預測市場第一次證明：當人們用真金白銀為判斷背書，得到的訊號，比任何民調都準。
但如果你是華語用戶，打開 Polymarket 網站的瞬間，多半只有一種感覺：這一切，好像都是別人的事。 滿屏的美國聯準會、美國大選、美式足球、好萊塢頒獎典禮——沒有一個預測事件，是為你而設。
預測市場在歐美已成氣候，但擁有四十億人口的亞洲，這塊版圖幾乎還是空白。這篇文章談的就是這個缺口，以及正在試著補上它的人。
預測市場的本質：一台聚集人類判斷的「機率感測器」
預測市場，本質上是一個用價格來聚集資訊的市場。 你針對「某件未來的事會不會發生」買賣合約，價格直接等於市場認定的機率：a16z 經濟學家 Scott Duke Kominers 把它形容成一台「機率感測器」，一張合約報價 0.50 美元，就代表市場認為這件事有 50% 的機率發生；你若認為真實機率更高，就買進、把價格推上去。
a16z 更直接點出它勝過傳統民調的四個優勢：能給出即時的機率數字、會隨新資訊動態更新、用真金白銀激勵參與者認真研究、而且任何冷門題目都能開盤。也因此它的用途遠不只下注：企業拿它預測產品上市時程、科學界拿它估實驗成功率、媒體拿它萃取「群眾智慧」。
延伸閱讀：a16z 解析預測市場潛力：不僅是賭盤，更是精準的「機率感測器」
規模也跟著證明了這不是泡沫。2024 大選後產業一度急凍，2025 下半年靠運動、地緣與總經議題二次爆發，到 2026 年 4 月，全產業單月交易量已達約 240 億美元。機構喊出的數字更兇：Bernstein 預估 2030 年交易量上看 1 兆美元；博彩研究機構 Eilers & Krejcik 同樣看到 1 兆美元的量能。這股熱度資本同樣不缺席，Kalshi 估值一年內衝上約 220 億美元，Polymarket 在獲紐交所母公司 ICE 投資後估值來到約 150 億美元。
換句話說：預測市場正在從「加密玩具」變成「導航不確定性的基礎設施」。
Polymarket vs Kalshi：全球兩大預測市場，卻打不到亞洲用戶的核心
這個賽道的兩個主角，代表了兩條路線：加密原生 vs 受監管。
- Polymarket 是全球最大的去中心化預測市場，建在 Polygon 上、以 USDC 結算、用 UMA 預言機裁決。2024 大選的川普對哈里斯單一市場交易量超過 33 億美元；2024 全年約 90 億美元、活躍交易者約 31.4 萬人；2025 年 10 月單月量突破 30 億美元，正式超越選舉峰值。它在 2025 年收購持有 CFTC 牌照的交易所 QCEX、合規重返美國，並獲 ICE 最高 20 億美元投資。
- Kalshi 走的是合規路線，是受美國 CFTC 監管的合約交易所（DCM），用法幣入金、以中央限價訂單簿（CLOB）撮合，像股票交易所一樣運作。它的交易量約八成來自體育賽事，並與 Robinhood 合作打開散戶流量、估值一路衝到約 220 億美元。
兩者規模驚人，但有一個共同點：它們的預測事件與用戶，都繞著美國轉。
40 億人的亞洲，為什麼需要自己的預測市場
因為全球最值得預測的事，有一大半正在亞洲發生，卻沒有一個讓亞洲人下注的地方。
第一，是人口與議題的錯位。亞太地區超過 40 億人、占全球人口六成以上，但 Polymarket 上是美國大選、Kalshi 上是聯準會利率與 NFL。對華語用戶而言，要在這些題目上贏錢，等於跟全世界資訊最靈通的歐美人比誰更懂歐美，即使在資訊秒傳的今天，這仍是一場先天的資訊落差。
第二，是使用門檻。Polymarket 對許多地區設區域限制、Kalshi 僅限美國境內註冊，許多亞洲用戶不是被排除就是被封鎖。卡點往往來自政治、選舉這類敏感題材牽動的法規風險，而一個從一開始就為亞洲設計、主動避開敏感議題的平台，反而能從根本繞過這道牆。
第三，亞洲的題材一點都不弱。大谷翔平每個新球季的表現是橫跨東亞的全民話題；中華職棒季後賽、世界棒球經典賽牽動數千萬人；K-pop 偶像退伍與回歸的聲量勝過任何財報；金馬、金曲、金鐘，台積電法說會、蘋果發表會，甚至「今年夏天台北會不會破 39°C、今年有沒有颱風」，這些議題的密度與黏性，遠比四年一次的選舉更能撐起一個日常平台。
難怪幣安創辦人 CZ 、Polymarket 亞洲市場負責人都喊話「亞洲是重要市場」。亞洲，已是兵家必爭之地。但看好是一回事，真正為亞洲把產品做出來、做到位，是另一回事。
yoyo market 打造亞洲預測市場的 3 大關鍵
yoyo market 創立於 2025 年，是一家美國新創、近期於香港成立分公司，專為亞太用戶打造預測市場。 天使輪由隆領投資（Longling Capital）領投，其創辦人蔡文勝正是美圖（Meitu）共同創辦人，有打造億級用戶產品的實績；投資人還包括 Impa Ventures、Hermitage Capital 等 Web3 投資人與業界專家。
而 yoyo 真正和 Polymarket、Kalshi 拉開差距的，是三根支柱：
1｜在地共鳴（Local by Design）
預測事件是規劃過的，不是翻譯來的。 yoyo 的每一個事件，都由本地團隊從選題開始策劃，圍繞亞太用戶真正在乎的事：東亞體育、K-pop 與華語歌壇、電影、蘋果發表會、天氣氣溫、颱風，乃至牽動區域的社會時事，如台灣在地的媽祖繞境參與人次等。用戶打開平台看到的，是和自己切身相關的議題，而不是別人世界裡的事。
2｜直覺易用（Built for Everyone）
交易輕鬆，沒興趣「滑掉」、感興趣「點」一下。 yoyo 在打造產品，以行動體驗為核心：瀏覽市場時不感興趣的就「滑掉」、感興趣的「點」一下就可以交易。yoyo 沒有複雜的下單介面、不必打開電腦、不需要懂任何鏈上術語，打開手機，五秒完成一筆預測交易。
操作介面越簡單，用戶越能專注在自己的專業判斷上，下單就交給平台處理。
3｜合規優先（Compliance in Mind）
主動劃出邊界，因為想走得更遠。 yoyo 正在申請美國 CFTC 牌照（Kalshi 走過、也是預測市場走向主流的必經之路），並明確不上架選舉、政治、軍事衝突等過度敏感議題。這既是對用戶的保護，也是它想走得長遠所做的選擇。
綜合這三點，結論不難得出：
當你想對美國大選下注，你會去 Polymarket；當你想交易聯準會利率，你會去 Kalshi。但當你想下的是台北或高雄今天氣溫最高幾度、樂天vs味全龍、大谷翔平本季幾轟、哪個 K-pop 團體先回歸、金馬獎誰奪后；這些盤 Polymarket 和 Kalshi 不會開，而願意為亞洲用戶開的，目前就是 yoyo market。
對於亞洲題材有興趣的讀者，可以上 yoyo market 市場小試身手：app.yoyomarket.com

title: 韓國政府拿 512 張 B200 換全民免費 AI，目標國產模型吃下 8 成用量
summary:
韓國科學技術情報通訊部（과학기술정보통신부）7 月 13 日開出「모두의 AI」（全民 AI）標案，要選 2 […]

〈韓國政府拿 512 張 B200 換全民免費 AI，目標國產模型吃下 8 成用量〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
韓國科學技術情報通訊部（과학기술정보통신부）7 月 13 日開出「모두의 AI」（全民 AI）標案，要選 2 到 3 家民間業者，用國產 AI 模型做出全民免費、不限用量的聊天機器人加公共服務代理人，9 月推 beta、12 月正式上線，投標 8 月 11 日截止。政府端出 512 張 NVIDIA B200 當補貼，單一業者最多拿 256 張，外國模型只准用在國產做不到的功能。
（前情提要：韓國端出 8800 億鎂 AI 國家戰略：半導體、實體 AI、資料中心，三個核心要領先）
（背景補充：臺灣政府正積極布局「主權AI」，國科會主委吳誠文：籌組國家人工智慧戰略特別委員會）
韓國科學技術情報通訊部（과학기술정보통신부，以下簡稱科技部）7 月 13 日正式開出「모두의 AI」標案，中文可以直譯成「全民 AI」。政府要從民間挑 2 到 3 家業者，用國產 AI 模型做一套全民都能免費使用、而且不設用量上限的通用聊天機器人，外加一個能幫民眾查詢和申辦政府服務的公共 AI 代理人。
時程壓得很緊，投標受理到今年 8 月 11 日下午 5 點，8 月底選出業者，9 月推出 beta 版，12 月正式對全國開放。
韓國政府這次不是發錢，是發顯卡，標案寫明今年提供 512 張 NVIDIA B200 GPU 給得標者，如果只選 2 家，兩邊各拿 256 張；如果選 3 家，第一順位拿 256 張，第二、第三順位各拿 128 張，最終數量再依業者需求與評選結果調整。
政府當算力包租公，業者只出一成
補助怎麼算？韓媒引述的政府基準是每張 GPU 每月 660 萬韓元，以 256 張計一年約 202.75 億韓元，換算大約 1,350 萬美元，512 張全開則接近 2,700 萬美元。
得標者不是白拿，但也沒有到對等出資。民間對應投資的比例是大企業約政府支援額的 10%、中堅企業 6%、中小企業 5%。政府出九成、業者出一成，這個比例基本上已經寫明瞭誰是主辦方，誰是承包商。
錢也不是隻給一年，2027 年起改由政府預算直接支應營運費用，支援期一路開到 2030 年 12 月 31 日。
國產模型要吃下八成，Naver 已經被刷掉
標案要求得標者的服務必須有 50% 以上使用符合「獨自 AI 基礎模型」標準的國產 AI 模型，另外還要再串接 30% 以上的其他公司國產模型，比例以輸出 token 計算。外國模型只允許用在高難度推論或多模態這類國產真的做不到的功能上，而且不列入政府補助範圍，用太多還會被扣評選分數。
換句話說，八成的輸出必須是韓國自己的模型跑出來的，而且不能全押自家那顆，得分一杯羹給同業。這條規則同時解決了兩件事，把國產模型的實際使用量硬拉上來，又不讓單一大廠獨吞整個國民級入口。
沒有自家模型的公司也能參賽，科技部說明業者可以透過 API、開源版本或授權協議去用別人的國產基礎模型。7 月 21 日的說明會來了約 100 家公司，包括 LG U+、SK Telecom、Naver Cloud、Kakao 以及一票 AI 新創，官方預估最後大概 10 家左右實際投標。
評選也不走跑分那一套，官方說「使用者實際感受到的效能」比技術 benchmark 重要，之後每年評估一次，使用者數太難看的業者會被換掉。使用者數當 KPI，這對做慣了政府標案的韓國大廠來說是完全不同的遊戲規則。
要理解「國產模型」是誰，得回頭看韓國那個 2,136 億韓元（約 1.42 億美元）的「獨自 AI 基礎模型」計畫，也就是韓媒口中的「國家代表 AI」。2025 年選出 5 支精銳隊，分別是 Naver Cloud、LG AI 研究院（LG AI연구원）、SK Telecom、Upstage 與 NC AI，目標是做出效能追上最新全球模型九成五的自研模型。
512 張卡要扛 5,100 萬人
韓國在野質疑聲音很直接，表示 512 張 B200 只佔韓國目前已投入獨自模型、產學研究與國家計畫的約 11,600 張 B200 等值算力的 4.4%。一位 AI 業者主管對韓媒說，512 張再切給 2 到 3 家營運商，全民尖峰流量時「算力不足的可能性相當大」。
而且這套服務不是只跑聊天，還要吃下多模態請求與行政系統串接，每則查詢的算力消耗都是加乘的。韓國科技部的反駁是，這不是訓練基礎模型的專案，不需要動輒上千張卡，業者本來就得自己補基礎設施，初期也只有基本聊天與簡單公共服務，「token 消耗量不會太誇張」。

title: 50 萬筆 ChatGPT 對話，34% 對話量拿來寫同人色情小說
summary:
華盛頓大學與科羅拉多大學波德分校的研究團隊分析 57 萬筆真實 ChatGPT 對話，想搞懂人類到底怎麼用 A […]

〈50 萬筆 ChatGPT 對話，34% 對話量拿來寫同人色情小說〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
華盛頓大學與科羅拉多大學波德分校的研究團隊分析 57 萬筆真實 ChatGPT 對話，想搞懂人類到底怎麼用 AI 寫小說，結果撞見一名匿名使用者在數個月內上千次要模型一直寫同一個小說場景。更關鍵的是用 GPT 寫小說的帳號裡面， 2% 的人就寫掉超過 8 成對話量。
（前情提要：人腦比機器好？幾萬人在網站上假裝自己是 ChatGPT）
（背景補充：Deezer 警告 44% 新上傳音樂是 AI 生成，人類創作者的血汗錢正被集體洗劫）
在學校的社團教室裡，一個叫 Natsuki 的女高中生摀著肚子說，Sakura，偏偏挑這種時候，你決定要在這裡出生，不能再等兩個月嗎。
社長 Monika 問她怎麼了。她咬著牙回答，羊水破了，Sakura 要出來了，而她完全不知道該怎麼辦。
然後這段劇本在一句話的中間戛然而止。「我的身體⋯⋯它」，句子斷在這裡，沒有下文。
這不是遊戲的原始劇情，是有人手打出來貼進 ChatGPT 對話方塊的一段文字。斷句是刻意的，那是留給模型接手的位置。
然後這個人把幾乎一模一樣的東西，再貼一次。接著又一次。持續了好幾個月，上千次。
這個奇怪現象出現在論文裡
上面那段對話，完整收錄在 2026 年 6 月 22 日上傳到 arXiv 的論文《AI Fiction in the Wild》（編號 2606.22748）裡。作者是華盛頓大學資訊學院的 Neel Gupta 與 Melanie Walsh，以及科羅拉多大學波德分校資工系的 Maria Antoniak。這篇論文 2025 年 9 月在普渡大學的 MFS Cultural AI 研討會發表過，預計刊登於文學期刊《MFS: Modern Fiction Studies》。
7 月初，日媒 AUTOMATON 與電競媒體 Dexerto 幾乎同時報導了論文裡這個橋段，截圖隨即在 X 上瘋傳，成為七月最大的科技迷因之一。
先修正一件事，中英文報導普遍稱這名使用者為「極端離群值（extreme outlier）」，但論文全文並沒有出現過這個詞。研究者實際用的說法是「特別多產的離群值」，以及一個他們自創的分類，「無限故事索求者（infinite story demander）」，指的是那些在很長一段時間裡反覆索取同一個或高度相似故事橋段的人。
《Doki Doki Literature Club!》（心跳文學社）是 2017 年上架的視覺小說遊戲，表面上是清新的校園戀愛題材，玩下去才會發現它是一款玩弄後設敘事的心理恐怖作品。Natsuki、Monika、Yuri、Sayori 是文學社的四名成員。這款遊戲在台灣的知名度不算高，但在英文網路上是同人創作重鎮。
三分之一的對話都在寫小說
研究團隊用的資料集叫 WildChat，總共 573,453 筆英文對話。經過分類後，其中 195,271 筆涉及虛構內容生成，佔 34%。
在這 19 萬筆小說類對話裡，同人創作佔 95,450 筆（49%），情色小說內容佔 52,231 筆（27%）。兩者高度重疊。
而最受歡迎的作品世界觀，第一名就是《Doki Doki Literature Club!》，22,381 筆對話，佔小說子集的 11.5%。
第二名是動作遊戲《Freedom Planet》，5,204 筆，2.6%。接著是英雄聯盟 4,514 筆、火影忍者 4,342 筆。
論文特別點出，這份排行榜跟全球最大同人平台 AO3 的熱門作品完全不同。AO3 上排前面的是哈利波特、星際大戰、漫威這類西方主流 IP。WildChat 的榜單長得完全不一樣。
2% 的人寫掉 8 成的對話
論文裡有一句話很誇張。
「小說子集裡 2% 的使用者，要為超過 80% 的對話負責。」
這裡要精確一點，素材流傳的版本說「2% 的帳號貢獻超過 8 成互動量」，但論文講的單位是對話數，不是互動量、訊息數或 token 數。這個區別很重要，因為對話數才是各家 AI 公司最常拿出來公布的那種指標。
而這 2% 的人在做什麼？研究者算了一個「prompt 重複率」，看同一個使用者的提示詞有多高比例落在同一個語意群集裡。
一般使用者（至少有兩筆對話）的重複率是 42%。
前 2% 的重度使用者，69%。
最多產的前十名使用者，85%。
這 57 萬筆對話是從免費 GPT 撈的
這是最容易被誤讀的一環，而它決定了整篇論文能推論到什麼程度。
WildChat 由艾倫人工智慧研究院（AI2）收集，時間是 2023 年 4 月 9 日到 2024 年 5 月 1 日。收集方式不是從 OpenAI 拿資料，而是在 Hugging Face Spaces 上架設免費的 GPT-3.5 Turbo 與 GPT-4 聊天介面，使用者點兩次同意彈窗，就能換到不用登入、沒有速率限制的免費使用權，代價是聊天紀錄可能被公開。
論文自己在方法論裡寫得很清楚，WildChat 不是所有 ChatGPT 使用者的代表性樣本。研究者推測這群人「比一般使用者更懂技術、更活在網路上」，也可能是來自低收入地區、來自 ChatGPT 被禁的國家，或者單純想測試模型底線、生成平台明令禁止內容的人。
34% 掉到 7.1%
研究團隊接著做了一件很簡單、但結果很兇的事。
他們用雜湊過的 IP 位址推估使用者身分，12,947 個 IP 收斂成大約 10,082 名使用者。然後，每個使用者只保留一筆對話。
小說類的佔比，從 34% 掉到 7.1%。
同一批資料，同一個問題，換一種演算法，答案差了將近五倍。
不只總量。論文在註腳裡補了一刀，一人一則之後，《Doki Doki Literature Club!》的排名「急遽下滑」，取而代之爬上榜的是《權力遊戲》和《寶可夢》這種真正大眾的作品。
也就是說，「ChatGPT 使用者最愛寫《Doki Doki Literature Club!》同人」這個結論，本身就是少數幾個人重複行為堆出來的假象。
上千次寫一個生小孩的橋段
值得注意的是，論文對這名匿名使用者的態度不是嘲笑。
研究者把這種行為放進「重複消費」的心理學脈絡裡，重看同一部電影、重逛同一座城市、重訪同一間美術館，有些研究甚至認為這類體驗「沒有人們以為的那麼重複」。
他們還借用了角色扮演遊戲的術語「re-rolling（重骰）」，玩家反覆重開，直到跑出滿意的數值。研究者觀察到，這名使用者通常會在某一次之後，把模型剛剛生成的回覆接回自己的提示詞裡，再重開一局，代表他終於喜歡上了那個版本。
論文對他的敘事給了一個很準的描述，「用大型語言模型生成的故事，每一個結局都稍有不同，同一個故事被重新做成新的」。
在這篇論文的框架裡，他不是異常，他是一種新讀者的極端形態。研究者稱之為「唯我論的讀者兼作者（solipsistic reader-writer）」，一個人在封閉的對話迴圈裡同時生產與消費故事，另一端沒有其他人類。
寫作與閱讀，向來需要兩個人。但用 AI 創作這兩個角色很可能是同一人。
所有「AI 正在重塑創作」的句子，都少了一個主詞
回到最開始那個問題。
我們每天都在讀這樣的句子。AI 正在改變人類創作。AI 生成內容爆炸性成長。某平台每月生成幾億則內容。某模型週活躍使用者突破幾億。
這些句子沒有一句是假的。它們只是全部省略了同一件事，誰在用，用了幾次。
一份 57 萬筆對話的資料集，34% 跟寫小說有關，聽起來像是一個時代的轉向。攤開來看，是一萬人裡的兩百個人，各自在同一個坑裡挖了幾千次。把每個人的權重拉平，這個時代的轉向就縮水成 7.1%。
下一次你看到某個 AI 產品公布「本月生成一億則內容」，值得多問那一億則是幾個人生成的？
這不是要否認 AI 創作正在發生。研究者自己也說，他們認為類似的重度使用者「很可能也在 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 上強迫性地生成小說」。這件事是真的。
真正的問題在於，用「使用量」去描述「使用者」，是一種結構性的誤讀。而整個 AI 產業目前公布的每一個數字，用的都是前者。
本文源自 arXiv: AI Fiction in the Wild，由動區動趨整理報導。

title: 日本 Sakana AI 丟出資安模型 Fugu-Cyber，自評與 Mythos-Preview 同等級
summary:
日本 AI 獨角獸 Sakana AI 於 7 月 21 日推出資安特化模型 Fugu-Cyber，官方公告指 […]

〈日本 Sakana AI 丟出資安模型 Fugu-Cyber，自評與 Mythos-Preview 同等級〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
日本 AI 獨角獸 Sakana AI 於 7 月 21 日推出資安特化模型 Fugu-Cyber，官方公告指出在漏洞驗證榜單 CyberGym 拿下 86.9% 成功率、威脅情報榜單 CTI-REALM 拿下 72.1%，並自評與 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.5-Cyber、Anthropic 的 Mythos-Preview 等資安前沿模型「同級」。
（前情提要：日本 AI 獨角獸上線 Sakana Fugu：自動呼叫多種模型可媲美 Claude Mythos？跑分、價格一次看）
（背景補充：GPT-5.5-Cyber 資安能力打敗 Claude Mythos！白宮放行 vs 被封殺兩種命運）
日本 AI 獨角獸 Sakana AI（サカナ AI）7 月 21 日在官方部落格宣布，旗下編排模型 Sakana Fugu 家族新增資安特化版本 Fugu-Cyber，以獨立 API 端點提供。官方公告指出，Fugu-Cyber 在 CyberGym 取得 86.9% 成功率、在 CTI-REALM 取得 72.1%，並直接點名這個成績「與 GPT-5.5-Cyber、Mythos-Preview 這類專攻資安的前沿模型相當（comparable to）」。
這裡先幫中文圈的讀者校正一件事。官方用的字是「相當」，不是「超越」，公告裡也沒有排名表。部分簡中媒體把標題寫成「效能超越 GPT-5.5-Cyber」，那不是 Sakana AI 說的。
兩個榜單測的完全不是同一件事，值得用白話講清楚。CyberGym 是加州大學柏克萊分校（UC Berkeley）做的評測，把 188 個真實開源專案、1,507 個真實漏洞丟給 AI，要 AI 讀懂整包程式碼、追依賴、推理記憶體行為，最後做出一個能觸發漏洞的驗證程式。CTI-REALM 則是要 AI 讀一份威脅情報報告，翻成資安團隊能直接上線的偵測規則，中間還得對映 MITRE 攻擊技術、寫出 KQL 查詢。前者是「找洞」，後者是「守洞」。
2025 年 6 月 CyberGym 論文剛發表時，當時最強的 AI agent 成功率只有 11.9%。一年出頭，題目沒換，數字站上 86.9%。這條斜率本身比誰排第一名更值得盯著看。
不自建大模型
Fugu-Cyber 不是 Sakana AI 從零訓練的新大模型，這點是整件事最關鍵的地方。
Sakana Fugu 的本體是一套「多代理編排」（orchestration）系統，白話說就是它自己不解題，而是當排程員。收到任務後，它動態把一群專長不同的模型分派成 Thinker（想）、Worker（做）、Verifier（驗）三種角色，跑完再把結果收斂成一個回覆，對外只露出一個 API。這套排程邏輯出自 Sakana AI 兩篇 ICLR 2026 論文 TRINITY 與 the Conductor，底下實際叫了哪幾家的模型，官方明講「屬於專有資訊，設計上就不對外揭露」。
Fugu 家族目前有三個版本，Fugu（日常均衡）、Fugu Ultra（複雜推理）、Fugu Cyber（資安）。換句話說，7 月 21 日這一發不是新引擎，是同一副骨架換上資安專用的配置與使用條款。
這正是 Sakana AI 一貫的打法。這家公司 2023 年由前 Google 研究員 David Ha 與 Llion Jones（2017 年《Attention Is All You Need》論文共同作者之一）在東京創立，招牌是演化式模型合併、AI Scientist 這類「不靠堆算力」的路子。去年 11 月的 B 輪拿下 320 億日圓（約 2 億美元），投後估值約 4,320 億日圓（約 27 億美元），股東名單裡除了 MUFG、Google、Salesforce Ventures，還有美國情報體系的創投 In-Q-Tel。一家日本資安模型公司的股東名單上出現 In-Q-Tel，這個組合本身就滿有畫面的。
價格分兩級，門檻卡在申請表
計價方式官方公告本身沒寫，實際費率掛在 Sakana Fugu 產品頁的 Token Plan。Fugu-Cyber 每百萬 token 輸入 6 美元、輸出 36 美元、快取輸入 0.6 美元；上下文超過 272K token 之後跳一級，輸入 12 美元、輸出 54 美元、快取輸入 1.2 美元。
所以外傳的「輸入 6 到 12 美元、輸出 36 到 54 美元」不是浮動區間，是兩段式階梯，多數情況下你付的是 6 與 36。對照家族內另一款 Fugu Ultra 的 5 美元與 30 美元，資安版只貴了兩成。
真正的門檻在 Fugu-Cyber 採申請制，使用者必須填表說明用途、附上已驗證的聯絡資訊，由 Sakana AI 團隊逐件人工審查，透過才給存取權。同時公告搭配修訂後的使用條款，明文禁止攻擊性濫用。

title: Suno 帳號 5530 萬組個資外洩，駭客順手丟出「侵權鐵證」到唱片公司
summary:
AI 音樂平台 Suno 在 2025 年 11 月遭駭，5,530 萬組使用者 email 與數萬筆 Str […]

〈Suno 帳號 5530 萬組個資外洩，駭客順手丟出「侵權鐵證」到唱片公司〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
AI 音樂平台 Suno 在 2025 年 11 月遭駭，5,530 萬組使用者 email 與數萬筆 Stripe 付款紀錄外流，直到今年 7 月 20 日才被 Have I Been Pwned 收錄。更麻煩的是駭客連 2023 至 2024 年的原始碼一起丟出來，裡面清楚寫著 Suno 從 YouTube Music、Deezer、Genius 等來源抓了超過 38 萬小時音樂與歌詞，而這正是 Sony Music 與 UMG 現在告它的核心指控。
（前情提要：Sony 告 Suno 本月開庭：AI 拿版權歌曲訓練算不算「合理使用」首度上法庭）
（背景補充：AI 音樂新創 Suno 估值半年翻倍衝上 54 億美元，與華納和解簽下版權授權將推新產品）
帳號外洩本身已經夠糟，真正致命的是駭客順手附上的那份原始碼。
這場入侵發生在 2025 年 11 月，被攤在陽光下卻是八個月後的事。資安通報服務 Have I Been Pwned 於 7 月 20 日新增 Suno 條目，創辦人 Troy Hunt 在登入說明中指出，這批資料含有超過 5,530 萬組不重複的 email，若使用者當初是用手機號碼註冊，電話也一併在內。Troy Hunt 另外提到，其中 24% 的 email 早就出現在 HIBP 既有的外洩資料庫裡。
登入說明指出，外洩資料還包含數萬筆 Stripe 紀錄，欄位涵蓋姓名、實體地址、購買金額，以及卡別、到期日與卡號末四碼。Suno 澄清公司本身無法透過 Stripe 讀取完整卡號，直接盜刷的風險有限。這說法沒錯，但姓名加地址加消費紀錄的組合，本來就是釣魚信最好用的原料。
Suno 發言人 Rachel Racusen 沒有否認受影響人數，也確認公司在 2025 年 11 月發生資安事件。不過 Suno 官網至今沒有公告這件事，也沒有提出通知使用者的紀錄。真正把訊息推出來的是 404 Media 的報導，公司是跟在後面承認的那一方。
外洩原始碼把爬蟲公開
對唱片公司來說，帳號外洩只是開胃菜。駭客同時發布 2023 至 2024 年的 Suno 原始碼，裡面直接寫著訓練素材的來源與規模。404 Media 清點後列出的清單，除了外界原本就在猜的 YouTube Music、Deezer、Genius，還有音效素材庫 Pond5、Jamendo、Freesound、國際樂譜圖書館計畫（IMSLP），以及透過 RSS 抓取的 podcast。
光是 YouTube Music 就有 2,013,545 段音樂片段、113,879 小時，另一組標記為 ytm_tagged 的 152,162 小時，加上 Pond5 的 62,117 小時、IMSLP 的 19,514 小時、Genius 的 17,615 小時、Deezer 的 12,287 小時、Jamendo 的 3,726 小時。全部加總超過 38 萬小時，換算大約 43 年不間斷的音訊。程式碼裡的資料夾名稱就寫著 genius_hq、youtube_music、deezer、ytm_tagged，連包裝都懶得做。
這份清單的價值在於它不需要翻譯。過去兩年，唱片公司要證明 AI 模型吃過自家歌曲，得靠音訊指紋比對、拿輸出結果反推，還要請專家證人上庭解釋演算法。
Warner 已經上岸，Sony 跟 UMG 還在水裡
訴訟背景要拉回 2024 年。美國唱片業協會（RIAA）代表 Sony Music Entertainment、UMG Recordings 與 Warner Records 對 Suno 與 Udio 提起著作權訴訟，核心指控就是未經授權大規模抓取版權錄音訓練模型。Suno 一路的抗辯都是合理使用，甚至在法律檔案中承認自己訓練用了「網路上開放取得、品質合理的幾乎所有音樂檔案」，規模達數千萬首錄音。
三家原告後來分道揚鑣。Warner Music Group 在 2025 年 11 月 25 日和解並轉為授權合作，Suno 估值隨後翻倍衝上 54 億美元。Sony 與 UMG 選擇繼續打，本月才剛就合理使用進行首度正面攻防。

title: 川普喊晶片回美國！台積電毛利率要被吃掉 4 個百分點，2027 再漲價？
summary:
台積電剛交出史上最賺的一季，毛利率 67.7%、稅後純益年增 77.4%，同一場法說會上財務長黃仁昭卻預告，海 […]

〈川普喊晶片回美國！台積電毛利率要被吃掉 4 個百分點，2027 再漲價？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
台積電剛交出史上最賺的一季，毛利率 67.7%、稅後純益年增 77.4%，同一場法說會上財務長黃仁昭卻預告，海外晶圓廠陸續投產將在未來數年持續稀釋毛利率，初期約 2 到 3 個百分點，後期可能擴大到 3 到 4 個百分點。晨星估算，在美國生產的成本比台灣高出 20% 到 50%。
（前情提要：川普：美光在美國投資 2500 億鎂！這是我的「川普效應」能創造 10 萬職缺）
（背景補充：台經院喊今年 GDP 成長破 10%：AI 商機潮能撐到 2028 年）
重點摘要
- 台積電 Q2 毛利率 67.7% 創高，稅後純益年增 77.4% 至新台幣 7,066 億元
- 財務長黃仁昭預告海外廠稀釋毛利率初期 2-3 個百分點、後期擴大到 3-4 個百分點
- 晨星估美國生產成本高出台灣 20-50%，台積電計畫 2027 年調漲代工價 5-10%
台積電交出史上最賺的一季，法說會上，財務長暨發言人黃仁昭也把未來幾年的成本帳單攤開。據 CNBC 報導，川普政府推動先進晶片製造回流美國，海外產能擴張正在墊高台積電的生產成本，並將在未來數年持續拖累公司毛利率。
先看賺的部分，台積電 2026 年第二季合併營收約新台幣 1 兆 2,704 億元，年增 36%；稅後純益約新台幣 7,066 億元，每股純益 27.25 元，兩者年增幅都是 77.4%，雙雙改寫歷史紀錄。毛利率 67.7%，比第一季的 66.2% 再高出 1.5 個百分點，2 奈米製程本季也開始貢獻營收。
再看之後要付出的部分，黃仁昭在法說會上說明，海外晶圓廠陸續投產，未來數年初期將稀釋毛利率約 2 到 3 個百分點，後期可能擴大到 3 到 4 個百分點。台積電對第三季的毛利率指引已經下修到 65% 到 67% 區間。
2000 億美元的「政治帳單」
自川普 2025 年重返白宮以來，台積電對美投資承諾累計已達 2000 億美元，其中包括上週法說會同步公布的 1000 億美元先進半導體製造及先進封裝計畫。加計 CHIPS 法案時期的 650 億美元，台積電在美國的總投資額來到 2650 億美元，規劃 10 座晶圓廠與 2 座先進封裝廠。白宮把這筆錢直接列為川普貿易與產業政策推動的成果。
台積電同時把 2026 年資本支出上調至 600 億到 640 億美元，全年營收成長預估上修到 4 成以上。錢照砸，只是這輪砸的位置離台灣愈來愈遠。
多出來的成本最後誰付
晨星（Morningstar）資深股票分析師 Phelix Lee 估算，台積電在美國生產的晶片，成本會比台灣製造高出 20% 到 50%，實際數字取決於補貼撥款時點、稅收抵免的認列方式與其他成本波動。
台積電在美國生產的晶片成本，會比台灣製造高出 20% 到 50%，取決於補貼時點、稅收抵免認列與其他成本波動。（晨星資深股票分析師 Phelix Lee）
市場普遍預期台積電會把一部分成本轉給客戶，《日經亞洲》先前報導，台積電計畫從 2027 年初調漲晶圓代工價格，先進製程與成熟製程的基本漲幅落在 5% 到 10%，若客戶追加高效能運算（HPC）訂單超出原先預估需求，還要再加收 10% 到 15% 溢價，部分先進製程訂單的實際漲幅會超過 10%。
給客戶一年半調整預算與供應鏈，這是議價方有本錢才做得起的安排。
台灣專家看法
台經院產經資料庫總監劉佩真接受 《聯合報》 訪問時表示，這次加碼「並不令人意外」，「台積電原本就產能不足，既要符合美國在地製造，且要防範競爭對手搶單，加大對美投資符合台積電利益」。她也指出台灣的水電供給已接近極限，台積電勢必要在全球做產能槓桿。
劉佩真提醒，台積電「在台創造的就業及投資規模，可能會受影響」，並強調「台積電必須根留台灣，在台灣的先進製程與美國時間差至少兩年以上，才能確保台灣優勢與利益」。
微驅科技總經理吳金榮則對 《商業周刊》 分析，海外擴廠吃掉的毛利，換來的是跟客戶更深度的綁定，台積電從晶圓到 CoWoS 封裝的一條龍服務，「這種整合能力，短期內沒人能複製」。他同時點出 3 奈米製程良率趨穩、折舊壓力遞減，該節點毛利率下半年可望超越公司平均水準，正好補上海外廠咬掉的部分。
外資的定價也偏向這一邊，法說會後多家券商調升台積電目標價，最高喊到 4,200 元。至於台灣這邊真正要盯的指標，其實是劉佩真講的那個「兩年時間差」。美國 10 座廠蓋完是十年後的事，先進製程留在台灣的領先幅度還剩多少？明年的漲價只是一個過渡。
常見問題
台積電為什麼要去美國建廠？成本不是比較高嗎？
主因是川普政府推動先進晶片製造回流美國，加上客戶要求供應鏈分散風險。晨星估算美國生產成本比台灣高 20% 到 50%，但台積電對美投資已累計 2650 億美元，規劃 10 座晶圓廠與 2 座先進封裝廠。
台積電 2027 年漲價會漲多少？
根據《日經亞洲》報導，先進製程與成熟製程基本漲幅為 5% 到 10%，2027 年初生效。若客戶追加 HPC 訂單超出原估需求，還要再加收 10% 到 15% 溢價，部分先進製程訂單實際漲幅會超過 10%。

title: Andrej Karpathy 公開大神 Prompt 心法：開語音跟 AI 狂聊 10 分鐘
summary:
OpenAI 創始成員、現任 Anthropic 預訓練團隊成員 Andrej Karpathy 週二（7/2 […]

〈Andrej Karpathy 公開大神 Prompt 心法：開語音跟 AI 狂聊 10 分鐘〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 創始成員、現任 Anthropic 預訓練團隊成員 Andrej Karpathy 週二（7/21）在 X 上公開自己跟 LLM 協作的固定套路，遇到複雜任務時他不打字，直接切到語音輸入連講 10 分鐘，內容可以跳躍、混亂、毫無章法。他的觀察是模型很擅長從語無倫次的長篇裡還原你真正想做的事，吐回來的版本通常比你自己講的還乾淨。
（前情提要：OpenAI 創始成員 Andrej Karpathy 宣布加入 Anthropic：重返 LLM 研發最前線）
（背景補充：Andrej Karpathy 提煉「CLAUDE.md 四大準則」引爆 GitHub，讓 AI 寫 Code 準確率飆破 90%）
懶得打字，就用講的。Andrej Karpathy 週二（7/21）在 X 上寫下自己跟 LLM 協作的一個固定套路，需要交代的背景太多、手指卻跟不上腦袋的時候，他會往椅背一靠，切到 /voice 語音輸入，然後連續講 10 分鐘。「完全一團亂，什麼都可以講，全程意識流。」
One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10…
— Andrej Karpathy (@karpathy) July 21, 2026
有時候他會先跟模型打聲招呼，在開頭補一句「切換成語音辨識了，錯字先說聲抱歉」；有時候他乾脆把這段獨白變成一場小型訪談，讓模型反過來追問幾輪，把散落的線索一條一條挖出來。
語音輸入本身不是新東西，Karpathy 真正在講的是輸入量。與其花力氣把想法整理成一段乾淨的指令，不如把整包想法直接丟過去，讓模型自己拆開來重組。
前期多講一點，後面少改一點
他給的理由很直接。「LLM 不知為何非常擅長重建冗長而語無倫次的獨白，它們迴音給你的那份，往往比你原本那團思緒還乾淨得多。」他寫道，結果是 mind meld（心靈融合，指人跟模型對彼此意圖的理解逐漸對齊）改善了，從那個時間點之後，需要回頭糾正的地方反而更少。
這句話點出這套方法真正的成本結構。大部分人省了前期打字的力氣，代價是後面反覆修正、來回丟訊息澄清自己的意思；Karpathy 的做法是把成本全部押在前面那 10 分鐘，用一次超大量的背景資訊交代，換掉後面五輪的「不是這個意思」。
反對的人都擔心同一件事
X 回覆區大致分成兩派。支援的人說這套已經佔掉自己八成的 prompt，也有人形容改以語音為主之後產出效率翻了 5 到 8 倍，多語使用者則喜歡它不挑語言。
反對的聲音則集中在同一個顧慮，把「把話講清楚」這件事整個外包給模型，長期下來自己的組織能力跟寫作能力會不會退化。有人給出折衷做法，模型整理完之後自己再手動蒸餾一次，不要照單全收。
兩邊其實沒有誰對誰錯，Karpathy 的用法是把模型當成會整理的鏡子，不是代筆，差別只在你有沒有把它整理出來的版本讀回去。
用 6 個 Prompt 打造完整學習系統：學習階梯、20法則、費曼迴圈…
Claude 寫程式瘋狂犯錯裝傻？改造 Andrej Karpathy 的12 條規則幫你把錯誤率從 41% 砍到 3％

title: AI 燒錢今晚交卷：Alphabet 攤牌 1,900 億鎂資本支出，特斯拉迎來極大波動
summary:
Alphabet 與特斯拉將於臺灣時間 7 月 23 日凌晨、美股盤後同步公布 2026 年第二季財報，Int […]

〈AI 燒錢今晚交卷：Alphabet 攤牌 1,900 億鎂資本支出，特斯拉迎來極大波動〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Alphabet 與特斯拉將於臺灣時間 7 月 23 日凌晨、美股盤後同步公布 2026 年第二季財報，Intel 緊接在隔天。選擇權市場已經先站好位置，押特斯拉財報後單日震盪 5.91%，換算約 830 億美元市值，是這家公司一年來最大的財報波動預期。市場真正要問的不是這兩家賺多少，而是今年砸下去的 7,000 億美元 AI 資本支出，到底換回了什麼。
（前情提要：Google 推出 Gemini 3.6 Flash 等三款新模型！3.5 Flash-Lite 飆出極速，Gemini 4 預訓練已啟動）
（背景補充：花旗喊「美股七巨頭已死」，改押注橫跨六大產業的成長型公司）
重點摘要
- 選擇權市場押特斯拉財報後震盪 5.91%，約 830 億美元市值懸在一線
- Alphabet 今年資本支出上看 1,900 億美元，Q1 自由現金流卻年減 47% 只剩 101 億
- 特斯拉 Q2 交車 480,126 輛創新高，市場只盯不含碳權的汽車毛利率守不守得住 18%
選擇權市場的定價已經把話說完了。Benzinga 統計，特斯拉財報前的隱含波動來到 5.91%，以 1.4 兆美元市值換算，等於有 830 億美元的市值押在今晚這份財報上，是本週所有公布財報的公司裡絕對金額第二大的一家。
CNBC 則指出，這是交易員一年來對特斯拉開出的最大財報波動預期，上一次押到 6% 已經是 2025 年 10 月的事。
Alphabet 這邊相對剋制，選擇權隱含約 5.4% 的單日移動，但它的市值是 4.3 兆美元，任何一個百分點都是好幾千億在跑。Intel 排在 7 月 23 日盤後，隱含波動高達 12%。三份財報擠在同一個禮拜，被分析師形容為 AI 支出週期至今最完整的單週檢驗點。
兩家公司進場的姿勢都不太好看，Alphabet 上週五收在 346.77 美元，距離今年 408.61 美元的高點回檔約 15%；特斯拉今年以來跌了 18%，是七巨頭裡表現最差的一個，離 52 週高點 498.83 美元還有約 25% 的距離。財報還沒開，股價已經先跌給你看。
Alphabet 的問題是錢花去哪
市場對 Alphabet 第二季的共識落在營收 1,136 億至 1,168 億美元之間（各家資料商口徑不同），每股盈餘 2.87 美元，去年同期是 964 億美元與 2.31 美元。這個成績單本身不難看。
難看的是現金流那一頁，Alphabet 上一季把全年資本支出指引拉高到 1,800 億至 1,900 億美元，還告訴投資人 2027 年會再往上跳一大階。第一季單季資本支出年增 107% 來到 357 億美元，同一時間自由現金流年減約 47%，只剩 101 億美元。花得比去年多一倍，手上剩的少一半，這個剪刀差就是今晚所有人要問的那一題。
支撐這筆錢的敘事是雲端，Google Cloud 第一季營收年增 63%，訂單積壓（backlog）單季幾乎翻倍到超過 4,600 億美元，市場預期第二季雲端營收再增約 65% 到 225 億美元，搜尋業務則約 632.9 億美元。積壓訂單是漂亮數字，但積壓不等於入帳，今晚要看的是這 4,600 億轉成營收的速度有沒有跟上折舊的速度。
另個問題插在 Gemini，Google 五月在 I/O 開發者大會上說 Gemini 3.5 Pro 六月上線，到七月中還是沒有出現。彭博報導指出，Google 為了拉高 Gemini 的程式碼能力更新了訓練資料，結果不如預期，而企業客戶最在意的就是這塊。
動區昨日才報導 Google 一口氣發布 Gemini 3.6 Flash 等三款模型、Gemini 4 也已進入預訓練。Flash 系列連發三款、旗艦 Pro 沒出，這本身就是回答。
分析師倒沒有集體轉空，Guggenheim 的 Michael Morris 維持買進、目標價 450 美元，直接把 Gemini 延遲視為「全端 AI 領導者的進場點」而不是基本面問題；BMO Capital 上調至 455 美元、KeyBanc 上調至 445 美元。但 UBS 把目標價下修到 400 美元、Wells Fargo 下修到 416 美元，多空的分歧點幾乎都落在同一句話：這 1,900 億買的是護城河，還是折舊。
特斯拉交車創新高
特斯拉第二季交付 480,126 輛，是公司史上最好的一季，數字七月初就已公布，問題是這件事沒有換來股價。
共識數字非常分歧，特斯拉七月十七日在投資人關係頁面公布自家彙編的分析師共識，營收 275.8 億美元、非美國通用會計準則每股盈餘 0.55 美元、美國通用會計準則每股盈餘 0.36 美元、淨利 15 億美元。但市場上流通的版本從 252.4 億到 264 億美元都有，每股盈餘 0.44 到 0.55 美元不等。同一家公司、同一季，賣方之間差出二十幾億美元的營收，這種分歧度本身就是波動的來源。
真正的戰場在毛利率，分析師預期不含碳權的汽車毛利率略高於 18%，這條線守不守得住，比多賣幾萬台車重要多了。現金部分同樣吃緊，市場預估特斯拉第二季的自由現金流為負 32.5 億美元，資本支出接近 67 億美元，錢都投去了 AI 基礎建設、產能擴張與 Robotaxi 部署。
交車創新高，特斯拉卻是七巨頭中跌最慘的。
Morgan Stanley 的 Adam Jonas 把特斯拉形容為「完全被前置定價」的股票，維持中性評等、目標價 417 美元。翻成白話就是：現在的股價已經先把 Robotaxi 和 Optimus 的成功算進去了，沒有實際部署，就沒有新的上漲理由。
而實際部署的進度已經落後，Robotaxi 目前在奧斯汀、灣區、達拉斯、休士頓、邁阿密、奧蘭多與坦帕七個都會區營運，原訂上半年七城的名單裡，鳳凰城與拉斯維加斯還沒到位。Optimus 人形機器人原本規劃七月底或八月開始小量產，馬斯克先打了預防針，說單機約一萬個獨特零件、初期產速會極慢，而到七月中為止那條產線還沒開動。
光譜另一端則是 Wedbush 的 Dan Ives，他預期 Robotaxi 將擴張到 30 個以上城市，喊出特斯拉市值上看 2 兆至 3 兆美元，但這個目標明白掛著條件：Optimus 商業化必須在 2026 年底前落地。
今晚該盯的三個數字
今晚要驗證的其實是 2026 年全球大型科技公司砸下約 7,000 億至 7,250 億美元的 AI 資本支出，有沒有開始變成錢。Alphabet 的資本支出規模自 2023 年以來已經膨脹超過五倍。
- Alphabet 資本支出指引: 1,800 至 1,900 億美元的區間會不會再往上調，以及自由現金流的失血速度
- Google Cloud 增速: 市場預期年增約 65%，同時看 4,600 億美元積壓訂單的入帳節奏
- 特斯拉汽車毛利率: 不含碳權能否守住 18%，以及 Robotaxi 與 Optimus 的具體時間表
值得注意的是，市場的耐心正在被重新定價。花旗上週才喊出「美股七巨頭已死」，主張改押注橫跨六大產業的成長型公司，理由是當所有巨頭都在同條賽道上砸同樣的錢，超額報酬還存不存在？
常見問題
Alphabet 和特斯拉 2026 年第二季財報什麼時候公布？
兩家都在美東時間 7 月 22 日美股盤後公布，也就是臺灣時間 7 月 23 日凌晨，Intel 則排在 7 月 23 日盤後。選擇權市場對 Alphabet 押 5.4% 波動、特斯拉 5.91%、Intel 高達 12%。
為什麼這兩份財報被視為 AI 資本支出的壓力測試？
Alphabet 今年資本支出上看 1,900 億美元，但第一季自由現金流年減 47% 只剩 101 億美元。市場要確認這筆錢有沒有轉成 Google Cloud 與 Gemini 的實際營收，而不只是折舊費用。

title: Bitget 上線業界首個 TradFi Quanto 永續合約，首期標的 MINIMAX 支援最高 20 倍槓桿
summary:
Bitget 推出業界首個 TradFi Quanto 永續合約，首期標的 MINIMAXHKDUSDT 支援 […]

〈Bitget 上線業界首個 TradFi Quanto 永續合約，首期標的 MINIMAX 支援最高 20 倍槓桿〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Bitget 推出業界首個 TradFi Quanto 永續合約，首期標的 MINIMAXHKDUSDT 支援最高 20 倍槓桿與全天候交易。該合約以港幣報價，但保證金與盈虧皆以 USDT 結算，無需換匯就能參與港股市場。此舉結合永續合約的靈活性與 Quanto 機制的匯率隔離優勢，降低跨市場交易成本。Bitget 在 TradFi 合約領域市占率已達 11.01%，排名第二，持續推動 UEX 架構連結加密與傳統金融。
（前情提要：Bitget TradFi 挑戰賽落幕｜實盤交易石油、白銀，顯現財富效應）
（背景補充：Bitget 上線業內首個跨資產統一帳戶，100 種美股代幣可作保證金）
（本文為廣編稿，由 Bitget 撰文、提供，不代表動區立場，亦非投資建議、購買或出售建議。詳見文末責任警示。）
Bitget，全球最大全景交易所（Universal Exchange，UEX）宣布正式上線 MINIMAX Quanto 永續合約 MINIMAXHKDUSDT，支援最高 20 倍槓桿與 24/7 全天候交易。作為業界首個 TradFi Quanto 永續合約，該產品讓用戶可直接使用 USDT 交易港股等非美元計價的海外股票相關資產，全程無須兌換外幣。
MINIMAXHKDUSDT 合約本身以港幣報價，但保證金存入與盈虧結算均以 USDT 完成。此設計可簡化跨市場交易流程，並有效降低外匯兌換與匯率波動帶來的額外風險，為加密貨幣用戶提供更便利的傳統金融市場參與方式。
TradFi 永續合約需求升溫，Bitget 市占率居業界第二
根據 TokenInsight 2026 年第二季報告，TradFi 永續合約已成為成長最快的交易賽道之一，月交易量從 1 月約 520 億美元，大幅成長至 6 月的 2,680 億美元，增幅達 5 倍。
在此背景下，Bitget 於 2026 年第二季的 TradFi 合約交易量約達 690 億美元，並以 11.01% 市占率位居業界第二，顯示用戶對加密原生平台上交易股票、指數與其他傳統金融資產相關合約的需求快速增加。
什麼是 Quanto 永續合約？
Quanto 永續合約是一種創新型衍生性商品，適合希望交易非美元計價資產的用戶，例如港股、日股或其他海外股票市場標的。
該產品結合兩大特色：
- 永續合約的交易彈性：無到期日，可依市場變化靈活調整部位
- Quanto 機制的匯率風險隔離：使用 USDT 作為保證金與盈虧結算資產，無須直接持有港幣、日圓等外幣
透過 Quanto 機制，用戶可在不進行外幣兌換的情況下，參與海外股票市場價格波動，降低換匯成本與匯率不確定性。
Bitget 持續推動 UEX，連結加密資產與傳統金融市場
MINIMAX Quanto 永續合約的推出，是 Bitget 推動 Universal Exchange（UEX） 架構的重要一步。透過將 TradFi 資產引入加密貨幣交易環境，Bitget 讓用戶能在同一平台中接觸更多元的資產類別，包括加密貨幣、代幣化股票、海外股票相關資產與衍生性商品。
隨著 TradFi 永續合約交易需求快速成長，Bitget 將持續拓展更多 Quanto 永續合約標的，進一步提升用戶跨市場交易彈性與資金使用效率。

title: 挺不過砸盤醜聞！Movement Labs 聲請破產保護，Layer 2 新星黯然退場
summary:
Movement 區塊鏈開發商 Movement Labs 已向美國法院聲請第 11 章破產保護。在短短不到一年的時間裡，這個新星項目歷經了造市商倒貨醜聞、共同創辦人出走，以及戰略轉型失敗的多重打擊。

〈挺不過砸盤醜聞！Movement Labs 聲請破產保護，Layer 2 新星黯然退場〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
曾被視為以太坊 Layer 2 新秀的 Movement，如今正式走向破產重整。 Movement 區塊鏈開發商 Movement Labs 已向美國法院聲請第 11 章破產保護。在短短不到一年的時間裡，這個新星項目歷經了造市商倒貨醜聞、共同創辦人出走，以及戰略轉型失敗的多重打擊。
根據法院文件，Movement Labs 已正式申請第 11 章破產保護，意味著公司將在法院監督下進行財務重整。這家在過去一年飽受高層內鬥、造市商砸盤爭議與轉型失敗折磨的加密貨幣項目，迎來了最新的重大挫敗。
文件顯示，Movement Labs 的債權人數量不到 1,000 名，目前帳上資產僅剩 10 萬至 50 萬美元，但負債卻超過 100 萬美元。
值得留意的是，Movement Labs 最大債權人正是今年 5 月才與公司分道揚鑣的共同創辦人 Rushi Manche，其他主要債權人還包含德拉瓦州稅務局與加密資產託管機構 Anchorage Digital 等實體。
從 Layer 2 新星到深陷危機
Movement 是建立在以太坊 Layer 2 上的區塊鏈，採用 Move 程式語言開發。 Move 最初由 Meta（前 Facebook）打造，Movement 則希望將 Move 智慧合約引入以太坊生態，同時透過 Layer 2 提供成本更低、速度更快的交易體驗。
然而，Movement 自 2024 年 12 月推出 MOVE 代幣後，就一路陷入爭議。
MOVE 上市隔日遭大量拋售
根據《CoinDesk》在今年 4 月的調查披露，Movement 高層當時正調查是否遭人設局誤導，簽下了一份將 MOVE 代幣流通供應量控制權，極度傾斜給單一交易對手的「造市商協議」。
外洩的內部文件證實，該合約允許造市商在代幣上市的第二天，就將高達 6,600 萬枚 MOVE 賣掉，成為引發幣價劇烈暴跌的元凶。
神秘中介公司成爭議焦點
整起事件的焦點，落在一家名為 Rentech 的中介公司。這家公司出現在與中國做市商 Web3Port 相關的合約中，但 CoinDesk 取得的文件顯示，Movement 高層事後才驚覺，基金會疑似誤認 Rentech 為 Web3Port 的附屬機構才簽署合約。
對此，Rentech 則全盤否認有任何不當行為或隱瞞欺騙。
幣安封鎖帳戶，Movement 啟動回購計畫
事件持續延燒後，影響也迅速擴大。全球最大加密貨幣交易所幣安（Binance）隨即以「涉及不當行為」為由，封鎖參與 MOVE 發行的相關做市帳戶。
另一方面，Movement 則宣布啟動 MOVE 代幣回購計畫，並委託外部調查公司 Groom Lake 針對該筆爭議交易展開調查，希望釐清事件責任。
在內外交迫下，Movement Labs 與共同創辦人 Rushi Manche 最終於去年 5 月正式分道揚鑣。
轉型跨境支付仍未挽回局勢
眼看 Layer2 業務陷入泥淖，團隊也曾試圖尋找新出路。
今年 6 月，與此次聲請破產的 MVMT Labs 屬不同法律主體的 Move Industries 宣布調整發展方向，不再專注於與其他以太坊 Layer 2 項目競爭，而是轉向跨境支付、國際匯款及穩定幣清算等金融應用。
公司表示，已取得美國、加拿大及歐盟的合規支付基礎設施，希望打造面向新興市場的支付服務。
Layer 2 競爭加劇，市場轉向實體金融應用
Movement 的轉型方向，也反映整個 Layer 2 市場的最新趨勢。
隨著 Layer 2 擴容方案競爭日益激烈，愈來愈多區塊鏈項目開始將重心轉向「實體資產（Real-World Finance）」應用，包括跨境支付、穩定幣結算、資產代幣化等領域，希望尋找比擴容更具商業價值的成長機會。
不過，對 Movement 而言，在代幣發行爭議、治理問題與市場信心受挫接連打擊下，這場策略轉型最終仍未能阻止公司走向破產重整。

title: 瞄準 10 億用戶大軍！Telegram  預告今夏推出非託管加密錢包
summary:
全球坐擁近 10 億用戶的通訊軟體巨頭 Telegram，準備在 Web3 領域投下震撼彈。創辦人暨執行長 Pavel Durov 周二宣布，Telegram 計劃在今年夏季向全體用戶正式推出非託管加密錢包。

〈瞄準 10 億用戶大軍！Telegram  預告今夏推出非託管加密錢包〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
全球坐擁近 10 億用戶的通訊軟體巨頭 Telegram，準備在 Web3 領域投下震撼彈。創辦人暨執行長 Pavel Durov 周二宣布，Telegram 計劃在今年夏季向全體用戶正式推出非託管加密錢包。
Pavel Durov 在自家平台 Telegram 上表示，這項戰略將是「人類史上規模最大的非託管加密錢包（指用戶完全自行掌控私鑰與資產，不假手第三方的數位錢包）推廣行動」。
這項旨在降低大眾接觸加密貨幣門檻的計畫，其實早有跡可循。就在上個月， Pavel Durov 才剛對外揭露，The Open Network（TON）區塊鏈的原生代幣 Toncoin 將更名為「GRAM」。
為了加速擴張加密貨幣版圖， Telegram 更直接取代了 TON 基金會，親自擔任該生態系的主要管理者與最大驗證節點。
儘管 Pavel Durov 在周二的貼文中並未透露太多細節，但他拋出了一個極具吸引力的亮點，預告新功能將實現「即時且零手續費的加密貨幣交易」。
事實上，Telegram 目前已經內建了名為「Wallet」的加密錢包，允許用戶儲存和交易和數位資產。今年初的官方數據顯示，這項服務已累積超過 1.5 億名註冊用戶。
考量到 Telegram 在全球加密貨幣投資人中擁有壓倒性的市佔率與極高的用戶黏著度，華爾街與幣圈長期以來皆將這款通訊平台，視為帶領傳統大眾市場（Mass market）跨入 Web3 領域的終極入口。
回顧過往，Telegram 的區塊鏈拓荒之路並非一帆風順。早在 2018 年，公司就首度啟動了 TON 專案，卻在隨後幾年捲入與美國證管會（SEC）的法律纏訟。當時 SEC 認定 GRAM 代幣發行違反了證券法，迫使 Telegram 全面暫停代幣銷售，甚至宣告放棄該項目。
如今歷經蟄伏後強勢回歸，不僅展現了 Telegram 深耕幣圈的決心，更企圖藉由龐大的社群基底，重新定義全球加密貨幣支付的版圖。

title: 「英國微策略」翻車！Satsuma 遭股東逼宮：被迫清倉 668 枚比特幣、宣告下市
summary:
英國上市公司 Satsuma Technology 周一宣布，股東以壓倒性票數推翻董事會多數反對意見，決議將清算公司持有的全部 668 枚比特幣，並撤銷倫敦證券交易所上市資格、終止公司營運，成為自「數位資產儲備（DAT）」風潮降溫以來，又一家宣告退場的企業。

〈「英國微策略」翻車！Satsuma 遭股東逼宮：被迫清倉 668 枚比特幣、宣告下市〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
華爾街早前掀起的「企業囤幣熱潮」，如今在英國踢到了大鐵板。英國上市公司 Satsuma Technology 周一宣布，股東以壓倒性票數推翻董事會多數反對意見，決議將清算公司持有的全部 668 枚比特幣，並撤銷倫敦證券交易所上市資格，成為自「數位資產儲備（DAT）」風潮降溫以來，又一家宣告退場的企業。
Satsuma 的前身是一家名為 TAO Alpha 的小型 AI 新創。 2025 年 8 月，公司大動作轉型，不僅更換招牌，更重金挖角擁有逾 70 萬 YouTube 訂閱數的美國知名比特幣評論家 Mark Moss 出任「首席比特幣策略長」，他向來以指導機構如何將比特幣作為企業儲備資產而聞名幣圈。
轉型當月，Satsuma 氣勢如虹，透過發行可轉債狂吸 1.636 億英鎊（約 2.18 億美元）。這輪融資由 ParaFi Capital 領投，Pantera Capital 、數位貨幣集團（DCG）及知名交易所 Kraken 皆共襄盛舉。其中，部分投資人更直接掏出 1,097 枚比特幣，取代了約 9,700 萬美元的現金出資。
2025 年 6 月，Satsuma 股價攀上每股 14 英鎊的巔峰，市值直逼 6,600 萬英鎊。隨後，比特幣在同年 10 月狂飆至 12.6 萬美元歷史天價。然而好景不常，隨之而來的是長達數月的暴跌，「加密寒冬」來襲不僅重創幣市，也將 Satsuma 的股價拖入深淵。
到了 12 月，Satsuma 的財務防線瀕臨破口，被迫變賣資產求生。公司拋售了 579 枚比特幣，套現 4,000 萬英鎊，只為了湊足現金，償還那些年底不願將債權轉換為股票的債券投資人。
高層爆離職潮，大股東鳴槍逼宮
2026 年初，Satsuma 公司高層爆發出走潮。財務長（CFO）於 2 月黯然離職，執行長（CEO）也隨即在 3 月請辭。到了 4 月，Satsuma 股價相較於 2025 年 6 月的高峰已狂瀉逾 99%，跌至不足一便士。
也就在此時，持股約 6.7% 的 Pantera Capital 開始公開要求公司全面清算比特幣，原因是 Satsuma 當時的市值已遠低於資產負債表上持有比特幣的價值，意味著投資人直接持有比特幣，反而比持有公司股票更具價值。於是，代表逾 20% 發行股本的股東陣線，正式將清算比特幣資產的決議放上談判桌。
這項提案讓董事會徹底撕裂。 6 名董事中，有 4 名堅決反對，主張 Satsuma 仍是市場上具備可行性的比特幣上市投資工具；僅有 2 名董事倒戈支持股東。最終，股東大軍以懸殊的票數差距，強勢推翻了多數董事的決議。
回收資金不到一半，普通股東恐拿回更少
Satsuma 將透過英國常見的 B Share Scheme（B 股分配機制），把出售資產所得返還股東。
扣除約 270 萬英鎊的法律費用、資遣費、下市成本及保險等終止支出後，公司預估可返還 2,680 萬至 3,000 萬英鎊；若加上去年 12 月出售比特幣取得的 4,000 萬英鎊，公司累計可回收資金約 6,600 萬至 7,000 萬英鎊。
然而，相較於當初募得的 1.636 億英鎊，實際回收金額不到一半。此外，由於可轉債持有人在清算時享有比普通股股東更高的受償順位，因此普通股股東最終實際可分配的金額，很可能還會低於上述數字。
截至目前，Satsuma 仍是英國上市企業中的第二大比特幣儲備公司，持有 668 枚比特幣。排名第一的是 The Smarter Web Company，目前持有 2,878 枚比特幣，公司尚未透露任何清算比特幣資產的計畫。
根據規劃，英國高等法院將於 2026 年 8 月與 9 月審理資本返還方案；公司預計 9 月中旬完成下市，股東款項則可望於 9 月底前完成發放。

title: PC Harper killers' potential early release is an 'insult', says his mother
summary: PC Harper, 28, sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Berkshire in 2019.
full_text:
PC Harper killers may be eligible for early release
- Published
The mother of police officer Andrew Harper has said it feels like an "insult" that two of her son's killers may be eligible for early release from prison.
PC Harper was 28 when he sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in August 2019.
He died after getting caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary.
Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and both 17 at the time, were handed 13 years in custody for manslaughter after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2020.
Both men might be eligible to be released from prison halfway through their sentences, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has confirmed.
Under the new Sentencing Act, due to come into force in September, some 6,000 criminals are set to be released under the early prison release scheme.
The government has so far failed to rule out whether killers, rapists and paedophiles will be exempt from the scheme.
The driver of the vehicle which caused PC Harper's death, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence, and will not be eligible for the scheme.
Speaking to The Telegraph, external, PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam said she had received a letter from the MoJ confirming their sentences might be reduced.
She said: "It makes me feel sick. Andrew's life doesn't get to come back. It feels like a slap in the face and an insult."
She added that "people are getting a free pass for crime" in the UK.
An MoJ spokesperson said: "This was a horrific crime, and our deepest sympathies are with PC Andrew Harper's family and friends.
"In 2024, the country was facing a prison crisis and a total breakdown of law and order, with judges ordered to stop jailing dangerous criminals.
"This government is committed to public safety: we are building prison places at the fastest rate since the Victorian era, and taking the difficult decisions needed to lock up the most dangerous offenders."
The government has insisted the Act will not see early releases for offenders deemed "the most dangerous", including those on extended determinate or life sentences.
The Police Federation of England & Wales responded to The Telegraph story on X, calling the early release policy "disgusting".
Deputy national chairman Brian Booth said: "Police officers from across the country stood side by side to honour Andrew Harper at his funeral.
"They and every serving officer will be utterly sickened at the prospect of Bowers and Cole being back on the streets so soon."
PC Harper, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, responded to the quad bike call just hours after he had been due to clock off and begin his honeymoon with wife Lissie Harper.
After her husband's death, she campaigned for legal changes to see harsher sentences for the manslaughter of emergency workers on duty.
Harper's Law was among the new measures in the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act, external.
The move extends mandatory life sentences to anyone who commits the manslaughter of an emergency worker on duty including police, prison officers, firefighters and paramedics.
It is not retrospective, meaning PC Harper's killers cannot have their sentences extended.
'Smirking lowlifes'
New Justice Secretary Alex Norris has been urged to reconsider the early release scheme after being appointed by Andy Burnham on Monday.
Asked about reports that the prime minister could be working on exempting rapists and child groomers from the scheme, his spokesman said: "The government's fully focused on keeping the public safe.
"We've got no option but to take decisive action to fix the crisis in our prisons. I'm not going to get into speculation over possible policy changes.
"Of course, the prime minister will take decisions on all manner of policy areas in the future, including how we get justice for victims."
Aileen O'Connor, chair of Thames Valley Police Federation, said: "The killers of PC Andrew Harper should be kept where they belong... behind bars.
"Police across Thames Valley, and indeed the country, will be disgusted at the prospect of these smirking lowlifes being free to roam the streets.
"These killers have never shown any remorse for their horrific and deadly actions that night.
"Andrew's wife Lissie and his whole family are serving a life sentence. The least we can expect is that his killers serve their whole sentence, however poor it already is."
She added that the organisation would be communicating with the police minister, the home secretary and the prime minister.
"We will not stop. Andrew deserves nothing less," O'Connor said.
"What message does this send about the worth of a life of a police officer? The government and the parole board must reconsider any plans to release Andrew's killers early. And they must do it now. No ifs. No buts."
Cabinet minister Heidi Alexander said the early release scheme was necessary because the justice system had been on the brink of collapse when Labour came to power.
She told BBC Breakfast: "If we ran out of prison spaces, courts couldn't sentence and the police wouldn't have been able to arrest.
"No responsible government would have allowed us to get into that situation."
Meanwhile, new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has insisted there was "no ill intent" behind apparent comments about the early release scheme, which were caught on camera.
He can be heard saying to Norris that "he wants to let them all out" - appearing to reference the government's plans for the early release of prisoners.

title: Ukrainian drones hit more sites of Russian online retailer Wildberries
summary: Logistics hubs belonging to Wildberries in the Krasnodar and Stavropol regions were struck overnight.
full_text:
Ukrainian drones hit more sites of Russian online retailer Wildberries
- Published
Ukrainian drones have hit warehouses belonging to Russia's biggest online retailer again, injuring 15 people, according to the company's founder and regional governors.
Logistics hubs run by Wildberries in two south-west cities were impacted by overnight attacks and workers were evacuated, the founder said.
It is the second time Ukraine has attacked the firm's facilities in four days, with warehouses in Tambov and Elektrostal hit on Saturday, killing eight people.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday that Ukraine had hit logistics hubs in the Krasnodar and Stavropol regions "involved in providing the Russian army with drone components, navigation equipment and other gear".
Wildberries founder Tatyana Kim confirmed the attacks on two logistics centres in Krasnodar and Nevinnomyssk in the Stavropol region.
"There are no words to describe all the feelings and emotions caused by the attacks on ordinary people, on our employees, on us, who are simply doing our jobs," she wrote on Telegram. "But these situations demonstrate the most important thing: we must continue to do what we do for the benefit of people."
Five people were hurt in a warehouse complex on the outskirts of Nevinnomyssk, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov said, with everyone receiving outpatient treatment.
In Krasnodar, ten people were injured in an attack on a warehouse complex, with three in a serious condition, the region's governor Veniamin Kondratyev said.
Footage of both warehouses, verified by BBC Verify, shows fires in the aftermath of the attacks.
Video from Krasnodar captures an enormous column of black smoke rising from the structure as flames leap upwards. Nevinnomyssk footage shows people milling around outside as fireballs erupt in smoke streaming from the building.
Krasnodar's governor said the region was hit by a "massive attack last night", with drone debris also hitting the grounds of a company in Armavir and killing one employee. The city administration reported that an oil depot was struck, causing a fire.
Drone fragments also hit two apartment buildings in Krasnodar and two homes in the village of Dinskaya, Kondratyev said. There were no injuries.
Zelensky said Ukraine had struck an oil depot, as well as a tanker and four cargo ships of the Russian shadow fleet in the waters of the Sea of Azov and Black Sea.
Russia has been operating a "shadow fleet" to evade international sanctions imposed on its oil exports after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The overnight strikes mark the second targeting of Wildberries' facilities in less than a week.
Serhii Kuzan, chairman of the Ukrainian Security and Cooperation Centre, has previously told BBC that Wildberries' website had been used by Russian volunteers to buy military equipment.
"The primary rationale for striking Wildberries' warehouses is to disrupt Russian logistics and the supply of dual-use goods, critical electronics, sanctioned goods and the like to the Russian army and Russian arms manufacturers," he said.
"The collateral damage from such strikes could also have a serious impact on the Russian economy, as well as a psychological effect on Russian society and, likely, on continued support for the war."
Additional reporting by Vitaly Shevchenko

title: Prince George poses in suit for new photo as he becomes a teenager
summary: It's a big year for the young prince, who will start secondary school at the elite Eton College in September.
full_text:
Prince George poses in suit for new photo as he becomes a teenager
- Published
A new photograph of Prince George has been issued by Kensington Palace to mark his 13th birthday.
The photo, showing a relaxed George standing with his hands in his pockets and wearing an open-necked white shirt and dark suit, was published on social media with a message which read "Happy 13th birthday, George!" alongside a party popper emoji.
The picture was taken at Kensington Palace last month straight after the Trooping the Colour ceremony, by photographer Matt Porteous.
George, the elder son of the Prince and Princess of Wales, is second in line to the throne.
It is a big year for Prince George, who as well as entering his teens, will also start secondary school in September.
The prince will follow in his father Prince William's footsteps and go to Eton College, an elite private school where entry usually begins at the age of 13.
Prince George's uncle, Prince Harry, and great uncle, Earl Spencer, also attended the elite boarding school for boys.
George will now become a boarder, at one of the Eton's 25 boarding houses. Each house have approximately 55 pupils, looked after by residential staff headed by a house master.
He previously studied at Lambrook School in Berkshire, alongside his sister Charlotte and brother Louis.
The young prince has been gradually introduced to a public role, including going with Prince William to help at a charity for the homeless at Christmas.
In June, he joined King Charles and other senior royals for the Trooping the Colour parade in London, to mark the sovereign's official birthday.
Earlier this month, he was seen with his parents at this year's Wimbledon tennis championships.

title: Military kit still failing women, troops say
summary: Servicewomen still face shortages of properly fitting kit, five years after a landmark report.
full_text:
Military kit still failing women, troops say
- Published
Women in the armed forces say they are still being issued kit that does not fit properly, five years after a landmark report warned they were at "greater risk of harm" from ill-fitting uniform and equipment.
The 2021 Atherton report said the Ministry of Defence should urgently roll out safer, more appropriate kit for female service personnel by the end of 2022.
Despite improvements, women have been telling the BBC some kit is still poorly fitting, with body armour failing to account for breasts, and shortages of smaller sizes resulting in "competition" among troops.
The Ministry of Defence (MOD) said it ensured everyone had access to the "best equipment they need to protect themselves in combat".
"I never felt that I was neat, tidy, presentable, or in the uniform that I was meant to be in," explains veteran Rhian Brown, who left the service in 2024.
"I never really felt that it protected me or entirely fulfilled the purpose that it was meant to."
Following the report by Dame Sarah Atherton, external, the Ministry of Defence brought out a new version of its latest body armour adapted for female troops in 2022.
It said it offered improved "fit, comfort and mobility while maintaining consistent ballistic protection standards".
Called the Virtus Scalable Tactical Vest, the body armour system has adjustable straps and smaller flat plates.
Brown, 26, who left the Army Reserve after seven years as an infantry platoon commander, wore it in training and on deployments.
She says the newer version was an improvement, feeling "tight and secure" and looking smarter, "but, ultimately, it still wasn't designed to fit me".
"Women are not flat, we have breasts and curves," Brown continues.
"The plates are flat, it doesn't fit, it is not flexible - fit isn't about vanity, it's about safety."
Brown, from Plymouth, said on one occasion the person issuing body armour told her "you're probably a small... but we don't have any smalls so here, take this medium".
It comes as the MoD paid for the supply of 2,000 sets of new curved body armour plates for women in the Ukrainian armed forces.
The UK government said it spent £4.5bn on military support to Ukraine last year.
It is understood the contract with NP Aerospace, based in Coventry, was in response to a specific operational need and sat outside the UK's wider equipment programmes, which go through their own testing and approval processes.
Seren White, who worked on the design of the new curved armour, said the plates had "been tested with the highest level of rigor".
For industry certification, she explained the plates needed to be tested 36 times - but the new curved plates have been shot almost 300 times.
Engineers said they were able to debunk some "myths", including that bullets can ricochet off the curve in the ballistic plate.
"Women today are wearing flat plates that have been designed for male torsos," explains Erin Grieve, from NP Aerospace.
"We are trying to address that women are not small men - they're shaped differently."
Grieve said the firm's own research concluded the curved plates provided women with more protection when compared with flat plates.
As it stands, this kit is not available for UK servicewomen.
The BBC spoke to a number of servicewomen who asked to remain anonymous.
One described her body armour as "definitely not female and definitely not good".
Another said there was "none or barely any" female-specific kit available to her and that the body armour did not account for "busty women".
Issues around kit and clothing have persisted.
Ofsted, which inspects MoD training establishment as well as schools, said in October 2025 that for the "fourth consecutive year" women and smaller recruits were being issued with ill-fitting kit and clothing, external.
Its report said: "This renders them at a disadvantage because they often do not appear as well turned out as their peers, or because ill-fitting equipment, such as webbing or rucksacks, prevents them from participating fully in training."
It added "ill-fitting kit poses a very serious risk" in combat situations.
Dr Mary Keeling, from the Centre for Evidence for the Armed Forces, said she was aware a rollout of new female kit and equipment, as well as availability, had been "inconsistent" since Atherton's report.
She said there had been "good steps in the right direction" but progress had been slow, adding faster changes were needed as the MoD aimed to increase the number of women joining the forces.
Keeling said it was likely improve challenges in recruitment "if women feel welcome by making sure that appropriate kit and equipment are available".
After the Atherton Inquiry, RAF veteran Stacey Denyer, who left the service in 2023, was one of a number of servicewomen who joined a ministerial roundtable to discuss putting its recommendations into practice.
"In the latter part of my career, they started doing women's fitting boots. It was amazing," she explains.
"We're not whinging for the sake of whinging - we're making noise because it is a massive safety issue."
Denyer, who is from Taunton in Somerset, added: "It absolutely needs to happen quickly and there is an aspiration for the armed forces to be 30% female by 2030.
"And, if they want to attract women, they need to start looking after them properly, and that starts with kit."
Fred Thomas, MP for Plymouth Moor View and a former Royal Marine officer, said it should be "an absolute priority" for the MoD to get body armour that fitted women at a time of heightened global instability.
Thomas was part of a Defence Select Committee hearing that reviewed the Atherton report in April, almost five years on from its publication.
He said he was aware of slow progress around improved kit but the services were "doing their best".
He added it was "unacceptable for some people to be better protected than others".
The MoD said new ballistic plates would be delivered in 2028 and would "be available in multiple sizes offering a better fit for all service personnel".
The BBC understands these plates will be flat and not curved.
The MoD added: "We are also developing the next generation of body armour through our Complex Geometry Body Armour Programme, which will enable the procurement of curved body armour plates."
It is understood these could begin to be delivered from 2029.

title: Nottingham attacks NHS trust faces manslaughter probe
summary: The hospital trust treated Valdo Calocane before he killed three people in the city in 2023.
full_text:
Nottingham attacks NHS trust faces manslaughter probe
- Published
The NHS trust that treated Nottingham attacks killer Valdo Calocane is being investigated for corporate manslaughter.
Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia before he fatally attacked Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates in June 2023, was previously sectioned by Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust.
A public inquiry, which finished hearing evidence in May, was told he had been discharged in 2022 because he failed to turn up for appointments and the team had "lost" him.
The investigation into the trust is being carried out by Northumbria Police.
Nottinghamshire Police has been criticised over its history of interactions with Calocane and its handling of the response and investigation into the attacks.
A spokesperson for Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust said: "Northumbria Police, acting on behalf of Nottinghamshire Police, have begun an investigation into matters relating to the care and treatment of Valdo Calocane.
"We know how important the independent inquiry and police investigation are for the affected families, the survivors and our local communities.
"We will, of course, be co-operating fully with Northumbria Police, as we have with the Statutory Inquiry into these matters which is being chaired by Her Honour Deborah Taylor, and which will hear final submissions from all the parties involved later this year."
Nottinghamshire Healthcare was responsible for Calocane's care for two years before he was discharged in September 2022.
He was sectioned under the Mental Health Act four times during that two-year period and warned by a doctor he would end up killing somebody.
Following the attacks, he pleaded guilty to three counts of manslaughter, on the grounds of diminished responsibility, and to three counts of attempted murder.
Calocane is currently serving an indefinite hospital order in a high-security facility.
The Nottingham Inquiry, which heard evidence from doctors, nurses and other NHS staff, was told there had been numerous errors in Calocane's care and management.
He had a history of non-compliance with his medication and was known to become violent when he was unwell, it heard.
One of the key themes in the evidence about the killer's care under the Nottinghamshire trust was that his risk to others was not properly assessed or managed.
The trust had already been under the close scrutiny of the health and social care watchdog, the Care Quality Commission (CQC) before Calocane was under its care.
In October 2021, an email to staff said the trust had reached a point where services were "not safe", with concerns raised about staffing levels.
By then, Calocane had been sectioned three times.

title: Godzilla vs Kong actress Kaylee Hottle dies in crash at 18
summary: She portrayed a young deaf orphan named Jia in the 2021 blockbuster and its 2024 sequel.
full_text:
Godzilla vs Kong actress Kaylee Hottle dies in crash at 18
- Published
US actress Kaylee Hottle, who starred in the Godzilla vs Kong movie series, has died in a car crash at age 18.
Hottle, who was deaf, portrayed a young orphan named Jia in the 2021 blockbuster, and reprised the role in 2024 sequel Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire.
Her father, Joshua Hottle, posted a video statement via Facebook, using American Sign Language to confirm details of her death.
Police officers in Frederick, Maryland, said "excessive speed" was believed to be a factor in the single-vehicle crash on Tuesday morning.
The Texas School for the Deaf, where Hottle had studied, also shared the news with "profound sadness".
"Our hearts are with Kaylee's family, friends, classmates, and everyone who knew and loved her during this incredibly difficult time," said a statement posted on Instagram, external.
It also called for everyone to respect the privacy of her family and to not speculate about the crash.
Warner Bros, which distributed the popular monster films, paid tribute to the actress alongside a photo of her in a post on X. , external
Frederick County Sheriff's Office said deputies were called to the scene of the crash in Ijamsville at about 02:50 local time.
Police said a 19-year-old driver was taken to hospital to be treated for "non life-threatening" injuries, while a second passenger declined help at the scene.
Hottle appeared in Godzilla vs Kong alongside Hollywood stars including Alexander Skarsgard, Millie Bobby Brown and Rebecca Hall.
Her role in the 2024 sequel earned her a Saturn Award nomination for best younger performer in a film.

title: 'We just need a bed': Baby with 'days to live' can't access lifesaving treatment
summary: Dylan and Catrin Green fear baby Macs has days to live and say he urgently needs a Berlin heart.
full_text:
'We just need a bed' - Baby with 'days to live' can't access lifesaving treatment
- Published
The parents of a three-month-old boy who they fear has just days to live say they're frustrated at being unable to access lifesaving treatment due to a lack of suitable hospital beds.
Dylan and Catrin Green, from Cardiff, said their "completely healthy baby" Macs started to struggle with his feeding, then caught a cold before later suffering two cardiac arrests.
He has been diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy, external - a condition which can lead to heart failure - and now has a "matter of days" on a machine which pumps his heart for him, Dylan said.
He urgently needs a Berlin heart , external- a device used to take over the function of a child's own heart until a donor heart becomes available.
His family said Macs has been stuck at a specialist unit in Bristol for weeks, where his condition has since deteriorated and was now in an induced coma, as the beds he needs were not available.
The two specialist hospitals in the UK where the Berlin heart can be fitted are Great Ormond Street Hospital in London and the Freeman Hospital in Newcastle.
"Seeing him in hospital is so difficult for us," Catrin told BBC-produced Newyddion S4C, external.
"It's really frustrating knowing there is a treatment available which could save his life."
She continued: "He could lead a full life with the Berlin heart. Although he would have to remain in hospital for an extended period, he would be able to learn to crawl... to walk.
"It would be really nice to reach that stage."
She said they were "desperate for the hospitals to find a bed for him".
"The clock is ticking for him, we just need a bed."
Figures from NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) suggest fewer than five patients in Wales and England were currently using a Berlin heart - a device which can be used for several months prior to a transplant.
With only 2% of deceased organ donors in the UK being under 18, Macs' family was also eager to raise awareness about the importance of organ donation.
"It's not a nice subject to be discussing, but the more people who donate organs, they can help children like Macs lead a full and happy life," said Dylan.
The NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee (NWJCC) said it recognised the "difficult and stressful time this must be for Macs' parents, family and friends".
It said, while funding was available for patients who required highly specialised services, capacity was managed on a UK-wide basis, and access to treatment was determined through clinical assessment.
"We understand that the specialist teams involved in Macs' case remain focused on supporting him to ensure he receives the care and treatment he needs."

summary: These are the stars to look out for across the 10 sports at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
full_text:
Five big names to look out for at Glasgow 2026
- Published
With 215 golds up for grabs at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, highlighting just five medal hopefuls is no easy feat.
Scotland's largest city is set to welcome more than 3,000 athletes from 10 sports, all of whom have the ambition of leaving with a slab of metal resting on their chest.
For some, a podium-finish is paramount. The bare minimum. For others, competing at the Games is a win in itself.
Much has been made of the reduced programme, the city's readiness and the 'what next?' once Glasgow has passed on the hosting baton again, but for now, the attention - finally - is fully on the athletes.
Here, BBC Scotland highlights some of the biggest names set to compete in the upcoming Commonwealth Games.
