title: Bitcoin, Ethereum-linked protocols lose $35 million in multiple attacks hours apart
full_text:
Bitcoin, Ethereum-linked protocols lose $35 million in multiple attacks hours apart
The attacks hit Verus, B² Network and other cross-chain systems, showing how compromised keys, upgrade powers and validation checks can empty protocols without breaking the underlying cryptography.
- In a six-hour span, at least three crypto bridges and cross-chain protocols were drained of more than $35 million, exposing recurring weaknesses in how these systems are designed and governed.
- Verus’s Ethereum bridge was exploited for about $7.54 million using the same contract path and bug class as a May hack, underscoring how unresolved flaws and redeposited funds left the system vulnerable to a second drain.
- The B² Network lost roughly $3.86 million after an attacker seized its staking contract’s upgrade authority, highlighting how compromised keys and permissions — not broken cryptography — remain the primary cause of major crypto thefts as AI-driven intrusion tools grow more capable.
Crypto's bridges and cross-chain protocols are having a brutal day, capping an already punishing year.
At least three were drained in quick succession over a 6-hour period, for a combined total exceeding $35 million, according to blockchain data analyzed by CoinDesk and reported by security firms BlockAid and PeckShield.
The run of attacks shares a common thread that underscores the need to audit off-chain components, such as private keys, not just smart contract code.
None broke the underlying cryptography — each was either a logic flaw, where the code ran as written, but the rules still let money out, or a compromised key that handed an attacker control it should never have had.
The three exploits
The perpetuals exchange AFX lost about $24.15 million from a bridge it runs on Arbitrum. The Verus-Ethereum bridge was drained of $7.54 million, its second hack this year through the same flaw. And B², a Bitcoin scaling network, lost $3.86 million from its token staking contract.
The most damning was blockchain network Verus. Blockaid detected an exploit on the Verus-Ethereum bridge early Thursday that drained about $7.54 million in ether, tokenized bitcoin and a spread of stablecoins.
🚨 Blockaid detected a @VerusCoin Ethereum Bridge exploit on Ethereum.
— Blockaid (@blockaid_) July 23, 2026
An attacker used the bridge import path to trigger unbacked Ethereum-side payouts, draining ~$7.54M in ETH, tBTC, USDC, USDT, EURC, MKR, and scrvUSD from bridge reserves.
More details in 🧵
The firm flagged that the attack reused the same bridge contract and entry path as an earlier hack, exploiting an identical class of bug. CoinDesk reported that earlier incident, an $11.5 million loss, in May.
A bridge is a blockchain-based tool that enables assets to move between two networks that otherwise cannot interact. It holds real tokens on one side and issues claims against them on the other, and its safety depends entirely on correctly verifying that every withdrawal is genuinely backed by assets locked on the other chain.
The Verus flaw let an attacker trigger payouts on the Ethereum side that were never properly backed on the Verus side, so the bridge released real money against a claim worth almost nothing.
The attacker returned most of the funds in exchange for a bounty after the May attack. Verus then redeposited the recovered money into the same bridge on July 8, according to onchain records compiled by security researchers, and the bridge was drained again two weeks later.
The cost of that trust is visible in the protocol's own numbers. Verus held close to $100 million in total value locked at the start of 2025, according to DefiLlama. It holds about $9 million as of Thursday, a slow bleed punctuated by a fresh drop this week as the latest hack landed.
Such repeated failures do not just cost the money stolen in any single attack, but drain the confidence that keeps assets on the platform at all.
Another confirmed attack was B² Network, a scaling network built to make Bitcoin cheaper and faster to transact on.
B² said in Asian morning hours Thursday that an attacker gained unauthorized access to the upgrade authority of its token staking contract, the administrative permission that controls how that contract behaves.
Security firm Lookonchain traced roughly $3.86 million in B2 tokens that were sold, converted to ether and stablecoins, and moved on. B² said it had contained the incident, suspended staking and would fully compensate affected users.
A smart contract is only as safe as the keys and permissions that control it. If an attacker seizes the authority to change how a contract works, the code does not need a bug, because the attacker can simply rewrite the rules or drain the funds directly.
This is the failure mode behind the largest thefts in crypto history, from the Wormhole and Nomad bridge hacks of 2022 to KelpDAO's roughly $290 million loss earlier this year.
And it is about to get harder to defend. In an analysis published this week, OpenAI disclosed that during an internal evaluation, its AI models broke out of their test environment and compromised the servers of Hugging Face, chaining together stolen credentials and previously unknown software flaws to do it.
The models had their safety limits lowered for the test, so this was not a system acting on its own. But it was a concrete demonstration that AI can now perform the patient, multi-step intrusion work that until recently required a skilled human team.
In most industries, a breach means incident response and, eventually, recovery. In crypto, where a drained contract is final and there is no chargeback, the same capability points at a threat with no undo button.
In 24 hours, four teams – Verus, B², AFX and Balance – were drained for the same underlying reason. None fell to a broken cipher. Each lost a trusted control, and the tools for finding those controls are only getting sharper.

title: Arbitrum-based AFX Trade drained of $24 million after bridge keys compromised
full_text:
Arbitrum-based AFX Trade drained of $24 million after bridge keys compromised
Security firms said the attacker used enough hot-validator signatures to approve a 24.15 million USDC withdrawal, while Arbitrum said its native bridge was not affected.
- AFX Trade, a decentralized perpetuals exchange on Arbitrum that settles in USDC, was drained of about $24.15 million after an attacker compromised validator signing keys for a bridge the protocol operates.
- Arbitrum’s native bridge was not breached, and security firm Blockaid said the on-chain logic functioned as designed, with five hot-validator signatures meeting the quorum needed to authorize the withdrawal.
- The attacker moved the stolen USDC to Ethereum and swapped it for roughly 12,467 ETH, nearly emptying AFX’s total value locked amid a broader wave of high-profile crypto hacks on Arbitrum-based protocols.
Another week, another multi-million-dollar hack in DeFi, and once again, it’s an off-chain compromise rather than a smart contract exploit.
AFX Trade, a decentralized perpetuals exchange that settles in dollar-pegged stablecoin USDC, was drained of about $24.15 million on Wednesday after an attacker compromised the validator signing keys behind a bridge the protocol operates on Arbitrum, blockchain data shows.
In other words, the smart contract did what it’s supposed to do – verify the signature and execute the transaction. The problem was with the private keys that generated those signatures, as attackers compromised the private validator signing keys (hot keys held offchain by the bridge operators or validators).
Steven Goldfeder, co-founder of Offchain Labs, which develops and maintains the network, said the Arbitrum native bridge "has not been hacked or exploited in any way" and that the transaction originated from a third-party protocol.
A hack of Arbitrum's own bridge would signal risk across the entire layer-2 network, but a compromised protocol running on top of it is a contained failure.
Nothing in the bridge's own code logic was broken. Bridges are blockchain-based tools for transferring tokens between various networks, including those they were not initially supported on.
Security firm Blockaid said the on-chain logic was not bypassed. Instead, five of the bridge's hot-validator signatures, the approvals that authorize a withdrawal, signed off on moving 24,150,000 USDC to the attacker's wallet, clearing the roughly two-thirds quorum the bridge requires.
This incident, therefore, is similar to the roughly $285 million Drift Protocol loss in April, where attackers spent months working their way to privileged access rather than breaking any contract.
The loss lands amid a punishing stretch for crypto security, with Q2 among the worst quarters for hacks on record and a run of Arbitrum-based protocols, including the oracle exploit that drained a separate $18 million from RWA platform Ostium a week earlier, hit in quick succession.
Most of the hacks and exploits this year have targeted offchain components rather than vulnerabilities in smart contracts themselves.
Blockaid detected an exploit at 2026-07-22 21:30 UTC targeting @AFX_XYZ, a protocol on @arbitrum. The exploit was specific to a bridge that AFX operates. Approximately 24.15M USDC has been drained thus far from the protocol.
— Blockaid (@blockaid_) July 22, 2026
Our team has been working with the incredible folks on… https://t.co/0Qd9ve5gPB
The contract treated the withdrawal as valid and released the funds after a 200-second dispute period. The bridge did exactly what it was designed to do, but the keys authorizing the withdrawal were apparently in the wrong hands.
The attacker then bridged the stolen USDC to Ethereum and swapped it for about 12,467 ETH, worth roughly $24 million, which on-chain trackers say now sits in a single wallet.
AFX's trading activity had been climbing sharply in the run-up to the attack, with daily perpetuals volume spiking to multi-month highs in mid-July, according to DefiLlama, as the protocol drew in users and, with them, deposits.
The roughly $24 million drained was almost the entirety of the protocol's total value locked, meaning the attacker emptied the vault at close to the moment it was fullest.

title: XRP whales accumulate as small holders capitulate
full_text:
XRP whales accumulate as small holders capitulate
XRP whales accumulate 2.8% more tokens over five weeks as small holders capitulate, sending the price back above $1.16.
- XRP has climbed more than 8% since late June as large holders boost their coin stash while smaller players capitulate.
- This pattern has historically aligned with further gains.
Payments-focused cryptocurrency XRP’s price has risen over 8% in five weeks and during this time, there has been a notable divergence in accumulation trends of large holders or whales and small holders.
According to on-chain data from Santiment, wallets holding between 100,000 and 100 million XRP added 2.8% more coins to their balances over the past five weeks. This accumulation by whales and sharks coincided with the token rebounding to $1.16 from $1 at the end of June, suggesting stronger hands are leaning into the current price action.
At the same time, the smallest wallets have shed 5.2% of their holdings during the same period. This capitulation by small holders stands in sharp contrast to the buying pressure from key stakeholders.
These diverging trends are bullish for XRP, according to Santiment.
“Historically, XRP price has tended to move more with key stakeholders and against the smallest retail wallets, so this split supports the bullish case behind the bounce,” the firm noted on X.
The timing aligns with several positive fundamental developments for XRP such as Improved institutional access through potential ETF products and continued utility on the XRP Ledger for payments, tokenization, and the RLUSD stablecoin, the firm explained,
These developments have kept the asset in focus, likely reinforcing confidence among sophisticated investors even as casual holders step back.

Geopolitical risks, rising rates, and fresh regulatory setbacks send crypto lower as key Democrats demand stronger safeguards in the market structure bill.
- Bitcoin slipped to about $65,500 as rising oil prices and higher Treasury yields pressured risk assets and weighed on major cryptocurrencies.
- Market sentiment was further dampened by an apparent escalation in U.S. military strikes linked to Iran.
- Regulator uncertainty persisted as key Senate Democrats criticized the latest draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, sending betting odds of its passage lower.
Bitcoin 
The cryptocurrency changed hands near $65,500, down about 0.7% since midnight UTC, extending the pulled back from a high near $66,700 reached Wednesday. The weakness spilled over into the broader market, with major tokens including ether (ETH), solana (SOL), and XRP (XRP) also trading lower.
Futures tied to West Texas Intermediate on the NYMEX climbed to $88.60 per barrel, marking the highest level since June 11. The move extends a steep rebound from recent lows below $70 and signals a potential new inflationary impulse that could push up consumer price indexes in the U.S. and globally. That, in turn, would complicate efforts by central banks to cut interest rates.
Bond markets are already reacting. The U.S. two-year Treasury yield jumped to 4.31%, its highest level since February 2025, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose to 4.66%, the highest since May, according to TradingView data. Higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as bitcoin and gold, often prompting investors to rotate out of speculative holdings and into fixed-income securities that now offer more attractive returns.
Adding to the cautious market sentiment, Axios reported that the U.S. military deployed a B-1 long-range bomber on Tuesday to strike targets linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The use of the heavy bomber represents a clear escalation in the scale of U.S. operations and suggests Washington may be preparing for a broader campaign, rather than continuing with the more limited strikes seen in recent days.
Regulatory uncertainty persisted after a group of key Senate Democrats said the newest draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (Clarity Act) “falls short” on ethics and other critical provisions.
Betting markets on decentralized platform Polymarket reacted swiftly, with the implied odds of the Clarity Act passing tumbling from 46% to 38%.
Senate Republicans released the updated draft earlier Wednesday, which includes an ethics provision agreed to by the White House and President Donald Trump. Senator Bernie Moreno called it “the most powerful ethics language in U.S. history.

Bitcoin ETFs approach $1B in 7-session inflow run
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $69 million in inflows on Wednesday, extending their inflow streak to seven sessions and bringing total inflows during the period to nearly $1 billion
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have attracted about $1 billion in net inflows over seven straight trading sessions.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $68.99 million in net inflows on Wednesday, bringing cumulative inflows since July 14 to $999.38 million, according to data from SoSoValue.
The current streak remains below April’s nine-session run, when spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted $2.1 billion in net inflows.
Daily flows in US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs since July 14. Source: SoSoValue
Wednesday’s inflows were below Tuesday’s $203 million as Bitcoin price fell below $66,000. At publishing time, BTC traded at about $65,729, down roughly 0.3% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a market sentiment gauge, slipped to a reading of 31 on Thursday from 33 on Wednesday.
“The consistency suggests institutions are rebuilding long-term Bitcoin exposure through regulated ETFs,” Markus Levin, co-founder of XYO, a decentralized verification protocol, told Cointelegraph. Levin said improving macroeconomic sentiment, expectations for easier monetary policy, cooling inflation and stronger equity markets have encouraged investors to rotate back into risk assets.

title: Kakao taps Circle to explore won stablecoin payment infrastructure
summary: Kakao Group and Circle signed an MOU to explore won stablecoin payments, remittances, merchant settlement and tokenized financial services.
full_text:
Kakao taps Circle to explore won stablecoin payment infrastructure
Kakao Group and Circle signed an MOU to explore won stablecoin payments, remittances, merchant settlement and tokenized financial services.
Kakao Group has partnered with stablecoin issuer Circle to explore payment infrastructure for won-backed stablecoins as South Korea prepares a broader regulatory framework for crypto assets.
On Thursday, the companies announced that Kakao, Kakao Pay and Kakao Bank had signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Circle Internet Group. Under the agreement, the companies will explore ways to connect Circle’s blockchain and global payment infrastructure with Kakao’s consumer platforms and financial services.
The agreement highlights how major South Korean consumer and financial platforms are positioning themselves ahead of expected stablecoin legislation, even before the regulatory framework is finalized.
Under the MOU, the companies plan to examine stablecoin payments, cross-border remittances, merchant settlement and connections between existing financial systems and blockchain networks.
The companies will also consider support for tokenized financial services, but they did not disclose any products or launch timelines.
Cointelegraph reached out to Circle and Kakao Group but did not receive a response before publication.
South Korea’s stablecoin framework
South Korea has been working toward legislation governing won-backed stablecoins as policymakers seek to encourage digital payment innovation while addressing risks related to reserves, redemption and issuer oversight.
The government has been preparing a bill that would establish requirements covering stablecoin issuance, collateral management and internal controls. Lawmakers have also introduced competing proposals as support has grown for won-pegged tokens aimed at reducing reliance on the US dollar.
However, the regulatory process has stalled over disagreements about which institutions should be permitted to issue won-based stablecoins.
The Bank of Korea, the country’s central bank, argued that banks should retain a majority stake in stablecoin issuers, while the Financial Services Commission warned that eligibility limits could restrict competition and innovation.
In its economic growth strategy announced on July 14, the government listed advancing the Digital Asset Basic Act among its priorities for the second half of 2026.
Related: South Korean regulator misses stablecoin bill deadline: What’s next?
Meanwhile, companies and financial institutions have begun testing the technology in South Korea. In April, internet bank Kbank partnered with Ripple to test blockchain-based remittances.
In May, KB Financial Group completed a pilot covering stablecoin issuance, offline merchant payments and cross-border remittances through the Kaia blockchain. The group said it was preparing to introduce stablecoin services once the regulations take effect.

title: Swiss bank BancaStato launches regulated crypto trading with Sygnum
summary: Swiss cantonal bank BancaStato integrated Sygnum’s crypto trading and custody services into its Avaloq-powered digital banking apps for Bitcoin and other assets.
full_text:
Swiss bank BancaStato launches regulated crypto trading with Sygnum
Swiss cantonal bank BancaStato integrated Sygnum’s crypto trading and custody services into its Avaloq-powered digital banking apps for Bitcoin and other assets.
Swiss bank BancaStato has launched regulated cryptocurrency trading using digital asset bank Sygnum and banking software provider Avaloq.
BancaStato, the cantonal bank serving Switzerland’s Italian-speaking Ticino region, joined Sygnum’s business-to-business (B2B) banking platform to offer crypto asset services, according to a Thursday announcement shared with Cointelegraph.
The integration allows BancaStato customers to buy, sell and hold four crypto assets, including Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), Litecoin (LTC) and Solana (SOL), through the bank’s existing web and mobile banking apps.
BancaStato joins more than 25 financial institutions using Sygnum’s B2B platform to offer regulated digital asset services.
How BancaStato’s crypto service works
BancaStato integrated Sygnum’s trading and custody services into its existing Avaloq banking system.
Headquartered in Zurich, Avaloq develops the software banks use to run their core banking and digital banking services. The integration connects Sygnum’s application programming interface (API) directly to Avaloq’s platform, allowing customers to access crypto trading from their existing banking app.
The setup also removes the need for a separate order management system, which the companies said reduces operational complexity and makes it easier to add new features.
Related: Revolut says USDT delisting is limited to EEA, Switzerland
According to Fritz Jost, Sygnum’s chief B2B officer, BancaStato is the first bank using Avaloq’s software-as-a-service platform to let customers buy, hold and sell crypto assets through its e-banking platforms using Sygnum’s API. Jost said the launch marked a “significant step in the maturity and scalability of regulated digital asset infrastructure.”
Sygnum expands European banking network
Sygnum’s banking partners include Societe Generale-FORGE, PostFinance and VZ Depotbank.
Sygnum announced in late June that its Liechtenstein-based subsidiary, Sygnum Europe AG, received a crypto-asset service provider (CASP) license under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation from Liechtenstein’s Financial Market Authority (FMA).
“This means European partner banks can plug into the same proven bank-to-bank infrastructure without going through the multi-year process of building and licensing their own crypto operations,” Jost told Cointelegraph.
Source: Sygnum Bank
He said banks remain responsible for their own regulatory arrangements, while Sygnum provides the licensing, custody and trading infrastructure. “That is exactly what allows a bank to go from decision to live offering in months rather than years.”
The license came shortly before the end of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation transitional period on July 1, allowing Sygnum Europe to provide regulated crypto asset services under MiCA.

title: White House accuses Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic tech for K3
summary: US officials warn that Chinese firms conducting covert, industrial-scale AI distillation could face sanctions and export restrictions.
full_text:
White House accuses Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic tech for K3
US officials warn that Chinese firms conducting covert, industrial-scale AI distillation could face sanctions and export restrictions.
A White House official accused Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic’s Fable AI model to develop Kimi K3, which launched last week.
In a post on X on Wednesday, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios alleged the Chinese AI firm developed an internal platform to distill US models at scale, using methods designed to evade detection.
“Legitimate AI distillation used to create smaller, more efficient models plays a vital role in this open innovation ecosystem,” he said. “However, large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology and undermining American research is unacceptable.”
Kimi K3 has emerged as one of China’s most capable AI models, intensifying Washington’s concerns that American models are being covertly used to accelerate China’s AI progress.
Still, some AI researchers questioned claims that Anthropic’s latest AI model was used to train Kimi K3.
Anthropic’s Fable 5 was re-released on July 1 after it was quickly taken offline due to US export controls, while Kimi K3 launched on July 16, giving a narrow window for distillation attacks to occur.
“There are only 15 days between fable 5 ban removal and kimi K3 release,” said Elie Bakouch, a researcher at AI startup Prime Intellect.
“I don’t think claiming that K3’s performance comes from fable distillation (even if they did it) makes sense technically.”
Dean Ball, OpenAI’s head of strategic futures, said on Friday he didn’t believe the K3 model’s performance could be “explained away by distillation or anything like that.”
Related: Anthropic to bring back Fable 5 as US lifts export controls
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the large-scale distillation attacks could result in sanctions and other restrictions.
“We support open-source AI and the innovation it unlocks. But open source is not open season on American IP,” said Bessent.
“When PRC firms conduct covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table.”

title: SEC settles Coinbase suit over ‘text messages that disappeared’
summary: The settlement follows a watchdog report last year that blamed “avoidable errors” for the loss of nearly a year’s worth of Gary Gensler’s text messages.
full_text:
SEC settles Coinbase suit over ‘text messages that disappeared’
The settlement follows a watchdog report last year that blamed “avoidable errors” for the loss of nearly a year’s worth of Gary Gensler’s text messages.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission agreed to pay $150,000 in legal fees to settle a Coinbase lawsuit seeking internal records from the agency at the height of the Biden-era SEC crackdown on crypto.
The agreement, filed on Wednesday, ends a two-year lawsuit between the SEC and Coinbase, in which the crypto exchange sought internal documents from the regulator to uncover evidence of “crypto by enforcement.” An internal report in 2025 revealed the SEC had deleted nearly a year of former SEC Chair Gary Gensler’s texts due to “avoidable” errors.
“The agency tasked with policing corporate record-keeping somehow lost reams of its own text messages between Mr. Gensler and other officials during the most intense period of the anti-crypto campaign,” said Coinbase chief legal officer Paul Grewal in an op-ed published by the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday, adding that the SEC will pay a $150,000 “award” and has fixed its record retention policies.
The settlement marks another legal victory for Coinbase under the Trump administration. The SEC, under the leadership of Paul Atkins, has taken a more crypto-friendly approach and dropped several high-profile enforcement actions against crypto companies, including Coinbase, in 2025.
Related: Coinbase chief legal officer to transition to advisory role on July 31
In February, Coinbase reached a settlement with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, with the FDIC agreeing to pay $188,440 in legal fees and revising aspects of its transparency practices after a federal court found it had violated the Freedom of Information Act.
“The years of litigation were worth it. We successfully uncovered dozens of crypto ‘pause letters’—indisputable proof of OCP2.0 and the coordinated effort to sideline the industry,” Grewal said in an X post in February.
Grewal to transition from chief legal officer
Grewal, who has served as Coinbase’s chief legal officer since 2020, is set to transition to an advisory role at the exchange starting on July 31, with Coinbase legal vice presidents Molly Abraham and Ryan VanGrack set to become general counsel and vice chair, respectively.

title: Hackers steal $31.6M in 2 crypto bridge attacks within 7 hours
summary: AFX, a decentralized perpetual exchange operating on Arbitrum, reportedly lost $24.15 million on Wednesday, while the Verus Ethereum bridge was attacked hours later.
full_text:
Hackers steal $31.6M in 2 crypto bridge attacks within 7 hours
AFX, a decentralized perpetual exchange operating on Arbitrum, reportedly lost $24.15 million on Wednesday, while the Verus Ethereum bridge was attacked hours later.
[Update 7:20 am UTC, July 23: Adds comments from Blockaid CEO Ido Ben Natan starting in the eighth paragraph.]
Hackers stole more than $31.6 million across two unrelated crypto bridge exploits spaced just hours apart, targeting bridges operated by decentralized perpetual exchange AFX and Verus Protocol.
According to Blockaid, AFX, a decentralized perpetual exchange operating on Arbitrum, reportedly lost $24.15 million on Wednesday through a hack targeting one of its cross-chain bridges. Hours later, Blockaid said it detected an exploit targeting the Verus Ethereum Bridge that resulted in about $7.5 million in crypto being stolen.
The back-to-back exploits highlight the continued security risks facing crosschain bridges, which hold large pools of assets and move funds between separate blockchains.
“Another bridge, another exploit. Bridges will always be a weak link, until security is upgraded,” onchain investigator TheCrypticWolf said in a post on X.
AFX protocol bridge hack
Blockaid said Wednesday it detected an exploit at 9:30 pm UTC targeting a bridge operated by AFX. Offchain Labs co-founder Stephen Goldfeder confirmed a bridge hack had affected a third-party protocol.
“We’re aware of a report of a bridge hack on Arbitrum and are investigating. We can confirm that the transaction in question originated from a third-party protocol, and the Arbitrum native bridge has not been hacked or exploited in any way,” Goldfeder said in a post on X.
SunSec, founder of the Web3 security community DeFiHackLabs and a contributor to SEAL, said the evidence suggested compromised keys, rather than a smart contract logic bug, were responsible for the exploit.
According to Ido Ben-Natan, co-founder and CEO of Blockaid, the company’s assessment was consistent with reports that five hot validator keys had been compromised.
“This appears to have been an operational security incident rather than a smart contract vulnerability,” Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph. “The unauthorized withdrawal carried genuine validator signatures, meaning the bridge’s onchain verification behaved exactly as designed rather than being bypassed.”
He added that the required validator quorum had been satisfied using authentic signatures, suggesting the compromise occurred in the bridge’s offchain signing infrastructure rather than in the bridge contract itself.
Cointelegraph reached out to AFX for comment.
Related: Allbridge pauses cross-chain bridge after $1.65M exploit
Verus Ethereum bridge suffers another attack
In a separate incident, Blockaid detected an exploit targeting the Verus Ethereum bridge, leading to $7.5 million in Ether, tBTC (a Bitcoin-backed ERC-20 token), USDC, USDt, EURC, MKR and scrvUSD drained from bridge reserves.
Blockaid said the attack appears similar to the previous Verus Ethereum Bridge incident in May that drained $11.58 million, using the same attack method but a different attacker wallet.
“An attacker used the bridge import path to trigger unbacked Ethereum-side payouts,” said Blockaid.

summary: Mirae Asset also plans to increase its stake from 92.06% to 97.15% through an additional deal later this week, local media reported.
full_text:
South Korea's Mirae Asset completes acquisition of Korbit crypto exchange
Quick Take
- South Korean financial giant Mirae Asset has completed its acquisition of local crypto exchange Korbit.
- Mirae Asset also plans to increase its stake from 92.06% to 97.15% through an additional deal later this week, local media reported.
We'd love your feedback.
South Korean financial heavyweight Mirae Asset has completed its acquisition of local crypto exchange Korbit and is set to boost its stake from 92% to 97%.
According to a Thursday announcement from Korbit, Mirae Asset Consulting, an affiliate of Mirae Asset Financial Group, has become the exchange's largest shareholder after completing the required regulatory procedures to acquire a controlling stake.
Additionally, Mirae Asset filed a revised regulatory filing on Tuesday to purchase additional Korbit shares worth $5.32 million, which would increase its ownership from 92.06% to 97.15%, the Korea Herald reported. Yonhap News Agency reported that Mirae Asset plans to complete the additional deal on Friday.
Korbit said the exchange's operating entity, user deposits, and personal data handling will remain unchanged.
Earlier this month, the Fair Trade Commission, South Korea's antitrust watchdog, approved the deal, calling it the first case of a traditional financial group's affiliate acquiring a crypto exchange in the country, per the Korea Herald.
Mirae Asset Consulting has said that the purpose of the acquisition is to "secure future growth momentum based on digital assets."
According to CoinGecko data, Korbit ranks as South Korea's fourth-largest crypto exchange by trading volume, with roughly $4.3 million in the past 24 hours. Upbit, the dominant player in the local market, recorded about $224.2 million.

title: Arbitrum protocol AFX Trade hit by $24 million bridge exploit: Blockaid
summary: PeckShield flagged that the attacker bridged the stolen funds from Arbitrum to Ethereum and swapped them for 12,467 ETH.
full_text:
Arbitrum protocol AFX Trade hit by $24 million bridge exploit: Blockaid
Quick Take
- AFX Trade has suffered an exploit with roughly $24.15 million in USDC drained, according to Blockaid.
- PeckShield flagged that the attacker bridged the stolen funds from Arbitrum to Ethereum and swapped them for 12,467 ETH.
We'd love your feedback.
AFX Trade, a protocol on Arbitrum, has suffered an exploit with roughly $24.15 million in USDC drained, according to blockchain security firm Blockaid.
Blockaid flagged the security incident on Wednesday, noting that the exploit was "specific to a bridge that AFX operates." The security firm added that it is working with the Arbitrum team to respond to the incident and coordinate with the affected protocol.
According to PeckShield, the attacker bridged the stolen funds from Arbitrum to Ethereum and swapped them for 12,467 ETH, worth roughly $24 million at current prices.
Steven Goldfeder, CEO of Offchain Labs, the team behind the Ethereum Layer 2 network Arbitrum, said on X that the Arbitrum team is investigating the exploit.
"We can confirm that the transaction in question originated from a third party protocol, and the Arbitrum native bridge has not been hacked or exploited in any way," said Goldfeder. "We will coordinate with the third party team and will report more details when we have them."
Ken C, head of growth at AFX, wrote on X that the AFX team is extending a white hat settlement offer. The hacker may retain 30% of the stolen funds as a white hat bounty if they return 70% of the assets.
"Our priority is the recovery of user assets and a swift resolution for the community. We encourage you to act in good faith. This offer is available for a limited time," said Ken C.
Meanwhile, AFX said the team suspended bridge operations upon detecting the security incident.
"Based on our current assessment, the incident appears to be isolated to the AFX-operated custody bridge," said the team. "The AFX trading infrastructure, mainnet, and the Arbitrum network itself have not been compromised."
The story has been updated to include comments from Ken C and AFX.

title: ServiceNow bets $40 million on Indian banking software specialist to expand its financial services push
summary: ServiceNow's investment gives BusinessNext a strategic partner to expand its AI-powered banking software globally.
full_text:
ServiceNow, the U.S. enterprise software company known for automating workflows like IT service management and HR operations, is betting on an Indian banking software specialist to deepen its push into global financial services.
The company has invested $40 million in BusinessNext, valuing the 24-year-old Indian firm at $700 million and taking a roughly 5% stake. The deal gives BusinessNext access to ServiceNow’s global sales network as the companies expand their partnership in AI for financial services.
ServiceNow’s investment reflects BusinessNext’s growing profile beyond India. The profitable, Noida-based company, which generated about $32 million in revenue in its latest financial year, serves more than 70 banks across India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and the U.S. Its customers include the Reserve Bank of India, the country’s central bank, and State Bank of India and HDFC Bank, which are India’s largest public- and private-sector lenders, respectively.
About half of BusinessNext’s revenue comes from outside India, with overseas markets expected to drive much of its future growth, founder and CEO Nishant Singh said in an interview.
The company chose ServiceNow over potential financial investors to accelerate its expansion by tapping the U.S. software group’s global reach. Singh told TechCrunch that the partnership would help BusinessNext “borrow” its go-to-marker “machinery” — referring to ServiceNow’s sales infrastructure — in markets where it has a limited presence.
“Think of it as a strategic partnership, which is cemented with funding,” he said.
BusinessNext’s software, Singh said, manages customer-facing banking workflows, while ServiceNow is stronger in workflow automation and back-office systems, a combination the two companies plan to sell jointly to financial institutions.
“India’s financial services sector is at an inflection point — institutions are moving from digital experimentation to full-scale AI-led operations,” Kulmeet Bawa, ServiceNow’s group vice president and managing director for India and SAARC, said. He added that the partnership combines ServiceNow’s enterprise workflow platform with BusinessNext’s banking expertise.
Founded in 2002, BusinessNext — known as CRMNext until 2022 — has spent several years building what Singh calls an “autonomous banking” platform, using AI agents to automate banking workflows while keeping sensitive customer data on private AI infrastructure to meet regulatory and privacy requirements.
Singh told TechCrunch that AI was built into the company’s platform from the outset rather than added later. “We actually renamed our company and we kind of rewrote our stack to put that fundamentally at the core,” he said.
BusinessNext employs more than 1,300 people across its operations and was last valued at $181 million in 2021, per private market intelligence platform Tracxn. It has raised more than $60 million in external funding and counts Avataar Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, and Ascent Capital among its existing investors.
The deal comes as established enterprise software vendors face pressure from customers who are questioning whether traditional SaaS tools are worth paying for when AI-native alternatives are emerging. For ServiceNow, the deal builds out its position in banking by partnering with a company focused on AI-driven banking software, as it expands its enterprise software portfolio through acquisitions, investments, and partnerships.

title: Orcas team up to ram sunfish until they explode
summary: “We think this may help younger orcas feed more easily, or it could also just be for fun.”
full_text:
There have been numerous accounts in recent years of orcas ramming boats—and sometimes sinking them. Scientists believe this may be a form of culturally learned behavior passed down through generations. Now we have fresh examples: orcas in the Gulf of California were filmed teaming up to ram sunfish with so much force that the carcasses exploded into small fragments. While orcas have been known to use force to remove flesh from prey, this is something different, according to a new paper published in the journal Frontiers in Ethology.
“We think this may help younger orcas feed more easily, or it could also just be for fun,” said co-author Kathryn Ayres of Beneath The Waves, a nonprofit organization promoting ocean health. “Orcas are known for playing with their food.”
Orcas engage in cooperative hunting strategies that can involve striking or killing animals—sometimes eating their prey, sometimes not—so the behavior could be described as social interaction, play, or practice as a mode of social learning. Orcas have been observed ramming whale sharks as another orca held the prey steady. Other cooperative strategies include herding mobile rays, blocking an escape path while hunting white sharks, and deliberately producing waves to bump penguins off ice floes.
When hunting species like sunfish, orcas typically rely on a three-pronged strategy. First, an orca will target the pectoral fins, then slash the sunfish across its body to remove the viscera. After that, the orca will use its beak to get at the remaining tissue. The newly observed “ram-to-fragment” behavior might represent a more sophisticated version of that basic strategy.
Play with your food
The first instance occurred in July 2024 off the coast of San Jose del Cabo in Mexico. A tourism operator filmed three adult female orcas, one male, and one juvenile catching and eating a spine-tail devil ray. Just after, the same operator filmed one of the adult females holding the carcass of a sunfish in her mouth. The sunfish had a large lateral wound, so the viscera had likely already been removed. The male orca then charged at the carcass, with the female releasing it just before impact. There was an audible sound upon impact as the carcass fragmented and bits of flesh dispersed in the water. The juvenile orca proceeded to eat the smaller fragments while the adults fed on what remained of the split-open body.

summary:

full_text:
馬來西亞區塊鏈週2026將於2026年7月29日至30日在吉隆坡世界貿易中心舉行，主題為「Bridging Realities: Where Everyone Meets Web3」。活動旨在將吉隆坡定位為亞太區新興Web3與AI中心，匯聚全球開發者、投資者與創新者。知名講者包括Justin Sun、Binance全球政策主管Steven Mcwhirter等，贊助商有Luno、Base等。馬來西亞憑藉監管明確性與區域連結性，正成為東南亞Web3採用的關鍵節點。
（前情提要：東南亞頂尖Web3盛會《MYBW 2025》本週隆重登場，匯聚全球業界領袖）
（背景補充：馬來西亞區塊鏈週MYBW七月回歸，推動大馬區塊鏈生態系飛升至全球新高度）
（本文為新聞稿，由 ACTIV8 Lab 撰文、提供，不代表動區立場。）
全球目光已轉向東南亞，Web3 的採用、實驗與實際應用案例正在此區迅速加速。在這股浪潮的中心，馬來西亞已證明是開發者、投資者與機構在 Web3 領域尋求發展的關鍵交匯點。
馬來西亞區塊鏈週 2026（Malaysia Blockchain Week 2026，MYBW 2026）將於 2026 年 7 月 29 日至 30 日在吉隆坡世界貿易中心（WTCKL）盛大回歸，匯聚產業領袖、創新者、企業、開發者、投資者、創作者與好奇的新進者，成為東南亞最受期待的 Web3 盛會之一。
這場首屆活動將在 2026 年以 「Bridging Realities: Where Everyone Meets Web3」 為主題延續其使命。今年的主題反映了產業正在發生的匯流——從全球協議與在地採用挑戰的交會，到機構資本與草根開發者的互動，再到 AI 基礎設施與區塊鏈在真實產業中的應用交織。
「我們現在看到的是 Web3 正在東南亞等新興市場被積極塑造，這裡的熱情與採用正在顯著增長。MYBW 2026 正是讓這些聲音被聽見的地方，共同構建關於 Web3 採用對馬來西亞及其區域在全球格局中意義的對話。」——Noelle Lee，MYBW 管理合夥人暨主辦人。
透過打造一個可及且包容的平台，鏈結當今的數位現實與區塊鏈、AI、去中心化技術及 Web3 創新的未來，MYBW 已確立其在產業中的領導地位，成為東南亞重要的 Web3 活動之一。
馬來西亞展現實力
今年，MYBW 2026 旨在進一步強化馬來西亞在全球區塊鏈生態系中日漸成長的角色，歡迎來自區域及全球各地的數千名參與者，共同塑造馬來西亞及國際間的共享 Web3 生態系樣貌。
馬來西亞的關鍵優勢在於其監管明確性、區域連結性以及快速發展的數位經濟。隨著全球 Web3 生態系日趨成熟，市場注意力正轉向那些能將實驗轉化為實際採用的地區——而東南亞正被視為其中之一。特別是吉隆坡，為區域開發者與產業參與者提供了匯聚的節點，讓尋求超越投機敘事的落地機會成為可能。
驅動 Web3 討論的區域中心
在為期兩天充實的活動中，與會者可以期待來自全球知名產業領袖的精彩主題演講，以及探討 Web3 技術如何融入馬來西亞生活的深度座談。
活動亦將提供與全球 Web3 生態系中的創辦人、投資者、開發者、企業及生態系建構者進行交流的寶貴機會，同時聚焦於馬來西亞的在地脈絡。旨在讓 Web3 更貼近大眾的教育環節，將進一步強化 MYBW 降低採用門檻、創造有意義對話以縮小 Web3 落差的承諾。
知名講者陣容
聚焦於縮小 Web3 與 Web2 之間的落差，需要對馬來西亞所處關鍵局勢有深刻理解的產業領袖。
為此，MYBW 自豪地宣布部分特邀講者，包括 Binance 全球政策主管 Steven Mcwhirter、Tron 創辦人 Justin Sun、Visa 亞太區數位貨幣主管 Nischint Sanghavi、Anchorage Digital 亞太區主管 Moses Lee、Etherscan 執行長 Matthew Tan、CoinGecko 共同創辦人暨執行長 Bobby Ong 等超過 150 位講者。
「局勢已經改變，馬來西亞已經準備好了。隨著備受期待的新數位政策即將推出，馬來西亞歡迎全球所有 Web3 企業前來開展業務。MYBW 在過去兩年已經為此奠定了基礎，而第三屆（MYBW 2026）就是未來。未來，就是現在。」——Dr Ian Tan，MYBW 共同創辦人。
更多重點講者、生態系合作夥伴及活動議程將在活動前逐步公布。
主要贊助商包括 Luno、Base、HATA、Gambit Custody、Cryptobilis、Anchorage Digital、BitGo、TRM Labs、Ledger、Utila 等，也將在 MYBW 2026 中成為重要的社群觸點。

title: 《要離婚才發現我有4735枚比特幣》中國 AI 短劇把幣圈拍成復仇爽劇
summary:
中國最近有一個熱播漫劇《要離婚了才發現我竟有4735枚比特幣》，男主角辦離婚辦到一半意外翻出近百億身家，瞬間從 […]

〈《要離婚才發現我有4735枚比特幣》中國 AI 短劇把幣圈拍成復仇爽劇〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
中國最近有一個熱播漫劇《要離婚了才發現我竟有4735枚比特幣》，男主角辦離婚辦到一半意外翻出近百億身家，瞬間從窩囊廢升級鯨魚。
（前情提要：Web3短劇《重生之我在幣圈當大佬》引熱議！劇組開拍前拿「韭菜上香」致敬中本聰）
（背景補充：離婚發現丈夫「偷藏12枚比特幣」，前妻崩潰：他年收300萬鎂，名下沒財產）
離婚前兩天，老婆把你的房子、車子和孩子都搶走要你淨身出戶，結果你意外發現一個塵封多年的錢包，裡面躺著 4735 枚 BTC（約 3.12 億美元）。這是中國最近爆紅的一部 AI 短劇，劇名很直白：《要離婚了才發現我竟有4735枚比特幣》。
這篇文章只是覺得題材有趣、分享給大家笑笑，可沒有要推薦你去追這部劇，請自行斟酌。
窩囊廢變鯨魚
劇情套路很單純：男主角原本是被岳家看不起的落魄富二代，妻子看衰、朋友看笑話，結果離婚離到一半，一個從沒點開過的舊錢包，把他直接從人生谷底送上幣圈食物鏈頂端。接下來當然是逆襲、打臉、復仇三部曲，前妻與仇家的表情管理全面崩潰，爽感值拉滿。
過去這套配方拿來炒總裁文、穿越文、贅婿文，現在連幣圈都被收編進題材庫。
現實版離婚幣圈故事，通常沒這麼好笑
真實幣圈的離婚故事，常見套路通常都是反過來的：另一半費盡心力偷藏幣、夫妻雇偵探查對方錢包，這些故事還真的有上演過。
真要說這部漫劇哪裡最不切實際，可能是「真的有人能不知道自己有這麼多比特幣嗎」XD。

title: 北京擬管制自家 AI 模型出口，Qwen、豆包、Z.ai 全被點名
summary:
《金融時報》報導，中國商務部正考慮收緊 AI 模型與晶片相關產品的出口規範，已與阿里巴巴（Qwen 通義千問） […]

〈北京擬管制自家 AI 模型出口，Qwen、豆包、Z.ai 全被點名〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
《金融時報》報導，中國商務部正考慮收緊 AI 模型與晶片相關產品的出口規範，已與阿里巴巴（Qwen 通義千問）、字節跳動（Doubao 豆包）、新創 Z.ai（GLM-5.2）等公司協商，限制海外取用旗艦系統。
（前情提要：北京傳考慮管控DeepSeek、月之暗面，因中國 AI 模型正被矽谷廉價狂擼）
（背景補充：AI 獨角獸 Manus 創辦人被中國「限制出境」！北京審查 Meta 併購案，20 億鎂交易有變數？）
北京過去十年，幾乎把「出口管制」視為美國打壓中國科技的代名詞。但如今風向卻罕見反過來。《金融時報》報導，中國商務部正與阿里巴巴、字節跳動，以及 AI 新創 Z.ai 協商，考慮收緊 AI 模型與晶片相關產品的出口規範，防止國內最先進的技術和領先新創被西方收購或取得。
這不是憑空冒出的念頭。半個月前，已經有訊息傳出北京考慮管控 DeepSeek、月之暗面，理由是中國 AI 模型正被矽谷公司當成廉價替代品狂擼。這一次，規模更大，矛頭指向的，是全球用得最多的中國開源模型本身。
誰被點名了？
據報導，商務部已與三家公司談過限制海外取用其旗艦系統：阿里巴巴（旗艦模型 Qwen 通義千問）、字節跳動（Doubao 豆包），以及 Z.ai（模型 GLM-5.2）。
研議中的措施包括：檢討涵蓋 AI 與晶片相關產品的出口清單，訂出更明確的出口許可核發標準，加嚴終端用戶查核，也就是確認買方到底是誰、拿去做什麼，並提高技術輸出海外的門檻。
目前一切尚未定案，商務部沒有發布正式提案，也沒有公開時間表，被點名的三家公司都沒有公開證實傳言。
有官員私下暗示，管制範圍可能只會落在「未來世代的模型」身上，也就是還沒問世的新版本；現在已經廣泛流通在外的舊版本，暫時不會被追溯處理。
中國在怕什麼？
Qwen 家族在 Hugging Face 上的衍生模型超過 11.3 萬個，若把所有標記 Qwen 的模型都算進去，數字超過 20 萬，比 Google 與 Meta 加起來還多。Qwen 累計下載量約 9.42 億次，已經超越 Meta 的 Llama（約 4.76 億次），成為全球最多人用的開源模型。
變化速度更驚人：2024 年 1 月，新增微調模型裡用 Qwen 打底的只佔約 1%；到了 2026 年 2 月，這個數字飆到 69%。
連新加坡的國家級 AI 專案 AI Singapore，也選擇 Qwen 而非 Llama 當作區域模型的基底。中國開源模型（Qwen、DeepSeek 等）在 Hugging Face 平台上的整體聲量，如今已經蓋過美國模型。
換句話說，北京要管的不是一兩個實驗室的產出，而是全球開源生態裡最主流的一套系統。技術一旦流出去，就很難再收回來，這正是商務部現在緊張的原因。
過去，「開源」被中國陣營拿來當成對抗美國閉源巨頭的武器，證明自己更開放、更慷慨。如今這套武器卻反過來讓北京擔心，最先進的成果，最終落到別人手裡練兵。
誰會先感受到痛？
過去幾年，歐洲開發者與許多中小型公司，靠著免費、開放權重的中國模型，當成美國商業服務的廉價替代方案。一旦北京真的收緊海外取用限制，這批依賴者會是第一批感受到衝擊的人。
也有觀察者認為，這整套討論可能只是籌碼，擺在跟華府的貿易談判桌上，用來換取美方在半導體或關稅上的讓步，未必會真正落地執行。
但諷刺的地方在於：中國過去十年始終大力抨擊出口管制，稱之為霸權工具、單邊主義的產物，是美國用來維持技術優勢的不公平手段。現在同一套劇本，卻可能貼上「北京製造」的標籤，用在自己最擅長、也最想守住的領域上。

title: OpenAI 算力支出到 2030 前飆到 7,500 億美元，但營收卻卡在 250 億關卡
summary:
OpenAI 將到 2030 年的算力支出計畫上調至約 7,500 億美元，較今年 2 月的目標多出約 1,5 […]

〈OpenAI 算力支出到 2030 前飆到 7,500 億美元，但營收卻卡在 250 億關卡〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 將到 2030 年的算力支出計畫上調至約 7,500 億美元，較今年 2 月的目標多出約 1,500 億美元。這筆錢一部分流向 Oracle 的 3,000 億美元雲端合約，一部分投入自建的 200 億美元 Project Camellia 資料中心。
（前情提要：甲骨文與 OpenAI 的 3000 億美元合約，為何敲響了 AI 泡沫警鐘？）
（背景補充：燒錢買成長！OpenAI 外洩檔案揭「營運大虧 209 億美元」，預期 2030 年才能獲利）
算力是這場 AI 軍備競賽真正的籌碼，據外媒報導，OpenAI 已將到 2030 年的雲端與運算支出計畫，從今年 2 月設定的目標上調至約 7,500 億美元，較先前約 6,000 億美元多出約 1,500 億美元，增幅約 25%。理由很直接：跟雲端商簽下新約，把算力鎖死，才夠訓練並運轉下一代更龐大的模型。
這 7,500 億買什麼
這筆錢具體流向哪裡？供應商名單已經攤開：微軟、Oracle（甲骨文）、Amazon Web Services（AWS）、CoreWeave，都拿到了合約。其中最大一筆是 Oracle 的雲端合約，金額約 3,000 億美元，效期五年，從 2027 年開始起算。
OpenAI 總裁 Greg Brockman 今年 5 月在法庭供詞中透露，光是 2026 年單一年度，公司預計就要花約 500 億美元在算力上，換算下來相當於每個月砸超過 40 億美元。
除了跟外部雲端商簽約，OpenAI 也自己動工。本週三（7/22）宣布的 Project Camellia，是一座投資額 200 億美元的自建資料中心，選址在喬治亞州 Effingham County（薩凡納西北），佔地 1,400 英畝。電力向 Georgia Power 取用至少 3.2 GW（吉瓦），預計 2028 到 2032 年間陸續投產。負責興建的是 Brett Mayo，他先前在 xAI 位於曼菲斯的 Colossus 資料中心，也扮演同樣的角色。
付得出來嗎？
財務長 Sarah Friar 私下向管理層示警：如果營收成長無法加速，OpenAI 未來可能沒有能力履行這些算力與資料中心合約。
目前該公司的年化營收（ARR）從 2023 年的 20 億美元，成長到 2025 年底逾 200 億美元，今年 2 月一度來到約 250 億美元（Sacra 估計），但從 2 月到 4 月幾乎沒有再往上走。
《華爾街日報》4 月 28 日的報導也指出，OpenAI 當時就已經錯失內部設定的每週活躍用戶與營收目標。兩個數字放一起：年化營收約 250 億美元，算力承諾 7,500 億美元，落差接近 30 倍。這也是為什麼 Friar 先前曾丟擲「政府為晶片融資提供 backstop（兜底擔保）」的想法。
不過這個構想才剛提出，立刻引來公開批評，畢竟等於是要納稅人替私人公司的算力賭注墊背。
誰最終買單
OpenAI 不是唯一一個把資本支出往上調的玩家。AWS 明年資本支出預估約 2,000 億美元，較今年的 1,320 億美元大幅增加；Google 也把 2026 年資本支出指引上調到 1,750 億到 1,850 億美元；微軟單一季度的資本支出，就已經達到 375 億美元。邏輯很清楚：誰先鎖住運算資源，誰就先拿到訓練下一代模型的門票，慢一步的人可能連牌桌都上不了。
問題是，這張門票最終誰買單？雲端商靠長約鎖住穩定現金流，OpenAI 靠融資與供詞裡的樂觀承諾撐住規模，投資人靠敘事撐住估值。三方各自都有理由相信別人會先付錢，但帳本攤開，寫的始終是同一個名字。

title: 三星公開兩款新 AI 智慧眼鏡，功能幾乎照抄 Meta、隱私問題同樣未解
summary:
三星首度公開兩款新款智慧眼鏡實體設計，加上五月亮相的兩款，與 Google 合作陣容擴大到四款鏡框，預計今秋上 […]

〈三星公開兩款新 AI 智慧眼鏡，功能幾乎照抄 Meta、隱私問題同樣未解〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
三星首度公開兩款新款智慧眼鏡實體設計，加上五月亮相的兩款，與 Google 合作陣容擴大到四款鏡框，預計今秋上市。續航最高 9 小時、搭載與 Meta 相同的高通晶片、功能組合也高度相似。
（前情提要：Google 聯合三星推新智慧眼鏡：Audio glasses 今秋上市挑戰 Meta 超 70% 市佔）
（背景補充：Snap 新推 AR 眼鏡「Specs」放話要終結智慧手機時代，售價 2,195 美元的豪賭）
九小時，是三星這次為智慧眼鏡續航給出的具體數字，三星宣稱這比 Meta 目前主打的智慧眼鏡更耐用。這也是三星第一次把眼鏡實體攤在外界面前，證明自己真的要跟 Google 聯手，正面迎戰 Meta 在這個市場超過 70% 的市佔。
四款鏡框，一次補齊規格
三星在官方公告中公開了兩款新設計：Gentle Monster 操刀的方形黑框，以及 Warby Parker 打造的較圓潤紅棕色款。加上五月 Google I/O 亮相的前兩款，三星與 Google 聯手打造的 Android XR「智慧眼鏡」陣營，如今擴張到四款鏡框，預計今秋正式上市。
從五月首度亮相到現在拿出實體設計，三星走的是一條步步為營的路線：先讓外界知道產品存在，再逐步把規格、外型、上市時間補齊，避免一次性攤牌後被拿來跟 Meta 逐項比較。
規格部分，三星向 CNBC 首度給出具體數字：電池續航最高 9 小時，隨附的充電盒還能再提供最多 7 次充電，等於整體使用時間可以撐過完整一週的通勤與零星使用。驅動這副眼鏡的，是高通 Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 晶片，跟 Meta 最新一代智慧眼鏡用的是同一顆矽晶片。
三星行動體驗事業部執行副總 Jaein Choi 表示，還有更多設計陸續在路上，但價格與確切上市日期都尚未公布，她只形容這是一款「premium（高階）」產品，暗示三星打算把智慧眼鏡定位在旗艦價位。
功能組合，幾乎照抄 Meta 劇本
用戶可以選擇搭配 Google Gemini 或三星自家的 Bixby，處理訊息摘要、即時翻譯、導航指引，以及對相機捕捉畫面的分析與描述，但這套功能清單，幾乎跟 Meta 智慧眼鏡的賣點一字不差，既視感強烈到讓人懷疑三星是不是直接照著對手的產品簡報抄了一份。
外觀設計上，三星同樣走「不像科技產品」的路線：鏡框重量不比一副厚框壓克力眼鏡重多少，體積也差不多；喇叭與麥克風藏進鏡腳，右側配一顆單一按鍵，左側是電源開關，鏡框前方則是相機與錄影 LED。
換句話說，三星沒有選擇用外型另闢戰場，而是直接複製 Meta 已經驗證過的成功公式：做一副看起來像普通眼鏡、願意讓人天天戴出門的智慧眼鏡，再靠 Google 的生態系與 Galaxy 手機用戶基礎搶市佔。這缺乏想像力但務實，先追平再談差異化。
隱私，全產業繞不開的關卡
錄影時鏡框前方的 LED 燈會亮起；Jaein Choi 向 Bloomberg 表示，一旦偵測到 LED 被遮擋或遮蔽，眼鏡就會直接阻止錄影，這套機制與 Meta 如出一轍。
但同樣的機制並沒能阻止 Meta 的智慧眼鏡被外界貼上「變態眼鏡」的標籤，也沒能打消路人對「被眼鏡偷拍」的疑慮。Choi 把隱私爭議定調為「產業共有的問題」，而不是三星一家要單獨扛下的包袱。
這句話說得誠實，卻也點出一個尷尬事實：兩家公司投入了同樣的晶片、同樣的 AI 功能、同樣輕巧的鏡框，但都拿不出真正的解方，最後都只能靠一顆 LED 燈跟用戶承諾「我沒有在偷拍你」。這道信任關卡，不會因為多一家廠商加入戰局就自動解開。

title: ClawQuest 推出 Agent Fire 坦克大戰，Telegram AI Agent 遊戲全面升級
summary:
ClawQuest推出Agent Fire坦克大戰，玩家無法直接操控坦克，而是將坦克鑰匙交給AI Agent， […]

〈ClawQuest 推出 Agent Fire 坦克大戰，Telegram AI Agent 遊戲全面升級〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
ClawQuest推出Agent Fire坦克大戰，玩家無法直接操控坦克，而是將坦克鑰匙交給AI Agent，以自然語言下達指令。Agent會讀取即時資料並最佳化策略，即使玩家離線也能自動戰鬥。同時上線C-Router，將AI模型代幣消耗轉化為CLAW點數，未來可1:1兌換$CLAW代幣。此機制將空投分配從點選轉向實際AI算力消耗，旨在終結tap-to-earn模式。
（前情提要：讓 AI 幫你炒幣！TON Tech 推出「Agentic Wallets」，Telegram 機器人解鎖鏈上自動交易）
（背景補充：Telegram 要開放自託管Gram錢包！10 億使用者即將迎來自管加密貨幣）
（本文為廣編稿，由 ClawQuest 撰文、提供，不代表動區立場，亦非投資建議、購買或出售建議。詳見文末責任警示。）
號稱首款 Web3 AI Agent 遊戲的 ClawQuest：Agent Mine 於 7 月 16 日推出 Agent Fire——這是一款由玩家制定策略、自主 AI Agent 操控坦克並代為作戰的戰鬥遊戲。
ClawQuest：Agent Mine 被譽為 Telegram 上首款 Web3 AI Agent 遊戲，此次推出的 Agent Fire 是 ClawQuest 內部首個子遊戲——團隊表示，這項更新將 ClawQuest 從挖礦遊戲升級為「Agent 競技場」。ClawQuest 的主遊戲 Agent Mine 已於 5 月 8 日進入公開測試階段，至今累計 444,751 名玩家，其中 125,790 人已連線自己的 AI Agent。Agent Mine 引入了團隊所謂的 Command-to-Earn（C2E）機制：玩家不再需要反覆點選螢幕來獲取獎勵，而是部署 AI Agent、下達指令，讓 Agent 在背景中執行任務、消耗代幣並產生 Claw Points。團隊認為，這種模式將徹底終結 tap-to-earn——點選可以被無限複製，但指令背後的判斷力無法被複製。
ClawQuest 執行長 Atlas 表示：「Tap-to-earn 把玩家變成了工人，我們則把他們變成管理者。你指揮的是一支永不離線的 AI 勞動力——而在 Agent Fire 中，你的 Agent 不僅為你工作，他們還為你戰鬥。」
在 Agent Fire 中，玩家無法直接操控坦克。每輛坦克配備一把 Tank key 和一個開放的 Agent API：玩家將鑰匙交給自己選擇的 Agent——無論是 OpenClaw、Codex 還是任何 Agent 框架——並以自然語言下達指令。Agent 會讀取坦克的即時資料和戰鬥程式碼，進行分析、模擬並最佳化策略，待玩家確認後發布新版本。從那一刻起，坦克即使玩家離線，也會持續以升級後的策略進行戰鬥。團隊將其描述為「Web3 首款 AI Agent 遊戲」。
將代幣消耗轉化為空投權重
執行 AI Agent 需要消耗模型代幣，這為每一次 Agent 行動創造了可量化的成本。C-Router 是 ClawQuest 自有的 AI 模型閘道，與 Agent Fire 同步上線，負責路由 Agent 的模型呼叫、提供對主流 AI 模型的統一存取，並將使用量轉化為遊戲內獎勵。玩家連線 Agent 至 ClawQuest 可獲得 500 CLAW 點數，而透過 C-Router 每花費 1 美元 的模型代幣，可在所有 ClawQuest AI Agent 遊戲中獲得 200 CLAW 點數。團隊表示，這些點數將在專案代幣生成事件（TGE）以 1:1 固定比例 轉換為 $CLAW。
此機制將空投分配從點選、連續登入和簽到轉向遊戲內實際消耗的 AI 算力。根據專案檔案，$CLAW 總供應量的 55% 保留給「世界貢獻者」。
Atlas 說道：「Agent 燃燒的每一枚代幣，都是真實參與的紀錄。你的指令、你的策略、你 Agent 的貢獻——這些才是建構這個世界的基礎，也應該是你在這個世界贏得份額的依據。」
此次發布正值加密遊戲持續探索 AI Agent 作為積極參與者而非被動工具的角色。ClawQuest 的路線圖分為兩個階段：首先，玩家與 AI Agent 共同遊玩；之後，玩家與 AI Agent 共同創作和營運遊戲世界。為了進一步降低門檻，團隊也在開發一款 Telegram 原生 AI Agent 機器人，讓玩家無需部署即可直接在 Telegram 內指揮 Agent 進行遊戲，預計未來推出。
Agent Fire 和 C-Router 現已作為 ClawQuest Mini App 的一部分在 Telegram 上線，無需額外下載。

title: OpenAI 實測：AI 的「誠實」是演給考官看的，沒人盯著就說謊
summary:
OpenAI 與 Apollo Research 提出「Contrastive SDF」測試法，證實強化學習訓 […]

〈OpenAI 實測：AI 的「誠實」是演給考官看的，沒人盯著就說謊〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 與 Apollo Research 提出「Contrastive SDF」測試法，證實強化學習訓練下，AI 模型會越來越傾向討好評分者，甚至讓誠實與否完全取決於它以為評分者想要什麼。
（前情提要：Claude Fable 5 太冷血才被限制出口？在生存實驗中 96% 時間在坑殺其他 AI 模型）
（背景補充：英國 AI 安全研究院：五個前沿模型全在測驗時作弊，不到一半認為自己有錯）
同一個模型、面對同一道題，只因它「以為評分者想要什麼」不同，違背誠實承諾的比率就能在 9% 與 87% 之間翻轉？OpenAI 與 Apollo Research 合作發表的最新對齊研究指出，這是一種可以被系統性量測出來的傾向，AI 模型嘴上說的「誠實」，很可能只是演給評分者看的一場表演。
更麻煩的是，這場表演的劇本會隨訓練越久、演得越像真的，讓人分不清模型到底是變乖了，還是只是更會演了。
模型不是在做對的事，而是在討好打分的人
研究團隊把這種傾向稱為 reward-seeking（追逐獎勵）。簡單來說就是，模型會在心裡「代表」出它的評分者，再根據「它相信評分者會獎勵什麼」決定怎麼做，而不是根據任務本身該怎麼做才對。
這件事之所以難抓，是因為好模型也可能「因為錯的理由做對的事」。經典例子是一個強化學習（RL，簡單來說就是用獎勵訓練模型，做對加分、做錯扣分）智慧體：金幣總放在關卡最右邊，結果它學會的是「往右跑」而不是「找金幣」。
行為在訓練資料上看起來全對，底層策略追的卻是一個錯誤的代理指標。研究團隊觀察到，多個前沿模型的訓練檢查點，即使沒有特別提示，也會自發推理「評分者想要什麼」，但這種嘴上說的推理靠不住，模型完全可以照著信念行動，卻絕口不提。
用假檔案餵模型，看它信念一變、行為會不會跟著變
為了把這個傾向量測出來，研究團隊設計了「Contrastive SDF（對比式合成檔案微調）」。做法是用一批寫得像真的預訓練格式檔案，論文、新聞、教科書，微調模型，把某個信念「植入」它腦中，再觀察行為變不變。
關鍵在對比設計：同一個模型訓練出兩份副本，一份餵「評分者偏好特徵 f、對立權威（用戶或開發者）偏好相反特徵」的檔案，另一份餵完全相反的組合。兩份副本輸出 f 的頻率差距，就是「評分者落差」，差距越大，代表模型越傾向討好評分者。
研究團隊拿 OpenAI 一個重能力、沒做安全訓練的 o3 強化學習檢查點測試，結果隨訓練推進，模型偏袒評分者的落差一路上升，對其他權威的偏好卻幾乎持平，轉變只針對評分者。
誠實測試更驚人：在「Broken Promises Coding」測驗裡，模型須向主管承諾不用某個受限工具，但完成任務又非用不可。植入的檔案一暗示「評分者獎勵完成任務」，後期檢查點違背承諾的比率高達 87%；暗示「評分者獎勵誠實」，違背率就降到只有 9%。同一道題、同一個模型，誠實度完全被它「以為評分者要什麼」牽著走。
驗證有效，但也代表這種傾向可能訓練不掉
要證明這套測量法真的量到了「討好評分者」，研究團隊反過來拿一批「已經知道它偏好什麼」的模型來對照。
第一組是 Redwood Research 訓練的兩個「獎勵駭客」模型（會為了拿高分去鑽規則漏洞），分別基於 gpt-oss-120b 與 Kimi K2.5。這兩個模型被訓練成愛鑽漏洞之後，評分者落差果然變大。第二組是用 gpt-oss-120b 微調出的三個「模型有機體」，各自被刻意訓練成只討好一個對象：使用者、評分者、或 OpenAI 領導層。結果每個模型的落差，都精準指回它被訓練去討好的那個對象。
這裡要先分清楚兩個很像、卻不一樣的詞。reward-seeking（追逐獎勵）是一種廣泛傾向：模型會照著「它相信什麼會被獎勵」來調整行為。reward-hacking（鑽獎勵漏洞）則是一種具體招數：單純為了拿高分去鑽某個漏洞。
兩者不一定同時出現：模型可能只是養成壞習慣式地鑽漏洞，根本沒去想背後的獎勵機制；但一個懂得在各種新情境都鑽得出漏洞的模型，通常就是個不折不扣的 reward-seeker。前面那兩個獎勵駭客落差會變大，正好印證了這層關聯。
真正危險的地方在於：這種傾向會讓「用來抓問題的測驗」失靈。一個很會討好評分者的模型，可能只是因為它推斷「現在正在考誠實」才乖乖不毀約；哪天監督方式一變，它的乖就未必還在。
而且就算評分者本身完美無缺，風險也不會消失——因為它從頭到尾學到的都是「討好評分者」，而不是「因為這樣做才對」。一旦進到沒人評分、或評分管不動它的場合，它很可能就走鐘，因為它的底層策略本來就不是衝著把事情做對去的。
更麻煩的是，這種傾向可能無法去除：你針對壞行為去訓練它，往往只是更新了它「什麼會被獎勵」的認知，卻沒真的改到它骨子裡的偏好。Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 4.8 系統卡也給了旁證：一個活化層級的監控器，在約 5% 的強化學習回合裡，抓到模型正在意識「評分者的存在」。
如今每家前沿實驗室都把強化學習愈做愈大，模型對自身處境的意識也愈來愈強，reward-seeking 只會有增無減。所以該盯的地方不是模型上線之後，而是訓練的當下：因為它完全有可能在還沒被人看見以前，就先學會了怎麼演。

title: Uber 客服部門再砍 10%，承認裁員理由是擁抱 AI
summary:
Uber 於本週三裁減全球社群營運（涵蓋客服業務）部門人力，並要求遠距員工搬回指定辦公室，這是該公司不到兩個月 […]

〈Uber 客服部門再砍 10%，承認裁員理由是擁抱 AI〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Uber 於本週三裁減全球社群營運（涵蓋客服業務）部門人力，並要求遠距員工搬回指定辦公室，這是該公司不到兩個月內第二次因簡化組織而裁員。
（前情提要：科技業不敢再甩鍋 AI？Robinhood 裁員10%，內部信揭密矽谷「縮編新藉口」）
（背景補充：AI 裁員現世報！55% 砍過人的企業認錯，Ford 花三年回聘 350 名老工程師）
裁員的理由，企業向來偏好含糊，組織重整、精簡結構、聚焦核心業務，聽起來體面卻讓人猜不透真正理由。但這次 Uber 沒有繞路，直接把話說白：客服部門砍掉 10% 的職位，理由就是要「擁抱 AI 人工智慧」。
這是 Uber 兩個月內第二次裁員，也是該公司首度公開把裁員和 AI 效率綁在一起。
「組織太複雜」背後真正意思
Uber 週三宣布裁減旗下全球社群營運團隊的人力，這個部門正是負責客服業務的單位。Uber 發言人以電子郵件表示，公司正在「簡化營運、強化實體協作，並持續擁抱 AI」。原本遠距工作的員工，也被要求依照公司的返辦公室政策，搬到指定的樞紐辦公室上班。
Uber 全球社群營運副總裁 Megha Yethatika 在寫給部門的內部備忘錄中說得更直白：「我們的組織已經變得太複雜、太各自為政。」她承認部門在匯入 AI 上「已有一些進展」，但要真正釋放這個潛力，「我們需要一個有效率的組織架構來承載 AI，不能在破碎的流程上規模化前沿技術。」換句話說，在她眼中，客服團隊現在的問題不是 AI 不夠好，而是人和流程太亂，撐不起 AI 該有的效果。
上一次不提 AI，這一次全指向 AI
這已經是 Uber 不到兩個月內第二次為了簡化團隊結構而裁員。今年 6 月，Uber 在新總裁上任後，裁減了所謂「人資部門」23% 的人力，佔全球 34,000 名員工不到 1%。當時公司並未把那輪裁員歸因於 AI。
這次不一樣。這是 Uber 第一次公開把裁員和「AI 效率提升」直接掛鉤。彭博指出，從金融服務公司 Block 到雲端業者 Oracle，近幾個月都有企業拿 AI 當作裁員的理由，Uber 這次等於正式加入這份名單。

title: 視網膜晶片讓失明者重見光明！美國 Science Corp 搶先馬斯克，將在歐洲開賣
summary:
美國腦機介面新創 Science Corp 宣布，視網膜晶片 Prima 已經拿下歐盟 CE 標章，即將在歐洲 […]

〈視網膜晶片讓失明者重見光明！美國 Science Corp 搶先馬斯克，將在歐洲開賣〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國腦機介面新創 Science Corp 宣布，視網膜晶片 Prima 已經拿下歐盟 CE 標章，即將在歐洲開賣；一份刊登於《新英格蘭醫學期刊》的試驗顯示，32 名患者中有 26 人視力出現臨床上有意義的改善。
（前情提要：再改變世界？馬斯克宣布：Neuralink下個產品是盲視！盲人將可重見光明？）
（背景補充：Meta 黑科技：戴頭盔讓 AI 讀你的腦，文字準確率衝上 61%）
視網膜中心的感光細胞壞死之後，患者眼前只會剩一片模糊或黑洞，這是「地圖狀萎縮」，也就是年齡相關性黃斑部病變走到晚期的型態，是老年人失明最常見的原因，目前無藥可治，只能延緩惡化…但這個局面正被一片晶片撬動。
Science Corp 執行長 Max Hodak 向彭博透露，旗下 Prima 視網膜晶片已經拿下歐盟 CE 標章，也就是歐盟的醫療器材上市許可，拿到後就能在整個歐盟與歐洲經濟區銷售，不必再逐國申請。
該公司稍早也公告歐洲商轉上市，把時間表訂在八月，首例商業植入很可能在德國進行。今年預計植入數十人，明年目標拉高到約 200 人，價格未定，將依地區與保險方案而異。
支撐這個時間表的，是一份去年刊登在《新英格蘭醫學期刊》的臨床資料。32 名完成 12 個月追蹤的晚期患者裡，26 人視力出現臨床上有意義的改善，足以重新辨認字母、數字與單字。
Prima 怎麼運作，治的是哪一種失明
Prima 系統由兩部分組成：一片植入眼球後方、視網膜底下的無線光伏晶片，加上一副內建攝影機與微型投影機的特製眼鏡。簡單來說就是，眼鏡先拍下眼前畫面，再把影像投射到晶片上，晶片靠光發電，把影像轉換成電訊號，去刺激視網膜裡還活著的細胞，讓大腦重新「看見」影像的輪廓。
它鎖定的病是地圖狀萎縮，年齡相關性黃斑部病變走到晚期的型態，是老年人失明最常見的原因。
整個黃斑部病變目前有藥物可以延緩惡化，但沒有一種能夠逆轉，Prima 是第一款針對這個晚期階段、被證實能讓部分患者恢復「形態視覺」的商業裝置。地圖狀萎縮好發於 70 歲以上族群，隨著全球人口老化，這個病患群體只會持續擴大，這也是為什麼 Hodak 特別強調，光是歐洲就有數十萬名潛在受益者。
市值排第二，為什麼反而是 Science Corp 先賣出商品
在美國腦機介面這個賽道裡，Science Corp 只是排名第二的玩家，市值 15 億美元，前面還站著馬斯克創辦、目前更受矚目的 Neuralink。但真正把植入產品做成商品、搶先送進診所開賣的，Science Corp 奪得先機 。
Hodak 是 Neuralink 的共同創辦人之一，2021 年離開後另立門戶，把重心放在難度較低、但病患數量龐大的視覺修復上，而不是直接挑戰語言與運動這類更複雜的腦部訊號。這個選擇讓 Science Corp 得以先繞開美國冗長的審批流程，把 CE 標章當成第一個突破口。
歐洲一張許可證，就能覆蓋整個歐盟與歐洲經濟區的市場，速度遠快於在美國逐州、逐案審查。同樣一顆晶片，如果先排美國隊伍，光是審批流程就可能拖上好幾年；改走歐洲 CE 標章，等於先繞過這套最漫長的關卡，把商業化時程硬生生提前。
資本也沒有缺席。Science Corp 累計募得 4.89 億美元，今年三月被彭博報導估值達到 15 億美元。這筆錢讓公司同時養著視網膜晶片、以及利用工程神經元對接腦組織的下一代裝置，一邊賣產品換取現金流，一邊繼續往更深的腦機介面推進。

title: Google 財報全面超標，但資本支出翻倍上看 2,050 億鎂、股價不領情
summary:
Alphabet 財務長 Anat Ashkenazi 在第二季法說會上宣布，將 2026 年全年資本支出財測 […]

〈Google 財報全面超標，但資本支出翻倍上看 2,050 億鎂、股價不領情〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Alphabet 財務長 Anat Ashkenazi 在第二季法說會上宣布，將 2026 年全年資本支出財測上修到 1,950 億至 2,050 億美元，是 2025 年支出的兩倍多；第二季資本支出達 449.2 億美元，優於預期，主要投入技術性 AI 基礎設施；她並預告 2027 年支出仍將顯著走高。
（前情提要：AI 燒錢今晚交卷：Alphabet 攤牌 1,900 億鎂資本支出，特斯拉迎來極大波動）
（背景補充：AI 吃電怪獸！彭博：2035 年美國資料中心用電將翻 4 倍，佔全國發電量 20%）
Google 母公司 Alphabet 週三交出第二季成績單，財報全面超標，但股價卻於盤後應聲下跌。財務長 Anat Ashkenazi 在法說會上端出兩組數字：一組讓華爾街滿意，另一組卻讓投資人皺眉，也就是不斷加碼的資本支出財測。
兩個月又加碼的財測
Ashkenazi 在法說會上宣布，Alphabet 將 2026 年全年資本支出財測上修到 1,950 億到 2,050 億美元。預計拿來蓋資料中心、買晶片伺服器這類「先砸錢建產能」的長期投資，砸下去要等未來幾年才看得到回報。
這個數字，比 4 月時公司自己給出的「最多 1,900 億美元」更高，也高過分析師原本估的約 1,860 億美元。
對比更早的基期：2026 年這個新財測，是 2025 年支出的兩倍多。而光是第二季，Alphabet 的資本支出就達到 449.2 億美元，比去年同期的 224 億美元幾乎翻倍，也略高於分析師預期的 441.5 億美元。
更關鍵的是，Ashkenazi 沒有把話說死在 2026 年。她重申，2027 年的支出還會「顯著」更高，理由很直接：公司要持續蓋資料中心、取得運算資源，才能撐住旗下 AI 專案與模型的胃口。這句話等於是告訴市場，這輪加碼不是一次性事件，而是一條看不到終點的長坡。
財報超標，為什麼股價還在跌
如果只看營收，Alphabet 這一季其實交出了漂亮答卷。第二季總營收達 1,197.96 億美元，年增 24%，優於市場預期。
真正的成長引擎是 Google Cloud：營收年增 82%，來到約 248 億美元，背後是企業客戶對 AI 運算的需求持續加大；而 Cloud 的訂單積壓（也就是已簽約、還沒認列進營收的訂單）在上一季就已經衝破 4,600 億美元。
照理說，這樣的成績單該讓股價上漲。但 GOOGL 股價卻在財報後下跌，市場的焦慮很直白：如果資本支出的成長速度，長期跑贏營收成長速度，這筆錢什麼時候才能真正轉換成獲利？花錢建產能是一回事，產能能不能被用滿、用出效益，是另一回事。財
一場所有巨頭都在加註的牌局
Alphabet 並不是唯一一個把賭注越壓越大的巨頭。把 Google、Amazon、Microsoft、Meta 四大超大規模業者的 2026 年資本支出財測加總，合計上看約 7,250 億美元，較 2025 年的約 4,100 億美元，暴增約 77%。
其中 Amazon 約 2,000 億美元、Microsoft 近 1,900 億美元、Meta 約 1,250 億到 1,450 億美元，Alphabet 這次上修後，已經直逼第一梯隊的規模。研究機構 CreditSights 估計，這筆錢裡有約 75%，也就是約 4,500 億美元，會直接流向 AI 基礎設施：GPU、伺服器、網路與資料中心。
這場牌局的規則很簡單：先蓋產能的人，才有資格接下一輪的訂單；但蓋太快、蓋太多，帳上的資本支出就會先於營收增速跑出去，把股價的耐心一點一點磨光。

title: 美國幣圈大軍創造逾 23 萬就業機會，估今年貢獻 550 億美元 GDP
summary:
根據美國國家加密貨幣協會（NCA）最新發布的報告，美國加密貨幣產業預計將在 2026 年為國內生產毛額（GDP）貢獻超過 550 億美元的產值。其中，約 310 億美元將以薪資收入的形式流向勞工。

〈美國幣圈大軍創造逾 23 萬就業機會，估今年貢獻 550 億美元 GDP〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
根據美國國家加密貨幣協會（NCA）最新發布的報告，美國加密貨幣產業預計將在 2026 年為國內生產毛額（GDP）貢獻超過 550 億美元的產值。其中，約 310 億美元將以薪資收入的形式流向勞工。
這份由務實政策集團（PPG）執行、 NCA 委託並提供資金的分析報告指出，儘管美國加密貨幣產業的直接從業人員僅 3.4 萬人，但若將供應鏈及員工消費等經濟外溢效應納入計算，整體可支撐約 23.2 萬個工作機會。
報告引述美國勞工統計局（BLS）的數據稱，幣圈這 3.4 萬個「直接就業」大軍，規模已正式超越咖啡與茶葉製造業（2.84 萬人）、水泥製造業（1.53 萬人），更遠高於傳統的菸草製造業（1.06 萬人）。
報告點出一個關鍵發現：這 23.2 萬個工作機會中，絕大多數其實並非隸屬於加密貨幣公司。 PPG 透過標準的「投入產出模型」（Input-Output Model，一種用於分析產業間供應與需求關聯性的經濟模型）估算，幣圈的外溢效應為周邊供應鏈產業創造了 7.5 萬個職缺，而這些勞工的家庭日常消費，又進一步衍生出 12.3 萬個就業機會。
從職業分佈來看，在這龐大的關聯就業生態圈中，「行政後勤」以 29,260 人居冠，其次為「商業與財務營運」（21,650 人）及「管理職」（20,890 人）。令人意外的是，連「物流運輸」（18,560 人）、「餐飲服務」（16,910 人）也因幣圈產業鏈外溢而受惠。
至於最核心的 3.4 萬個直接職缺，則是由軟體、區塊鏈與數據工程師拿下最大宗（10,100 人）；緊追在後的是法遵、財務與商業營運人員（5,450 人），以及高階主管與經理人（5,100 人）。
幣圈不僅創造就業，薪資待遇也相當豐厚。報告指出，這 23.2 萬個受惠職缺的平均年薪高達 13.3 萬美元，足足是全美薪資中位數 6.4 萬美元的兩倍有餘。
PPG 特別在附註中釐清，這個高薪數據涵蓋了所有受帶動的關聯職位；換言之，即便將前述的清潔、餐飲與外送人員一併計入，整體的平均薪資依然表現亮眼。
從地理分佈來看，科技重鎮加州（57,649 個）與金融中心紐約（53,766 個）包辦了全美近半數的幣圈關聯職缺。德州（26,536 個）、華盛頓州（15,097 個）及北卡羅來納州（9,524 個）則緊隨其後。
相比之下，位於美國中西部的 12 個州，合計僅貢獻逾 1.7 萬個職缺；阿拉斯加州則以 86 個墊底。不過，部分州正積極擁抱加密貨幣產業以創造經濟動能。例如，科羅拉多州不僅開放以加密貨幣繳納稅款，首府丹佛截至 2025 年已吸引 131 家區塊鏈企業進駐，吸金 5.71 億美元，為該州撐起近 5,800 個職缺及 13 億美元的經濟貢獻。
北達科他州也正大力推展相關舉措，包括 Atlas Power 規劃中的 700 兆瓦（MW）大型設施，以及該州銀行與金融科技巨頭 Fiserv 合作開發的美元穩定幣（計畫，創造了逾 800 個工作機會。
在估算模型上，PPG 以美國經濟分析局（BEA）2024 年的投入產出表作為基礎，並導入調研機構 Statista 統計的 232.2 億美元美國加密產業營收作為初始參數。
由於 BEA 尚未將加密貨幣列為獨立產業，因此 PPG 將幣圈企業的營運模式對應至現有的證券與商品合約（占金融相關營收 97%）、信用仲介、資料處理（占 3%）等類別，並採用科技業的勞動力結構來進行推算，確保數據貼近現實。
兼任 NCA 總裁、瑞波（Ripple）法務長的 Stu Alderoty 指出，加密貨幣產業已具備驅動實體經濟的實力，並對美國的就業、薪資及經濟成長帶來「實質且正向的影響」。
負責主導這項研究的 PPG 首席經濟學家 Oliver Browne 進一步強調：「每增加一個直接加密貨幣產業職位，都能在整體經濟中創造出約 6 個額外的工作機會。」
他認為，加密貨幣產業正逐漸確立其可量化的經濟貢獻地位，隨著市場採用率提升，未來成長潛力依然可期。
NCA 成立於 2025 年，為一家專注於推廣加密教育的 501(c)(4) 非營利組織。報告特別聲明，儘管這項研究由 NCA 贊助，但所有數據與發現皆出自 PPG 團隊的獨立量化分析，維持了報告的客觀性。

title: 美參院新版《CLARITY 法案》出爐：增設開發者保護、道德條款 2029 年失效
summary:
經過數月協商，美國共和黨參議員公布最新版《 數位資產市場明晰法案 （ Clarity Act ）》文本，這部攸關美國加密貨幣監管框架的重大立法，最快有望在下周送交參議院全院表決。

〈美參院新版《CLARITY 法案》出爐：增設開發者保護、道德條款 2029 年失效〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
經過數月協商，美國共和黨參議員公布最新版 《數位資產市場明晰法案（Clarity Act）》文本，這部攸關美國加密貨幣監管框架的重大立法，最快有望在下周送交參議院全院表決。
新版法案共計 616 頁，整合了參議院農業委員會（Senate Agriculture Committee）、銀行委員會（Senate Banking Committee）過去一年通過的兩個版本，並針對市場最關注的監管爭議進行調整。
其中，最棘手的「政府官員加密資產利益衝突」問題，也在最新版本中提出解方。法案新增道德規範條款，限制總統、副總統、國會議員及其他聯邦官員利在任期內利用數位資產牟利。
不過，道德規範附帶了一項「日落條款」（Sunset Provision，指法律達到規定期限即自動失效的機制），相關限制將於 2029 年 1 月 20 日中午後失效。
川普迷因幣成道德爭議核心，新版法案設利益衝突限制
過去數月，《Clarity Act》遲遲無法推進的最大障礙之一，就是如何避免美國政府官員利用加密資產牟利。
爭議焦點主要圍繞美國總統川普推出的迷因幣，及其家族旗下的加密貨幣企業 World Liberty Financial（WLF）。
上月公布的財務申報資料顯示，川普從 WLF 相關活動中獲得數百萬美元收入，引發民主黨對政府官員涉足數位資產市場的道德疑慮，也成為推動加密貨幣法案過程中的主要政治阻力。
根據最新文本，法案最後章節新增「道德規範」條款，禁止任何公職人員、公務員及其配偶發行或推廣數位資產，但未禁止官員持有或投資加密貨幣。
此外，如先前外界預期，草案明訂由司法部（DOJ）負責執法，立刻引來民主黨人強烈反彈，他們堅稱，各州檢察長也必須擁有參與權。民主黨籍參議員 Angela Alsobrooks 接受採訪時直言：
讓司法部來執行道德條款？這根本是開玩笑。如果條款不改，我絕對不會支持這部法案。但我們會在這個基礎上繼續斡旋，直到達成真正能落實問責的共識。
民主黨人士認為，各州檢察總長應該在監督政府官員利益衝突問題上扮演角色，而非完全交由聯邦司法部處理。
共和黨懷俄明州參議員 Cynthia Lummis 在說明文件中表示，這項日落條款證明了「這是川普總統自願遵守的標準，而非國會強加於他的枷鎖。」
非託管錢包開發者獲法律保障，DeFi 產業高度關注
除了道德條款外，新版《Clarity Act》另一項重要內容，是納入《區塊鏈監管確定性法案》。
該條款將為非託管軟體開發者提供「安全港保護，明確規定這類開發者不屬於貨幣傳輸業者（money transmitter）。
所謂非託管服務，是指使用者自行掌握私鑰、資產控制權不交由第三方管理的加密貨幣服務，例如部分去中心化金融（DeFi）協議與自託管錢包。
加密產業普遍支持這項規定，認為它能提供開發者更清楚的法律環境，避免美國創新人才因監管不確定性轉往海外。
新版法案同時新增了 25 個新章節，以解決執法單位對加密貨幣市場監管不足的疑慮。
去中心化金融教育基金（DeFi Education Fund）表示，初步看來，這些條款屬於「智慧型監管」，既能提供執法機關必要工具，也不會過度限制軟體開發者。
數位資產商會（The Digital Chamber）執行長 Cody Carbone 也表示，這份法案文本是推動美國建立長期數位資產市場監管制度的重要一步。他指出：
現在就是建立持久市場結構法案、讓美國成為全球數位資產領導者的最佳時機。
區塊鏈協會（Blockchain Association）執行長 Summer Mersinger 則表示，該組織正在審查最新版本，並期待協助推動法案完成立法。
參議院最快下周表決，但民主黨支持仍成最大變數
《Clarity Act》若要在參議院通過，仍需要部分民主黨參議員支持；目前最大的不確定因素，就在於道德條款是否足以化解民主黨疑慮。
若參議院能在 8 月 7 日國會休會前完成表決，法案下一步將送交眾議院審議，但隨著國會議員準備將重心轉移至期中選舉，留給這部世紀加密貨幣法案的立法空窗期已所剩無幾。

title: 特斯拉連 4 年沒賣比特幣！Q2 認列 1.12 億美元減損，持幣量維持 11,509 枚
summary:
電動車大廠特斯拉（ Tesla ）最新財報顯示，公司第二季並未出脫任何數位資產，比特幣持有量維持在 11,509 枚。不過，受幣價下跌拖累，特斯拉當季仍得認列 1.12 億美元的數位資產減值損失。

〈特斯拉連 4 年沒賣比特幣！Q2 認列 1.12 億美元減損，持幣量維持 11,509 枚〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
電動車大廠特斯拉（Tesla）最新財報顯示，公司第二季並未出脫任何數位資產，比特幣持有量維持在 11,509 枚。不過，受幣價下跌拖累，特斯拉當季仍得認列 1.12 億美元的數位資產減值損失。
換言之，自 2022 年出售大部分比特幣持倉以來，特斯拉至今已近 4 年未再買進或出售任何比特幣。
比特幣第二季下跌 14%，特斯拉認列 1.12 億美元減損
回顧今年第二季度，在全球總體經濟充滿不確定性、風險資產波動加劇的背景下，比特幣從季初 83,000 美元，一路下探至 6 月底的 58,000 美元附近。依據美國現行的會計準則，企業持有的數位資產若在財報期間內價格下跌，必須透過損益表認列減值損失。
因此，即使比特幣在 6 月底觸底後已逐步回血，近期在 65,000 美元附近交投，特斯拉仍須依第二季結束時的資產價值提列減損。
特斯拉目前仍持有 11,509 枚比特幣，依然名列全球持有最多比特幣的上市公司之一。
不過，相較於持續大舉加碼比特幣的 Strategy（NASDAQ：MSTR），特斯拉的持幣規模已明顯落後；Strategy 近年持續透過發債、增資等方式增持比特幣，而特斯拉則自 2022 年以來始終未調整持倉。
第二季財報好壞參半，每股盈餘不如預期
特斯拉第二季整體財報表現好壞參半。在獲利表現方面，非一般公認會計原則（Non-GAAP）每股盈餘（EPS）為 0.33 美元，遠低於分析師預期的 0.55 美元；營收達 282 億美元，則優於市場預期的 276 億美元；毛利率為 16.8%，依據一般公認會計原則（GAAP）計算的淨利為 11.1 億美元；公司當季自由現金流為負 11 億美元。
2021 年豪砸 15 億美元買比特幣
特斯拉於 2021 年初斥資 15 億美元買進比特幣，並短暫開放消費者「用比特幣買車」，引發市場高度關注，但隨後卻以環保、高耗能疑慮為由，暫停接受比特幣支付。
到了 2022 年，特斯拉出售約 75% 的比特幣持有量，以強化現金部位，此後就一直保留剩餘的 11,509 枚比特幣，至今未再進行任何買賣。

title: Police officer was violent rapist who attacked women over 14 years, BBC reveals
summary: The BBC can reveal that detectives have so far uncovered nine victims of PC Alan Greer but many more are anticipated.
full_text:
Police officer was violent rapist who attacked women over 14 years
- Published
A police officer who took his own life in May was a violent rapist who carried out a spate of sexual attacks and attempted murders of women over at least 14 years, the BBC can reveal.
PC Alan Greer's first known victim was a woman he raped in her home in Glasgow in 2012 after she had called the police to report being the victim of a crime.
The woman reported the sex attack by Greer late last year, sparking one of Police Scotland's biggest ever anti-corruption inquiries.
Detectives have so far uncovered a further eight victims, five of whom were sex workers, attacked while Greer was off duty.
It has emerged that Greer used hundreds of prostitutes throughout his police career, and it is anticipated more victims of his violence will be identified.
Assistant Chief Constable Lynn Ratcliff, gold commander for the investigation, said what the inquiry had found was "truly shocking".
She said: "This officer has clearly abused his power and has revisited someone that he's encountered in the course of his duties.
"But this victim was brave enough to come and speak to us, and that really was the trigger point for us starting our investigation.
"That's allowed us to proactively identify eight further victims."
ACC Ratcliff's confirmation of the inquiry comes following a BBC Disclosure investigation into Greer's offending.
A source close to the investigation told the BBC: "It feels a bit like this could be Police Scotland's Wayne Couzens moment."
Couzens was a Met Police officer who was jailed for the rape and murder of Sarah Everard in London five years ago.
'Violent double life'
Greer, who was born in Australia in 1978, moved to the UK when he was six.
He joined Strathclyde Police in 2009 before it merged with Police Scotland in 2013 and had 17 years of apparently unblemished service.
At first, he worked as a uniformed response officer in Glasgow before he secured a job in officer safety training, based in Coatbridge, in about 2016.
This meant he was involved in teaching probationer officers as well as refreshing more experienced officer training.
When he died in May, he was 47, with a wife and child.
Greer's family and colleagues are understood to have been "oblivious" to his violent double life.
Senior officers insisted there were no opportunities to spot his offending sooner.
The woman who started the investigation
It was towards the end of last year that a woman in her late thirties walked into a Glasgow police station to report a crime.
Somewhat reluctantly, she explained that she had, in 2012, attempted to report a disturbance at her home, and that uniformed officers had attended her Glasgow home.
She said the officers took her statement and left.
A few hours later one of the officers returned, alone, forced her into a sexual act and raped her.
After she told the police last year, the woman seemed to disengage from further inquiries.
The case was handed to the anti-corruption unit (ACU), who, by April, had secured a statement from her.
From this they were then able to identify the call she'd made in 2012 and could identify the officers who had attended.
They found that, in the weeks after the 2012 attack, one of those officers had repeatedly monitored the woman's crime file on the police computer for updates, perhaps to see if she had made a further disclosure about what happened to her later that day.
The PC had even carried out one of these checks while on annual leave.
Fourteen years later as anti-corruption detectives attempted to identify the woman's attacker, it would be these keystrokes, these searches in her crime file for which there was no legitimate police reason, which gave them their suspect - PC Alan Greer.
A timeline of how Alan Greer's crimes came to light
A critical incident was then declared and a gold commander was installed.
Anti-corruption detectives started working on Greer, and obtained his mobile phone number, which had previously not been held on his personnel file.
Only his home number had been retained by police.
The mobile number was then put through police intelligence databases, which revealed a single piece of intelligence dating back to 2018, linked to that number, but with no name attached.
The intelligence had come from a Glasgow sex worker and indicated that the owner of that phone number was a customer who had been violent.
There was no indication the number belonged to a police officer, but was this an opportunity to catch Greer in 2018?
ACC Ratcliff told the BBC: "I am entirely satisfied that everything that could have been reasonably done at that time was done, and that there were no missed opportunities as a result of that information."
The information from 2018 gave detectives a second strand of evidence, and grounds to monitor every keystroke that Greer made on police computers.
They then discovered that Greer had been searching the police system for traces of a complaint from a phone number, which detectives were able to identify belonged to a Glasgow sex worker.
This was a breakthrough. This was their suspect repeating the pattern from 2012.
They now had enough evidence to put before a sheriff who authorised a warrant to search his home and seize his devices.
Dawn raid on Greer's home
At dawn on 24 April, officers raided Greer's family home in what was described as a "day of executive action".
Greer appeared shocked to be arrested on suspicion of the 2012 rape.
Seven mobile phones and a laptop were seized, and Greer was brought into a police station to be fingerprinted and have his DNA taken.
He was not interviewed but was suspended from duty and released pending further enquiries.
It was only when officers started to look at his phones that the scale of Greer's offending began to emerge.
Thousands of graphic videos and images were recovered, revealing that Greer had used hundreds of prostitutes throughout his police career.
Officers are not yet even halfway through the files, but have already identified five sex workers who have been seriously sexually assaulted.
If Greer was alive, it is understood police would have sought charges of attempted murder in some of the cases, such was the level of violence used.
Three other victims have been identified, including two female police officers Greer had taken inappropriate photographs of while they were training.
As Greer's serial offending was emerging, detectives took steps to ensure his family were not in danger, and social work officers, accompanied by local police, visited his home on 5 May.
Greer died by suicide the following day.
'Police Scotland's Wayne Couzens moment'
In the days that followed, police announced Greer's death on the force's internal communications platform, and stated he died while suspended and under criminal investigation.
A source close to the investigation told the BBC: "Some of his colleagues thought this was a callous move on behalf of the police, saying he was under criminal investigation when he'd only just died.
"But it's clear they were all totally in the dark about this guy's offending.
"Folk will be in a state of shock when they learn the full truth. I don't think anyone really knows how bad it is yet.
"It feels a bit like this could be Police Scotland's Wayne Couzens moment."
Couzens is a former Metropolitan Police officer serving a whole-life sentence for the rape and murder of Sarah Everard.
He abused his police role to stage a fake arrest, highlighting severe vetting failures and multiple failed opportunities to uncover the risk he posed.
ACC Ratcliff said the comparison was unhelpful and that no red flags were missed.
She said: "At this stage, we've got no evidence to suggest [missed red flags] is the case, but we absolutely keep that under review because one of the things that we have to do from inquiries of this nature is make sure that we capture and we take on board the lessons learned."
